home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta said Perez received the nod as the Opening Night starter because he has more experience than anyone in the starting rotation. The southpaw, who's entering his 10th Major League season, was 8-11 in 26 starts for the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson will be making his fifth Opening Day assignment and looking to continue his career-long dominance against the Nationals franchise.  In eight starts against the club dating back to Montreal, he's gone 5-1 with a 1.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Myers makes his second straight Opening Day start after a whirlwind 2007 season that ended with him as the team's closer. Myers appears to have made a seamless transition back to the rotation, with a 1.13 ERA in three spring starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chico, who changed his mechanics late in Spring Training, delivered a solid rookie campaign in 2007, going 7-9 with a 4.63 ERA in 31 starts for Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels sputtered through another Grapefruit League season with lackluster results, but the confident lefty isn't concerned. He had a poor Spring Training in 2007, then won 15 games. His biggest goal this season is to stay healthy,  something he'll have to do if he's going to realize his goal of winning 20 games.
away_pitcher_note: Redding said he is feeling better after back problems, so expect him to pitch against the Phillies. Redding acknowledged he was able to relax a little more this offseason because he was able to show he still is a quality pitcher. Last season, Redding was one of the feel-good stories on the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran begins his 22nd season in the Major Leagues with 230 career wins. Fourteen of them came last season, including one on the final day of the season that clinched the National League East.
away_pitcher_note: One of the reasons behind Bergmann's success this spring is the return of his sinker. Last season, Bergmann abandoned the pitch after walking six batters and giving up four runs against the Diamondbacks on April 5.

home_pitcher_note: Considering the skepticism with which his transition was met, Looper's first year as a starter actually went pretty OK. He made 30 starts and pitched 175 innings, and for the most part he was reasonably effective. Looper's ground-ball rate dipped significantly, though, and that's something he'd like to see change. He doesn't have the kind of repertoire to succeed for long as a fly-ball pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Perez will face the Cardinals for the 12th time in his career. He is 3-4 with an 8.46 ERA against them. Perez is looking for his first winning season since the 2004 season, when he was with the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: If Wainwright can pitch a full season like he did in the second half in 2007, he'll be a Cy Young Award contender. He believes he can. After a slow start in '07, Wainwright posted a 2.71 ERA with 77 strikeouts, 30 walks and only four homers allowed in 99 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. He pitched two excellent games against the Nationals last season, but got minimal help from his offense and bullpen, and the Cardinals lost both games. Wainwright's first '07 start was washed out after three innings.
away_pitcher_note: His new high-leg delivery is starting to impress teams. The Braves, for example, noticed that the new maneuver helped Chico add more miles to his fastball. In the past, the Braves knew Chico as a guy who threw in the low-to-mid 80s. But they were surprised to see that Chico was throwing in the 90s during Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse did everything that was asked of him in his Cardinals debut, pitching five shutout innings against a good Rockies club. His limited work in spring contributed to his being removed without facing a batter in the sixth, but he should build up his innings and pitches quickly. Lohse had a rough time against Washington last year, allowing 15 earned runs in 16 2/3 innings over five outings (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals placed closer Chad Cordero on the disabled list on Friday night and recalled left-hander John Lannan, who will pitch against the Cardinals on Sunday at Busch Stadium. The Nationals needed a fifth starter because they didn't want right-hander Tim Redding to throw on short rest. Lannan was the Nationals' best pitcher during Spring Training, going 2-0 with a 2.18 ERA in five games. He was the Nationals' Minor League pitcher of the year in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Redding ended up having one of the best games of his career, pitching seven-plus innings and giving up just one hit, as the Nationals blanked the Phillies, 1-0, at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday. The only hit Redding allowed came in the second, when Pedro Feliz singled to center field. After that, Redding retired 15 of the next 17 batters. Redding managed to pitch so well despite that fact that it was cold. The game-time temperature was 49 degrees.  On Monday, Redding will face the Marlins for the sixth time in his career. He is 3-0 with a 2.00 against them.
away_pitcher_note: Miller's debut for the Marlins was a rough one, as the 22-year-old ran up a high pitch count and issued five runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Mets at Dolphin Stadium. Working deep into games is a concern for the Marlins, and Miller has the makings of being a top-of-the-rotation sensation. For now, he is still learning, and falling behind in counts was a problem against the Mets. It also gave him trouble for most of Spring Training. Miller used 90 pitches in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Bergmann was cruising through the first five innings, giving up one run against he Philies. Bergmann had a 6-1 lead, but he couldn't get out of the sixth. After getting the leadoff hitter out, Bergmann allowed four consecutive hits and RBI singles to Pat Burrell and Geoff Jenkins to make it a 6-3 game. The Nationals ended up losing the game, 8-7, in 10 innings. On Wednesday, Bergmann will face the Marlins for the 12 time in his career. He is 1-0 with a 5.28 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Despite some rough spots in his first outing, Olsen battled through six innings in a no-decision against the Pirates. The left-hander threw 97 pitches, and he was able to ease the workload of the bullpen, which was overworked in the opening series of the season. Olsen was 2-2 while taking on the Nationals in 2007, and for his career, he is 3-3 with a 4.36 ERA in eight games.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Perez found himself in trouble from the beginning. In the first, Brian Barton led off with a double and Rick Ankiel followed with a two-run homer. By the time he left the game, Perez gave up five runs in four-plus innings and threw 103 pitches. He had problems throwing his fastball for strikes. It didn't help that Perez was pitching with a blister on the middle finger of his left hand. He had the blister since Opening Night against the Braves. Perez is hoping the fingernail grows so he won't put any more pressure on the blister. Perez didn't use the blister as an excuse for his struggles on the mound. He gave the Cardinals credit for scoring runs.
away_pitcher_note: Effective in his last start, Hendrickson tossed 5 1/3 innings, giving up three runs (one earned) on five hits in a win over the Pirates. He struck out four and exited after 88 pitches. Hendrickson has worked at least five innings in both of his starts, and he has shown composure as he works toward battling deeper into games. In his career, Hendrickson has faced the Nationals five times, and he's 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Left-hander Matt Chico lasted six innings and gave up four of the five runs. Bad mechanics had nothing to do with giving up the runs. He made a couple of mental mistakes, according to pitching coach Randy St. Claire. For whatever reason, Chico had problems with the bottom of the Cardinals' batting order. In the second inning, Adam Wainwright and Cesar Izturis, batting eighth and ninth, respectively, had RBI singles, while Yadier Molina, a career .248 hitter, drove in two runs with a single in the next inning. Chico didn't have any problems with meat of the order -- Brian Barton, Rick Ankiel, Albert Pujols, Troy Glaus and Ryan Ludwick -- went a combined 2-for-14. The rest of the order -- Molina, Adam Kennedy, Wainwright and Izturis -- went 5-for-10.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was undefeated against the Nationals last year, going 4-0 with a 0.60 ERA over 30 innings. He faced them on Opening Night in D.C., allowing two runs on three hits over seven innings while striking out three, though he got no decision in a game the Braves ultimately lost. After surrendering two first-inning runs, he retired the final 19 Nationals he faced. He got a win against the Mets on Saturday, going six innings and allowing three runs while continuing to baffle hitters with his sinker.

home_pitcher_note: One thing can be said about Lannan: He finds a way to right the ship whenever he gets off to a slow start. Last Sunday afternoon was an example of how Lannan battled back. He walked Brian Barton to lead off the game and then gave up an RBI double to Rick Ankiel, but retired the next eight hitters he faced. After looking shaky again in the third -- getting two outs, then giving up a solo home run to Ankiel and walking the next two hitters -- Lannan righted himself again and went on to pitch 6 2/3 innings, while giving up only seven hits. He struck out four and walked three but took the loss in a 3-0 defeat.
away_pitcher_note: Smoltz looked both impressive while recording six strikeouts in five scoreless innings against the Mets on Sunday afternoon.  The 40-year-old hurler opted to cut his effort short after feeling some tightness in between his neck and right shoulder.  He experienced similar discomfort in late March, but isn't concerned about missing this next start. Along with a 96 mph fastball, he showed the Mets some curveballs and backdoor sliders.

home_pitcher_note: In a 10-7 loss to the Marlins last Monday, Redding thought some of the damage in the game could have been avoided if he was able to get Alfredo Amezaga out to end the third inning. With runners on second and third, two outs and the Nationals leading 3-2, Redding was supposed to pitch around Amezaga and get to pitcher Andrew Miller instead. But Amezaga drove a 2-2 pitch to right field, doubling in two runs. Miller reached on an infield single and scoring on Hanley Ramirez's three-run homer to make it a 7-3 game. Redding lasted four innings and gave up seven runs, only one earned because of two errors.
away_pitcher_note: Although he's allowed just one earned run in his first 11 1/3 innings this season, Glavine still has only two no-decision to show for his effort.  He surrendered just three singles in 6 1/3 scoreless innings at Coors Field on Monday night. The 42-year-old southpaw has shown his usual control and is still baffling hitters with his patented changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey wasn't efficient, needing 100 pitches to complete five innings during his season opener last Wednesday against the Phillies. But it was enough for a victory, and enough, he said, to help him with a certain confidence that he lacked last year. Pelfrey has faced the Nationals more than any other team, posting a 1-1 record and 5.64 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: It looked like Perez was going to help the Nationals get out of their funk last week against the Marlins. Perez was staked to a 1-0 lead and cruising during the first five innings, allowing just two hits. But the Marlins started to get to him in the sixth. With one out, Hanley Ramirez scored the tying run on single by Jeremy Hermida. Two batters later, Mike Jacobs singled to put runners on first and second. Manny Acta took Perez out of the game, and it was time for the bullpen to work its magic. On this day, the relievers didn't get the job done and handed Perez the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Maine hardly was challenged in the first five innings in his most recent start, a no-decision victory against the Philliies Thursday. But he walked three batters, allowed a single and needed 24 pitches to extricate himself from the sixth inning without allowing a run. Then he surrendered a home run and a double to right-handed hitters before being removed. He struck out merely one of 26 batters, an abnormally low number for him.
away_pitcher_note: Chico made one mistake and it proved costly as the Nationals lost to the Braves, 1-0, at Nationals Park last Friday night. Chico pitched a great game, going eight innings and giving up one run on five hits. But his biggest mistake came in the sixth inning. Braves shortstop Yunel Escobar took the first pitch and hit the ball over the right-center field wall for his second home run of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa made an emotional start in front of his hometown crowd last Friday night, taking a no-hitter into the fifth inning and ultimately winning his first decision since 2003. He was efficient with his pitches, throwing first-pitch strikes with a fastball that rested around 87 miles per hour. The effort was enough to earn him a start against the Nationals, whom he's never faced. The last time Figueroa spent time in the Major Leagues, they were the Expos, and he produced a 2.81 ERA in four career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan had nothing in the tank as he gave up six runs in four innings against the Braves last Saturday. Jeff Francouer did most of the damage, driving in five runs against the youngster. Lannan acknowledged that he didn't follow pitching coach Randy St. Claire's gameplan and he paid the price. After the game, Lannan spent almost an hour watching video with St. Claire.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous start, there was some good news and bad news for Miller. The positive is he worked five full innings for the first time in three starts. The downside? The 22-year-old left-hander was tagged for five runs on eight hits, walking four while striking out six. He did battle, though, after allowing four runs in the second, by tossing three straight scoreless innings. His slider was an effective pitch, but early on his fastball elevated and was hit hard. The five innings were his longest outing of the year. He faces Washington for the second time in 11 days. On April 7, he lasted 3 1/3 innings at Nationals Park, finishing with a no-decision despite allowing six runs.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Redding faced the Marlins was on April 7 and the Nationals lost the game, 10-7. Redding thought some of the damage could have been avoided if he was able to get Alfredo Amezaga out to end the third inning. With runners on second and third, two outs and the Nationals leading by one, Redding was supposed to pitch around Amezaga and go after pitcher Andrew Miller instead. But Amezaga took a 2-2 pitch and doubled to right field, driving in two runs. Miller ended up reaching on an infield single and scoring on Hanley Ramirez's three-run homer, to make it a 7-3 game. Redding lasted four innings and gave up seven runs, only one being scored as earned because of the two errors.

home_pitcher_note: Now with two big league appearances and one start under his belt, Badenhop will make his first home start. The 25-year-old right-hander will face the Nationals -- the team he debuted against on April 9, when he tossed a scoreless ninth. In his start in Houston, Badenhop worked into the sixth inning, but he didn't record an out. So in five-plus frames, he was credited with four runs on seven hits. Badenhop was victimized by the long ball, giving up two homers. Still, he showed signs that he could be a welcomed addition to the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Hill, who hasn't pitched in the Majors yet this season because of tightness in his right forearm, is hoping to make his first appearance. He pitched six innings for Triple-A Columbus on Sunday and gave up six runs (five earned) on nine hits against Charlotte. Hill was cruising the first three innings, but he then gave up a combined six runs in the fourth and fifth innings.

home_pitcher_note: With each start, Olsen is blossoming into what many envisioned out of him when he broke in as a rookie in 2006. Olsen comes off an efficient and impressive win over the Braves, tossing seven shutout innings. He didn't walk a batter, and exited with 84 pitches. On April 9 at Washington, Olsen threw 120 pitches in 7 2/3 innings in a victory. The last time Olsen started without issuing a walk, before facing the Braves, was on Aug. 22, 2007, against the Cardinals. He ended up losing that day.
away_pitcher_note: Perez had another strong outing last Tuesday, but it wasn't good enough as the Nationals lost to the Mets. Perez pitched six innings, giving up two runs on six hits. His only blemish occurred in the first inning, when David Wright hit a home run with Ryan Church on first. Perez has given the Nationals three good outings thus far, but he doesn't have any wins to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson provided some concern Wednesday night when his fastball was clocked between 83-85 mph -- at least seven mph slower than normal. He allowed four earned runs in three innings and was removed with what the Braves hoped was just a dead arm.  In his two previous starts against the Nationals this year, Hudson has worked 15 innings and allowed just two earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Chico admitted that he didn't feel right once he stepped on the mound against the Mets. He was rushing to throw his pitches, and couldn't find a happy medium when he was on the mound. Not feeling right proved to be costly for Chico, as he gave up three home runs in a 5-2 loss. The Nationals were ahead, 1-0, when he gave up a solo home run to Ryan Church in the bottom of the first inning. The biggest blows came in the fifth inning. The Nationals had a 2-1 lead when Jose Reyes tied the score with a solo shot. Three batters later, Carlos Beltran hit Chico's first pitch -- a changeup -- for a three-run home run.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz has won each of his three starts and allowed just one earned run in 16 innings, despite the fact that he's battled tightness between his neck and right shoulder. His 10-strikeout performance in five innings against the Marlins moved him within four of becoming the 16th Major League pitcher to record 3,000 career strikeouts. The 40-year-old veteran says his slider might be better than it's ever been.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan had the game of his life in his hometown on Thursday. A native of Long Beach, N.Y., Lannan pitched six innings and struck out a career-high 11 batters, while giving up a run on three hits against the Mets. It marked the seventh time in Nationals history that a pitcher had double-digit strikeouts in a game. Prior to the game, Lannan did not have a history of striking out a lot of batters. Lannan said he was able to fool hitters on Thursday because of a slider he developed during Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Redding earned the victory in his last game against the Marlins. He allowed just four baserunners over six innings -- three of them on hits -- but the Marlins' Josh Willingham touched him for a two-run home run. Overall, Redding is off to a nice start as one of the Nationals' most reliable pitchers.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was terrific in his last outing at Philadelphia, giving up four hits and three earned runs in seven-plus innings. He walked none and struck out 10, the 40th time in his career he has posted double-digit strikeouts. Santana threw 105 pitches, 70 for strikes and had excellent command of all of his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hill showed enough in his 2008 debut against the Marlins last Saturday to make the Nationals think he is picking up where he left off last season before he was injured. That means Hill, who fashioned a 3.42 ERA last year, could be pretty good. He had held the Marlins to a run before they hit him for three in the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Perez threw a solid 5 2/3 innings on Saturday in his last start, holding the Phils scoreless in a 4-2 victory. Perez gave up four hits, but he surrendered a season-high five walks. It was the third time in Perez?s four starts this season he left a game without giving up a run. His seven strikeouts were his second most in a game this season, one behind his eight-strikeout performance on April 2 against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Perez is still winless, but it's mostly not his fault. He's pitched well enough to win in four of his five starts. The latest example was against the Marlins on Sunday. The only run off him in six innings was unearned, on a Ryan Zimmerman throw from third that nearly landed in the first-base box seats.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster looks to remain unbeaten on the season when he pitches in new Nationals Park on Friday. Dempster has allowed just four earned runs over his last 18 innings. He's 6-0 lifetime against the Washington/Montreal franchise with a 3.40 ERA in 18 appearances, including 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Chico lasted four innings and gave up six runs on eight hits against the Braves. He walked three batters and struck out none. In his last two starts, Chico has given up 11 runs in nine innings. On Monday, Chico acknowledged he had nothing in the tank. He had a tough time throwing his pitches for strikes. It got so bad in the third inning that Chico walked Tim Hudson with the bases loaded.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano may want to only pitch at home. The right-hander is 3-0 with a 1.63 ERA in four starts at Wrigley Field this season. In his only road game April 11 in Philadelphia, he took the loss. Big Z is coming off a win over the New York Mets on Monday in which he gave up one run on five hits over seven innings while striking out four. Zambrano is showing signs that he's maturing. Instead of trying to overpower batters, he's focusing more on locating his pitches. Zambrano said he learned that lesson from Greg Maddux. That's a good teacher.

home_pitcher_note: When the Nationals are involved in historical moments, left-hander John Lannan knows when to rise to the occasion. On Aug. 6, 2007, Giants outfielder Barry Bonds was a home run away from the being the career home-run leader. But Lannan held Bonds hitless in three at-bats in San Francisco. Tuesday was another historical night. Braves right-hander John Smoltz, 40, became the 16th pitcher to reach career strikeout No. 3,000. But the Nats won the game, 6-0, thanks to a superb performance by Lannan. He tossed seven innings and giving up five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly finally picked up his first win of '08, in his last start against the Mets. The lefty gave up one run on four hits, four walks and struck out four over six innings. His velocity was better, he was able to mix in his breaking pitches, and he was more aggressive. All good signs for Lilly, who won 15 games last season. He is 3-2 with a 2.06 ERA in six games against the Nationals in his career.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start on Wednesday, Redding ended up pitching five-plus innings, giving up three runs on four hits against the Mets. Redding had problems with the bottom of the order. In the top of the fifth inning, Redding walked both Brian Schneider and pitcher Johan Santana. Two batters later, the Mets had runners on second and third when Luis Castillo reached base on an infield single that allowed Schneider to score. Redding had a feeling that Wednesday would be a long night, because he didn't feel right during his warm ups. Nats manager Manny Acta said Redding had poor command of his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine will be returning to the scene of where he suffered the injury that forced him to make his first career trip to the disabled list. The strained right hamstring that Glavine suffered before he'd registered an out against the Nationals on April 13 has healed and the 42-year-old southpaw is looking to resume the success he had during his first two starts of the season. During those outings, he worked 11 1/3 innings and allowed just one earned run.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hill pitched five innings while giving up six hits and three runs for the no-decision. He said the pain in his right forearm is almost gone and he's expected to make his next start against the Braves. Hill has an 0-2 record with a 4.91 ERA in two previous starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has continued to show maturity beyond his 22 years and proven that he has the stuff to be a successful Major League pitcher.  The young hurler was perfect in five of his six innings against the Mets on Friday and rebounded from four consecutive third-inning walks to retire each of the final 10 batters that he faced.  He has pitched into the sixth inning of each of his first five starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Perez pitched well against the Cubs, giving up two runs in six innings, but he ended up with his third no-decision of the season, as the bullpen was unable to protect a 3-2 lead. With the bases loaded in the eighth, left-hander Mike O'Connor walked pinch-hitter Matt Murton to force home Aramis Ramirez and tie the score at 3.
away_pitcher_note: Dealing with baserunners on an inning-to-inning basis is not going to change with Duke, whose game is making hitters put the ball in play. However, in each of his last two starts, the balls have been finding the holes, and those baserunners have been scoring. After giving up nine hits and six runs in his last start (six innings), opponents are now hitting .344 against the lefty, who is struggling to get his pitches down.

home_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Lannan showed once again that he is Washington's best pitcher. He threw seven shutout innings and helped the Nationals blank the Cubs, 2-0, at Nationals Park. One cannot say that Lannan, 23, was dominating in the game, but he showed that he could can get out of jams.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait replaces Matt Morris in the Bucs rotation. Dumatrait had been pitching in long relief, so he is stretched out in terms of innings. For Dumatrait, it is a second chance to start in the Majors. He was 0-4 as a starter last season in Cincinnati and posted a 15.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Just when the Nationals thought that Chico turned the corner after pitching eight solid innings against the Braves on April 11, it's time for them to ask: What's wrong with the promising young left-hander? Chico had his third consecutive sub-par outing in the Nationals' 7-0 loss to the Cubs on Saturday. He lasted four innings and gave up five runs on eight hits, falling to 0-5. In his last three games, Chico has allowed 16 runs in 13 innings. Pitching coach Randy St. Claire said that Chico is pressing on the mound. The reason St. Claire gave was surprising, because Chico is a guy who has a reputation of having ice water in his veins. Manager Manny Acta has often said he never knows how Chico is feeling because he doesn't show his emotions.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm tossed his third career complete game in a 5-1 win over the Phillies on April 27. He was outstanding, giving up one run on two hits, walking four and striking out two. In going the distance, he threw a total 99 pitches and was in the zone with 56 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Redding pitched well his last time out, tossing six innings and giving up two runs on four hits against the Braves. But he ended up with no decision. Braves first baseman Mark Teixeira scored the first run of the game in the second inning, when Mark Kotsay grounded out into a force play. But Washington came back and took the lead in the bottom of the third inning, when Zimmerman and Johnson hit back-to-back home runs. Atlanta tied the score, however, when Chipper Jones hit a solo home run off Redding in the top of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up a season-high five walks in his last start, Snell was visibly irritated with himself for not bearing down and pitching like he knows he is capable. Between rushing himself in between pitches and concentrating too hard on locating rather than just throwing to his strengths, Snell struggled with his command throughout much of April. Despite having made five appearances (three starts) against the Nationals before, Snell still has not registered a win or loss against the D.C. team. He has given up 10 earned runs in 23 innings, while striking out 22 and walking 11.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon had his least effective outing of 2008 in his last start on Wednesday, yielding five runs over five innings in an eventual loss to the Diamondbacks. Still, Chacon took a no-decision in that game, which brings his number of starts without a decision to a grand total of six. His most recent outing was the only one that didn't qualify as a quality start. Chacon faced the Nationals three times last year, allowing four earned runs over seven innings. Lifetime versus Washington, Chacon is 3-2 with one save and a 4.30 ERA over 11 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Hill is coming off his best game of the season, when he gave up one run on four hits in eight innings against the Braves. He retired 14 of the first 16 batters he faced, but he ran into trouble in the sixth inning, when Yunel Escobar singled to right field to drive in Blanco and give Atlanta a 1-0 lead. A tough critic on himself, Hill was satisfied with his outing, but he still needs to work on his breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt won his third consecutive decision in his last start, though he still says he has not had his good curveball on a consistent basis. Oswalt gave up four runs on six hits, including a pair of homers, in that outing May 2 against Milwaukee, but picked up the victory when the offense cranked out five home runs. Oswalt's personal winning streak is his longest since his six-game streak of July 20-Aug. 29, 2007. The right-hander is 3-1 with a 2.45 ERA in eight career games against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Perez ended up pitching another quality game last Thursday. He went seven innings and gave up the two runs on three hits against the Pirates. However, he got no decision for the fourth time this seaosn. Perez continues to say that he is not frustrated that he hasn't picked up a win this season.

home_pitcher_note: Backe picked up his second win of the season Saturday night with a good outing against Milwaukee. In 5 2/3 innings Backe gave up two runs on five hits. But he struggled with his control, walking five. He also hit his third career home run. Backe has faced the Dodgers just once, allowing three earned runs in six innings two years ago in a start at Minute Maid Park, and will be making his first start at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: One thing that Lannan proved last Friday night: He is human. After three straight solid outings, Lannan was hit hard as the Nationals were pounded by the Pirates, 11-4. Lannan was out of the game after three innings. He gave up six runs, five of them earned, and all of them occurred in the third inning. The biggest blow came when Jose Bautista hit a three-run homer. Even in the first two innings, during which he didn't give up a run, it appeared that Lannan was in for a long night. The first hitter Lannan faced -- Nate McLouth -- was hit by a pitch. After two innings, Lannan had already reached 44 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta has often said that Redding gives him peace of mind when he is on the mound. The skipper has a reason to relax. Two years removed from shoulder surgery, Redding arguably has been the most consistent starter on the team since the second half of the 2007 season. Last Sunday afternoon was no different as Redding had another quality outing and helped the Nationals defeat the Pirates, 5-2. He lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on six hits, striking out five batters and not allowing a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Ricky Nolasco threw five straight balls to start Saturday's game against the San Diego Padres. Nolasco regained his command, but not his best stuff, and allowed six runs in a 7-2 loss. He finished with two walks and two strikeouts, and threw 84 pitches, 55 for strikes. The first three runs all scored with two outs. After allowing three runs in the first two innings, he did battle back to pitch a scoreless third and fourth frame before allowing three more in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: O'Connor will be making his first start since going 3-8 with a 4.80 ERA in 20 starts with the Nats in the 2006 season. O'Connor has previously pitched against the Marlins twice -- both times in '06 -- going 0-1 with a 14.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe it wasn't the defining breakthrough game for Miller, but it certainly was significant. In his last start, the 6-foot-6 left-hander was on the winning end in a matchup against Padres legend Greg Maddux. Miller worked a season-high six innings, and scattered four hits and two runs. He walked two and struck out two. Finding consistency is Miller's biggest struggle right now. In beating Maddux, Miller threw 88 pitches, 55 for strikes. This will be his third meeting against the Nationals. He hasn't factored into a decision in his first two tries. Miller last faced Washington on April 18 at home, where he gave up three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hill followed his best outing of the season with an inconsistent performance Tuesday at Houston. Hill pitched 5 1/3 innings, giving up eight hits and three runs, keeping the Nationals in the game. He walked four, including the pitcher, which knocked him out of the game. Hill led 3-2 going into the bottom of the fifth and retired the first two hitters on grounders back to the mound. But he allowed three straight singles by the Astros, the last a bloop by Hunter Pence, to tie the game and take away the chance of collecting his first win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen is coming off the longest outing of his three-year career after going 8 2/3 scoreless innings while giving up two hits and striking out eight to get the win against the Brewers on Tuesday. The win was a much-needed bounce-back outing for Olsen, who had his worst start of the season when he gave up four runs in five innings in a loss to the Dodgers on April 30. Olsen is 2-0 against the Nationals this season, giving up five runs in 14 total innings while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa lasted five innings against the Dodgers last Tuesday, tied for his shortest start of the season. It was enough to keep the Mets in the game but not enough to win it, with the offense unable to turn opportunities into runs. He'll instead search for his third victory against the Nationals, a team he held to two runs over seven innings last month. Figueroa struck out seven in that start, allowing only three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Odalis Perez can't seem to get a win. He pitched five innings Wednesday at Houston, giving up five hits and three runs despite being sick. He did not figure in the decision. He left with the Nationals down by one, but they quickly tied it on a Ryan Zimmerman homer. Perez struck out three and walked two, giving up a home run to Lance Berkman, the hottest hitter in the Houston lineup, and hitting a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Maine pitched longer than any Mets starter in nearly a year, lasting into the ninth inning in a 12-1 victory over the Dodgers on Wednesday. Sporting a fastball that reached 97 mph and a sharp changeup, Maine allowed four hits and one run. If not for a bloop double and a walk conspiring to end his day in the ninth, he might have recorded the second shutout of his career. Maine has beaten the Nationals once already this season, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan earned his third win in his last four starts when he beat Houston Thursday night, throwing six innings and allowing seven hits and just one run. He struck out three and walked only one. It was good enough to keep Washington from getting swept in a three-games series in Houston. He relied mostly on his changeup and slider against the Astros, throwing curveballs only to the last batter he faced in the game.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets purchased Vargas' contract from Triple-A New Orleans on Tuesday to make this start. The 29-year-old right-hander, 43-38 with a 4.95 ERA in parts of five seasons with the Expos, Nationals, D-backs and Brewers, went 1-1 with a 4.91 in two starts, walking one and striking out 11 in 11 innings, for New Orleans.
away_pitcher_note: One can say this much about Redding: When he has a bad outing, he is not afraid to say that he wasn't at his best. Last Friday was one of those days as the Nationals were pounded by the Marlins, 7-3, at Nationals Park. Redding lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up six runs -- five earned -- on four hits. Manager Manny Acta said that Redding wasn't pounding the strike zone like he usually does. Redding walked five batters and three of them scored.

home_pitcher_note: Although he lost his third straight start Saturday, against the Reds, Pelfrey pitched more aggressively and impressively than he had since winning his first two starts. He all but abandoned his two-seam fastball, the one teammates call his "bowling ball" in favor of a rising fastball that produced more strikes, more swings and misses and more fly-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: After Tuesday's game, Nationals manager Manny Acta announced that Bergmann will make the start against the Mets on Thursday. It will be Bergmann's second stint with the club this season. He made the Opening Day roster, but was soon shipped to Columbus on April 12. After posting the best ERA in Spring Training, Bergmann had a tough time getting people out once the season began, giving up 16 runs over 12 1/3 innings. Bergmann's worst game came on April 9 against the Marlins. He was cruising the first four innings, but in the fifth inning, the Marlins scored seven runs. A few days later, it was more of the same as Bergmann gave up four runs against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Olson has taken Adam Loewen's rotation slot -- vacated by an injury -- by storm, pitching into at least the sixth inning in all three of his starts. The southpaw, who finished third in the International League in ERA last season, has temporarily managed to shake the command problems that plagued him in his first big league audition.
away_pitcher_note: Sunday's loss against the Marlins spoiled a great outing from Hill, who pitched seven innings and gave up two runs on five hits. He struck out three batters and walked none. Hill was pleased with the outing and felt he had a lot of good action on his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles elected to skip Steve Trachsel this time through the rotation, using a couple off-days to keep the rest of their staff on normal rest. That means that Burres will go Friday and Garrett Olson will start on Saturday, placing two lefties back-to-back. Baltimore may eventually maneuver away from that situation but is stuck for now.
away_pitcher_note: Perez had four straight no-decisions entering Monday's game against the Mets, and he pitched well enough to win at least three of those outings. But lack of run support and a shaky bullpen have played a large role in his deprivation of victories. Monday was a different story, however. Perez wasn't at his best on the mound, giving up three runs after four innings. And it looked like Perez was in for an early exit, but he settled down long enough to pick up the win.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles shuffled their rotation to keep Guthrie on turn, a maneuver made necessary by three days off during a seven-day span. Baltimore elected to skip Steve Trachsel, who will likely slot back into the staff in the middle of next week. Guthrie overcame two errors and a three-run first inning in his last start to work deep into the game and lead Baltimore to a victory.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan pitched six innings and gave up four runs on 12 hits against the Mets. He had serious problems with left-handed hitters and the bottom of the order. The eighth and ninth spots in the order went 4-for-5 and left-handed hitters went 5-for-9. Lannan's biggest problem was a former member of the Nationals, Ryan Church, who had four RBIs, including a solo home run.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Redding pitched six solid innings and gave up one run on two hits against the Mets. He struck out four batters and walked two others. New York took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the sixth off Redding, when Brian Schneider took a 2-0 pitch and hit the ball over the right-field wall for his second home run of the season. But Redding became the winning pitcher when the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Nothing is working for Myers, who has now allowed six earned runs in two straight starts. His velocity was largely there, but location and pitch selection have betrayed him. He seems like an open book, with hitters seemingly knowing what's coming, and teeing off. Myers suspected earlier this season that he was tipping pitches, but pitching coach Rich Dubee had ruled that out. Myers will be the first Phillie to pitch at Nationals Park. He's 7-7 with a 4.91 ERA in 27 career appearances against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: On Thursday afternoon, Bergmann found himself in a pitchers' duel with Mets right-hander Mike Pelfrey. When it was over, it was Bergman who came out on top as Washington defeated New York, 1-0, at Shea Stadium. Bergmann was dominating. He pitched seven shutout innings, gave up three hits, struck out nine and walked two. The weird thing was, Bergmann was in control without having a good fastball. It was his slider and curveball that helped keep the Mets off balance.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels can't be much more dominating than he was May 15 against the Braves, when he tossed a four-hit shutout, throwing 120 pitches. Three of the four hits were singles, and he walked two while striking out six. He's gone 4-3 with a 2.49 ERA in 10 career starts vs. the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: With the Nationals wanting Shawn Hill to rest his ailing right elbow, Chico will face the Phillies. Chico began the season as a starter, but he was demoted to the bullpen after four consecutive bad outings. The major reason for the bad starts was because Chico was pressing on the mound. However, it has been a different story out of the bullpen. He has given up just one run in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer was solid in his last start. He went 6 2/3 innings, surrendering seven hits and three earned runs in a 10-3 victory over Toronto on Friday. It helped to get great run support, as the Phils vaulted out to an 8-0 lead after three innings. It was one of Moyer's best starts, rebounding from two previous poor starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perez started last Friday, and a defensive miscue was his undoing against the Orioles. In the first inning, Melvin Mora hit a line drive to left over Wily Mo Pena's glove for a double on a catchable ball. Mora then scored on a single by Nick Markakis. In the third, things got worse for Perez. Brian Roberts led off and hit a fly ball near the left-field line. The ball was up in the air long enough to be caught, but it dropped in for a double. Roberts scored on a single by Mora. Markakis then hit a two-run homer. Perez, who lasted five innings and gave up six runs on 10 hits, blamed himself for the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will be facing a former team for the third straight start, having defeated the Cardinals and lost to the Red Sox in his last two outings. In Boston, he surrendered all four of his runs in the first two innings, all with two outs, but then settled in. After throwing 54 pitches in his first two innings of work, Suppan held the Red Sox scoreless over the next four frames on 43 pitches. Brewers manager Ned Yost elected to give Suppan an extra day of rest after he warmed up for Friday's game that was rained out, then warmed up again the following afternoon.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta usually doesn't compare his players to future Hall of Famers, but after watching Lannan pitch one of his best games in a 2-1 victory over the Orioles last Sunday, Acta called Lannan's performance Greg Maddux-esque. Lannan pitched 7 1/3 innings and gave up one run on four hits. In his first seven innings, Lannan had 10 ground-ball outs and allowed only two hits. He threw 94 pitches by that time, including 74 for strikes. The only time the Orioles had runners in scoring position during those seven innings was in the sixth, when Melvin Mora hit a two-out double.
away_pitcher_note: McClung replaces right-hander Carlos Villanueva, who was bumped to the bullpen after posting a 9.00 ERA in four May starts. Brewers manager Ned Yost figures to get about 75 pitches out of McClung, a hard-thrower who has made 37 Major League starts for the Rays, but had pitched exclusively in relief since joining the Brewers late last season.

home_pitcher_note: Redding wasn't sharp last Monday, giving up seven hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Phillies, but he managed to get his sixth win of the season. He believes that he is pitching the quality innings that he did for the Astros in 2003. The difference is that he is getting more run support.
away_pitcher_note: Parra was effective against the Pirates on Tuesday, but not efficient. He held Pittsburgh scoreless through 5 2/3 innings, with just four hits and one walk, but needed 116 pitches to do it. It was the second straight strong outing for Parra, who has surrendered one earned run in his last 11 2/3 innings over two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann has been great since coming back from the Minors. He threw seven shutout innings in a 1-0 victory over the Mets, and the right-hander did it again against the Phillies. Bergmann was in trouble just once, when the Phillies loaded the bases with two outs in the seventh, but Bergmann got Shane Victorino to line out to center.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets bounced back from what he called the worst inning of his career with one of his best starts. He surrendered six Dodgers runs and three home runs in the seventh inning on May 15, then returned six days later with the 15th complete game of his career, scattering 11 hits including a solo home run in a 4-1 win at Pittsburgh. Sheets threw a season-high 123 pitches and went the distance for the second time this season, improving to 4-0 with a 2.29 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf is coming off an impressive outing against the Reds on May 22 when he limited Cincinnati to two runs on four hits over seven innings. He became the first Padres starting pitcher to pitch seven or more innings since April 27. Wolf had good command of his breaking ball to right-handed batters and his slider to left-handers. He struck out nine and walked one and retired 20 of the final 23 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Hill is scheduled to make his next start against the Padres in San Diego. Hill played catch on Tuesday and was still feeling some pain in the elbow and right forearm, an injury he has had since Spring Training. Hill missed his last start because of the elbow injury.

home_pitcher_note: The 35-year-old Estes took a two-hit shutout into the seventh inning against the Reds in his last start before allowing two critical runs that helped set the Reds up for a 3-2 victory. It wasn't a 29 minute rain delay -- that's right, a rain delay in San Diego -- that hindered Estes in that seventh inning that saw him load the bases before leaving but much more exhaustion. "I felt a little fatigued in the seventh when I went out there," Estes said. "I figured I could get through it." Estes -- who missed the entire 2007 season after recovering from reconstructive elbow surgery -- is 1-0 with a 2.55 ERA in four appearances, including three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Perez started for the Nationals last Friday and picked up his sixth no decision of the season. The reason he didn't last longer than five innings was because he cut his left thumb while throwing a breaking ball in the fourth inning. Blood could be seen on his pants leg. Perez would pitch one more inning, but didn't want to take the chance of making the cut worse.

home_pitcher_note: Ledezma is coming off two poor starts. He lasted four innings against the Cardinals and just three against the Reds last Saturday. In that Reds game, he allowed five runs on five hits, walked two and hit a batter, with the big blow coming via a three-run homer off the bat of Joey Votto. Ledezma had trouble commanding his fastball, running into trouble with pitches up in the zone. In Saturday's game he threw 78 pitches in just three innings, 47 for strikes. Ledezma is filling the rotation spot of the injured Jake Peavy.
away_pitcher_note: Less than a week after pitching one of his best games of the season, Lannan had sort of a letdown last Saturday, as the Nationals were edged by the Brewers, 5-2, at Nationals Park. Unlike his previous game against the Orioles, in which he pitched 7 1/3 innings and gave up a run on four hits, Lannan couldn't establish his fastball and throw it at any count. He gave up three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Owings overcame a rough first few innings to get the win in his last start against the Braves at Turner Field. The right-hander allowed two runs in the second and one in the third, but then kept the Braves off the board before departing after a leadoff single in the seventh. He deserved a better fate in his start before that against the Marlins in Florida. He scattered seven hits and allowed three runs over seven innings in a 3-2 loss. One of the RBI hits was just out of the reach of a leaping Mark Reynolds at third and the other landed just fair down the right-field line. Owings struck out a career-best 10 in the game.
away_pitcher_note: With Redding on the mound last Sunday, the game between the Nationals and Brewers was a one-sided affair in favor of the Nationals. By the fifth inning, they had a 6-0 lead. With the way Redding has been pitching this year, it appeared he would be able to hold the lead. But Milwaukee ended up tying the score in the top of the sixth inning. Corey Hart and Mike Cameron highlighted the scoring with a two-run home run and a two-run double, respectively. Saul Rivera came in to replace Redding, and Gabe Kapler singled to right to send home Cameron and tie the score.

home_pitcher_note: Webb has now lost his last two starts after winning his first nine on the season. He didn't have his best command in his last outing against the Braves, as he allowed seven runs (four earned) on 10 hits over 4 1/3 innings. His winning streak came to an end May 21 at Dolphin Stadium, as he fell, 3-1, to the Marlins. Webb was trying to become just the third pitcher since World War I to win his first 10 starts of the year. Andy Hawkins won his first 10 starts in 1985, while Eddie Cicotte won his first 12 in 1919. Dating back to last July, Webb is 19-4 with one no-decision in 24 starts.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, Bergmann continued his stellar work since being recalled from Triple-A Columbus on May 14. The right-hander struck out eight members of the Brewers in 5 2/3 innings and extended his streak of scoreless innings to 19 2/3. He has 22 strikeouts over that stretch. Bergmann said that confidence in his fastball, curveball and slider have made him a better pitcher than even last year, when he almost no-hit the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has dropped three of his last four starts after starting the year 4-1. The right-hander allowed five runs on nine hits over six innings in his last start against the Giants. The big blow was a two-out, three-run homer by Bengie Molina. Haren said he feels like his stuff is getting better, but is struggling to put it all together on the mound right now. Haren has lasted at least six innings in 11 of his 12 starts this year. In his four losses the D-backs have scored a total of seven runs.
away_pitcher_note: Hill took the mound again after missing his last start because of discomfort in his right elbow and forearm, a problem that's plagued him since Spring Training. He became the third straight Nationals pitcher to pick up a no-decision when he got the hook after five innings Tuesday against San Diego. The right-hander only allowed two runs and struck out five, but he struggled with control, walking five Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was strong for the Nationals in the second game of their West Coast road trip. The veteran left-hander threw 99 pitches -- 60 of them for strikes -- scattering six hits and three runs over 6 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out four, and got good run support in form of a Jesus Flores grand slam and later a Lastings Milledge solo home run, as the Nationals took a 6-4 win at PETCO Park.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse pitched one of his best outings of the season in his last start against the Astros and has now won two starts in a row. In his last three starts, Lohse has thrown 18 innings while only giving up three earned runs. Lohse is 1-1 against the Nationals for his career in seven appearances with a 5.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan registered what's turning into a typical result for the Nationals last Thursday against San Diego. He threw 86 pitches over six innings, allowing just two runs and striking out five. However, the Nationals offense could only muster two runs of support, and the Nationals' bullpen lost the lead late, as San Diego won, 5-2, to take the rubber match of the three-game series.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals found a treasure when they plugged Wellemeyer into the starting rotation at the beginning of the year. In 10 of 12 starts this year, Wellemeyer has lasted at least six innings, and he's picked up six wins on the year. He turned in one of his best performances five days ago against Pittsburgh, when he threw a one-run, six-hit gem.

home_pitcher_note: Redding lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up three runs on four hits against the Diamondbacks last Friday. He cruised through the first three innings and didn't allow a hit. But he struggled through the next 2 1/3 innings because of mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Parisi gets one more chance to show his stuff. In his first Major League start, he was roughed up, but with Pineiro still out, he gets another shot. The right-hander, who throws a fastball, a curveball and a changeup, pitched very well in eight relief appearances before he was slotted into the rotation. He hopes to benefit from having a regular five-day routine, as opposed to last time, when he pitched four days after a relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Last Saturday, Bergmann pitched eight innings for his first career complete game and gave up four runs on seven hits, but the long ball did him in against the Diamondbacks. In the bottom of the second inning, Mark Reynolds hit a fastball for a home run, which snapped Bergmann's scoreless streak at 21 innings. In the seventh, Justin Upton and Reynolds hit back-to-back home runs, both coming on sliders. In the bottom of the eighth, Chris Young hit a 3-1 slider to the center-field mezzanine for his 12th home run of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum received a no-decision in his last outing, working two batters into the eighth inning against San Diego. He left with a 1-0 lead but departed after a single and a walk as the Padres proceeded to score the tying run. Lincecum faced Washington once last year, emerging with a no-decision despite surrendering just one run in seven innings in a 3-2 Giants victory on Aug. 6. Lincecum happened to throw 116 pitches that night, his most in any game during his rookie season.

home_pitcher_note: Hill struggled in last Sunday's loss to Arizona, giving up five runs on seven hits in four innings on the final day of the Nationals' road trip as Washington fell, 5-0. The Nationals need for the injury-plagued Hill to show the form he's displayed in the past as their lineup has been nearly decimated by injures. The runs have been few and far between, and Hill has shown he can be a solid pitcher in the past. But he's still looking for his first victory of the season, and will need everything with his arm and forearm to let hit throw like he's done before.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez got into a bases-loaded jam in the first inning of his last start, but was in control from there, throwing seven innings of two-run ball. The Giants gave him a six-run cushion with which to work in the bottom of the first inning, and the Mets never recovered. Against a lineup that previously had been on a roll, Sanchez had eight strikeouts in his best performance since late April, when he went eight innings with 10 strikeouts against the Reds. Sanchez has allowed two or less runs in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: It was revealed Friday through baseball sources that Garrett Mock will be called up from Triple-A Columbus on Sunday to pitch in place of the injured Odalis Perez. Mock is 3-2 with a 3.06 ERA in 11 appearances this season, finally free of a left knee injury that had hampered his progress since sustained in late 2006. Mock has never pitched in a Major League game.
away_pitcher_note: After showing encouraging signs in his first four starts following his brief demotion to the bullpen, Zito struggled Tuesday against the Mets by allowing six runs (five earned) and seven hits in 4 1/3 innings. Zito lamented his poor command in explaining his trouble. He issued five walks, including two in New York's eight-run fifth inning. Zito has thrived against three Nationals who have amassed more than 10 at-bats against him: Aaron Boone (.083, 1-for-12), Cristian Guzman (.050, 1-for-20) and Dmitri Young (.200, 5-for-25). But Ronnie Belliard (.367, 11-for-30) has enjoyed success against him.

home_pitcher_note: Clippard pitched just two innings in his last Triple-A start on June 4, and it was widely speculated he would replace injured Nationals starter Odalis Perez. However, after last Wednesday's rainout forced rookie starter John Lannan to pitch Thursday, the Nationals chose to have Garrett Mock pitch Sunday for Perez and will bring Clippard up to pitch Monday so Lannan does not have to go on short rest. So far this season, Clippard has been an anchor of the Columbus staff, with a current record of 4-4 and a 3.41 ERA. He's struck out 59 batters in 60 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cain's ERA rose from 4.38, as he allowed five runs in five innings to the Mets on Wednesday. He has won once in his last seven starts, enduring another frustrating stretch. Moreover, the Giants are only 4-9 when he pitches. Cain's last start ended a streak of six in a row in which he worked at least six innings. He's 18-15 lifetime when he pitches that long. Cain has faced the Nationals four times, posting a 1-2 record with a 3.38 ERA. Cain has struggled on the road, where he's 0-2 with a 4.79 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: After letting up three runs on five hits in the first two innings of his last start, Maholm settled down and threw a near-flawless game. He retired 20 of the next 23 batters and didn't issue a walk for the second start in a row. He is 0-2 with a 6.38 ERA against Washington in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Redding lasted just 5 1/3 innings Thursday night in Game 2 of the Nationals' day-night doubleheader against St. Louis. He surrendered six runs over the start -- all with two outs -- but picked up a no-decision as the Nationals won a thrilling come-from-behind game 10-9 on a walk-off Elijah Dukes home run.

home_pitcher_note: Well, the good news was that Snell limited the D-backs to just one earned run in five innings, striking out nine in that span. However, with a pitch count of 58 by the end of the second and of 107 through five, Snell obviously needs to better his efficiency. He wasn't helped either by being struck in the lower back by a line drive, something that Snell said bothered him in his final two innings but shouldn't cause him to miss any time. Snell has not won since April 12 and has pitched more than five innings only once in his last five games. He is 0-1 with a 4.34 ERA in six career appearances (four starts) against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan turned in another strong performance Thursday in game one of a doubleheader against St. Louis. Despite struggling with his control, the left-hander only allowed two runs over six innings, dropping his ERA to 3.47. However, he picked up the loss as the Cardinals shut down the Nationals' offense in a 4-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: The beginning of Gorzelanny's last start looked like many that preceded it: unpleasant. The lefty gave up three quick runs in the first, but settled down and allowed no runs through his final six innings, earning a no-decision in the process. Gorzelanny, who hasn't won since May 22, beat the Nationals in his only career start against them, going 7 1/3 innings with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann struggled mightily in his last outing, giving up eight runs -- five earned -- and 10 hits over just three innings. It was the rockiest start by far for Bergmann, who had been stellar since returning from Triple-A Columbus in May. Bergmann threw 83 pitches over the start, 51 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey, a knuckleballer, moves into the spot previously held by Miguel Batista, who has been largely ineffective after leading the team with 16 wins last season. Dickey has done a good job in the few relief appearances he has made, allowing one run on six hits while striking out 10 in his past 10 1/3 innings. He has started once this year and allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings against the Angels on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Hill had some of his best stuff last Saturday against the Giants. He threw 7 1/3 innings, giving up just two runs on seven hits while striking out two. But he ended up saddled with the loss, as three San Francisco pitchers combined to shut out Washington in a 6-0 loss. Regardless, Hill had his second-longest outing of the season, and dropped his ERA to 4.35.

home_pitcher_note: Cooler temperature and lower humidity will be a welcome sight for the Canadian-raised left-hander, who wilted in the Boston heat in his last outing. He limited the Red Sox to one run over five innings, departing because the 98-degree heat and 102-degree heat index wore him out more than the Red Sox hitters. Bedard has faced the Nationals once in his career, limiting them to one run over seven innings in an Interleague Play game, receiving a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: A mainstay of the Triple-A rotation, Clippard will again be asked to toe the rubber for the big league club after lefty Odalis Perez was forced to miss another start due to shoulder tendinitis. In his last start, Clippard was effective through four innings but struggled in the fifth before being replaced. In total, the right-hander threw 4 1/3 innings, giving up five hits and three runs. He walked four and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn put together his third consecutive solid outing with an impressive performance during his last start against the Blue Jays. The Seattle left-hander allowed just one run on five hits while striking out four over six innings. His only trouble came during the bottom of the fourth inning when he surrendered a two-out RBI double off the bat of Jays first baseman Lyle Overbay. Washburn was forced to take the no-decision due to a lack of run support, but he now possesses a 3.63 ERA over his past three outings. The 33-year-old has only faced the Nationals once during his career. In that start, he allowed just one run over six innings en route to victory.
away_pitcher_note: Redding's last outing didn't start out as planned. He gave up three runs in a matter of minutes. But he settled down and limited the Pirates to only one run the remainder of his six innings. He earned a no-decision when the Nationals hit three home runs in one inning to tie the game. Redding was a member of the Padres when he faced Seattle for the only time in his career. He pitched 3 1/3 innings of relief, giving up six runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: After a very solid start to the year, Hernandez has started to look like a much different pitcher recently. He struggled mightily in his first career start against the Indians, giving up seven runs on 12 hits over just three-plus innings. It was the fifth straight start that he had been tagged for at least five earned runs. He's now allowed 136 hits on the season, putting him in line become the first Major League pitcher to give up more than 300 hits in a single season since Phil Niekro, who allowed 311 for Atlanta in 1979. Hernandez will next face a former team of his, the Nationals, in Interleague Play. He is 6-5 with a 4.19 ERA in 12 career appearances vs. Washington.
away_pitcher_note: The first time Lannan faced the Pirates in May, he made it only three innings into the game. The second time in June, he went out and threw six quality innings, giving up only two runs on seven hits. He said he wanted to establish his territory with his fastball. He did just that by throwing 61 of his 93 pitches for strikes. Lannan has yet to face Minnesota during his two-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey rebounded from two so-so starts to deliver a stellar performance in the Twins' series opener against the Brewers. The right-hander allowed just two runs on five hits over eight innings in the start, but he provided almost as much support with his bat by tallying two RBIs on the night. For only the third time this season, Slowey kept the ball in the park and did not give up a single home run. He'll try to repeat that trend when he faces the Nationals in the series finale, marking his first career appearance against the club.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman's struggles continued again the Pirates in his last start on June 12. The Bucs connected for eight hits and six runs to knock the right hander out of the game after 4 2/3 innings. Bergman has now given up 18 hits and 11 runs in his last two starts. He has not faced Seattle in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins delivered his fifth quality start of the season in his last outing against the Brewers in Milwaukee. He pitched six innings, giving up three runs on eight hits. Perkins walked just one in his start and struck out six, tying his career-high. One thing the left-hander could work on is limiting his pitch count. He threw a total of 93 pitches over his six innings. Next up for Perkins will be his first start against the Diamondbacks at the Metrodome. The Minnesota native has struggled at home this season, going 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA in five starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Hill picked up his first win since Sept. 10, 2007, after getting plenty of run support early against the Mariners. Hill allowed 12 hits but just four earned runs -- five total -- over five innings and got plenty of backup from the bullpen as the Nationals took a game in Seattle, winning, 7-6. Hill also struck out three.

home_pitcher_note: Redding was the pitching star for Washington last Sunday, lasting six innings and giving up two runs (one earned) on five hits against the Mariners. Redding will face the Rangers for the fifth time in his career. He has given up 17 earned runs in 8 2/3 innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood snapped a 10-game losing streak over his past 14 road starts with an 8-7 win over the Mets on Sunday. Millwood allowed two runs in six innings and is now 3-0 with a 4.50 ERA in four starts since coming off the disabled list on May 30. He missed 20 days with a strained right groin muscle. Millwood has never faced the Nationals since the move to Washington, but he is 15-5 with a 3.60 ERA against that franchise while they were in Montreal. That's his most victories against any Major League team.

home_pitcher_note: Nationals right-hander Garrett Mock is the leading candidate to replace left-hander Odalis Perez in the rotation against the Rangers. Mock has a 4-2 record and a 3.12 ERA with Triple-A Columbus. The last time Mock pitched in the big leagues was on June 8, against the Giants. It was his Major League debut, and it was an outing he would like to forget. He didn't get past the fifth inning, as the Nationals lost, 6-3, at Nationals Park.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard is 0-3 with an 8.22 ERA in his past five Major League starts. That includes a 4-2 loss to the Mets on Sunday in which he gave up four runs on eight hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings. That was his first start since returning from Triple-A Oklahoma. He was optioned to Oklahoma at the end of May to work on his command and was 0-1 with a 4.97 ERA in two starts for the RedHawks. This is his first appearance ever against the Nationals. Gabbard is 2-6 with a 5.44 ERA in 21 games, including 18 starts, on the road in his career.

home_pitcher_note: It looked like Lannan was going to have one of his best outings last Tuesday against the Twins, but he made one mistake. He didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning -- a double by Joe Mauer. Lannan was cruising, in fact, until the sixth inning. After getting two quick outs in that inning, Lannan's breaking balls betrayed him. On a 2-2 slider, he gave up a single to Mauer. The next hitter was Justin Morneau, who hit the first pitch he saw -- a curveball -- for a two-run homer. The ball landed in the right-field upper deck.
away_pitcher_note: After earning his ninth victory Tuesday against Atlanta, Padilla has won seven of his last 10 starts. He allowed just two runs, one earned, in six innings against the Braves, striking out four and lowering his ERA from 3.89 to 3.73. In addition to leading the Rangers in victories, Padilla leads the team with seven quality starts. In his 15 starts this season, he's held opponents to three earned runs or fewer 11 times, and seven times he's kept opponents to no more than one earned run. In 14 games, 10 of which starts, against the Washington franchise, Padilla is 3-4 with a 3.99 ERA. In his last two starts against Washington, which both came in 2005, Padilla is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann turned in another solid start for the Nationals against Minnesota. He surrendered just three runs -- only one of them earned -- over six innings. Bergmann struck out two and threw 106 pitches, 61 of them for strikes. However, he picked up the loss, as the Twins pitching staff shut down the Washington lineup in an 11-2 defeat.
away_pitcher_note: There hasn't been a more consistent pitcher in the game than Lackey since his return May 14 from a triceps injury. He went 7 2/3 innings in his latest gem, holding the Mets to a run on a pair of ground-ball singles and a double play. He struck out seven and walked one man, the final hitter he faced. In the sixth, with a runner in scoring position, he reached back and struck out the side, including David Wright looking. Lackey has yielded one earned run in five of his seven starts, surrendering two and three earned runs in his other appearances. Lackey has faced the Nationals once, giving up four earned runs in six innings of a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hill struggled in his last start in Minnesota, lasting just 3 2/3 innings. He gave up seven runs -- six earned -- on 10 hits over the start, while striking out two. Hill's problem wasn't throwing strikes, as 53 of his 78 pitches found the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky start, Garland settled down and kept the Angels in the game Wednesday against the Mets, holding them to three runs (two earned) in six innings. The big right-hander has settled into a nice groove of late, getting early-count outs and pitching with a nice tempo by keeping his fastball in the strike zone. Garland, with the White Sox, faced the Nationals franchise twice, going 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Redding pitched strong through a sour stomach in the Nationals 14-inning 4-3 win. The right-hander showed up to the park under the weather, but turned out a strong performance for Washington, going six innings and striking out five while only giving up three runs. He also retired 13 of the last 14 batters he faced. The Nationals have won Redding's last eight starts, though he hasn't picked up a decision since May 19.
away_pitcher_note: In an outing that ranked with the best of his career, Santana shut down the Phillies Friday night in their own park, holding them to one unearned run on two hits and two walks in seven dominant innings. Overpowering in the middle innings, he produced three of his nine strikeouts in the fourth -- Ryan Howard and Pat Burrell looking, Geoff Jenkins swinging. Santana's fastball was consistently in the 95-97 range, and his changeup and slider were finding excellent spots. He never has faced the Nationals (or Expos).

home_pitcher_note: Perez will make his first start in almost three weeks after missing his last two with shoulder tendinitis. The southpaw pitched four innings Saturday night for the Class A Potomac Nationals, going four innings and striking out five. He gave up just one earned run over the start, throwing 56 pitches and 41 strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera rebounded in his last start, when he allowed three runs in the first three innings and settled down to work through the seventh. The right-hander hasn't won since May 20 and has gone six starts without a positive result. Cabrera struck out a season-high eight batters in his last start and has walked zero batters four times this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan upped his quality start total to 11, best among rookies, in a performance that is becoming typical for the young left-hander. Over six innings, he allowed just two hits and four runs while striking out six and walking none. He got no decision for his trouble, but he dropped his ERA to 3.34, 13th best in the Majors and second best among rookies.
away_pitcher_note: Olson had another middling start in his last outing, a performance where he showed the best and the worst of his abilities. The southpaw recorded three perfect innings against Milwaukee, but he also gave up two long home runs. Olson has completed five innings in all but two of his starts and has allowed three earned runs or less seven times in 11 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann went seven innings and gave up one run on six hits in his last start. He struck out six batters and walked none. Manager Manny Acta said he knew in the first inning that Bergmann was going to have a great outing. The Nats starter was getting quick outs and his pitch count was low.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie allowed two home runs and not much else in his last start, an adrenaline-pumping victory over the Cubs. The right-hander has won just twice in his last eight starts, though, a function of low run support and untimely runs allowed. Guthrie has steadily worked late in the game this season and leads the Orioles in innings (108 2/3) and strikeouts (70).

home_pitcher_note: Tucker's last start was one he'd probably like to forget. The 21-year-old rookie surrendered a career-high seven runs off eight hits against the Rays on Wednesday and was never able to get out of a brutal fifth inning. That inning saw the Marlins give up a season-high 10 runs, with Tucker giving up three before getting a single out. Despite retiring six of the first seven batters he faced, Tucker left after throwing 83 pitches while walking two and striking out three in four-plus innings. The Burbank, Calif., native will be facing the Nationals on Monday for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Redding had seven straight no-decisions. In each of those decisions, Redding went at least five innings. The last time he won a game was May 19 against the Phillies. His last start was on Wednesday against the Angels. He lasted six innings and gave up two runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Hendrickson had a hard time commanding his fastball against the Rays on Thursday, and it ended up costing him his fourth loss in his last four decisions. The 6-foot-9 lefty finished the day allowing five runs on five hits and five walks and left the game after throwing 102 pitches -- 56 for strikes -- in just 4 2/3 innings. It was the sixth time in his last 10 outings Hendrickson has thrown over 90 pitches in less than six innings. The most telling moment in that game was when he intentionally walked the No. 8 hitter with two outs to get to pitcher Matt Garza -- who threw a complete-game, one-hitter -- but ended up walking him to load the bases, leading to a run.
away_pitcher_note: Balester will make his Major League debut for the Nationals in Miami, taking the place of the injured Shawn Hill. Balester is considered one of the Nationals' top prospects, and he follows Tyler Clippard and Garrett Mock in getting a Major League appearance in place of an injured Nationals pitcher. Balester is 9-3 with a 4.00 ERA in 78 2/3 innings pitched. The young right-hander has struck out 64 batters while only walking 23 this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco may not make the All-Star team, but he's pitched like one in June. A winner of three consecutive decisions, Nolasco yielded one run in eight innings, with nine strikeouts and one walk, in his last start -- a 3-1 decision over Arizona. Nolasco is more comfortable with his cut fastball, and his fastball is reaching 94 mph. He threw 120 pitches, marking his third straight outing of at least 100 pitches. For the second time in his career, he has a streak of three straight starts of seven or more innings.
away_pitcher_note: Perez pitched well in his return from the disabled list. Working on an 80-pitch limit, the veteran left-hander tossed four shutout innings, striking out three. He said after the start that he felt no pain, and he's expected to make his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was solid in his last outing at Cleveland on Saturday and didn't allow a single run for the first time this season. Having lost his three previous starts, Cueto's resounding return to the win column came in a solid 6 1/3-inning performance in which he gave up just five hits with three walks and two strikeouts as his ERA dipped below 5.00 for the first time since late April. The 22-year-old hasn't given up more than five hits in any of his last four starts and has a 1.47 ERA over his last three. Cueto has never faced the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan struggled in his last outing, allowing four earned runs and seven runs overall. He lasted just five innings and struck out only one batter. The young left-hander also hurt himself in the field, committing an error that led to a run. Still, his 3.54 ERA is one of the best in the league among rookies.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo followed what he called the worst outing of his career with one that was much more palatable. He threw six innings and gave up just two runs -- one earned -- with two walks and six strikeouts in a 9-5 victory over the Indians on Sunday. He didn't allow a run through his first five innings, though he was the first to admit after the game that he didn't have anywhere near his best stuff while on the mound. The win snapped a five-game winless streak for Arroyo.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann nearly shut down the Orioles in his last start, allowing only a seventh-inning home run by Luke Scott to blot the scoreboard. He threw 62 strikes in 100 pitches and struck out three in seven innings of work. He got a no-decision, however, as the Nationals snatched a 3-2 walk-off victory over Baltimore on Ronnie Belliard's 12th-inning, two-run homer.
