home_pitcher_note: Fogg is expected to return to the Majors from a rehab assignment and be activated from the disabled list prior to Saturday's game, starting in place of Aaron Harang, who has been bothered by stiffness in his right forearm and will face the Cubs on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Redding recorded his eighth straight no-decision on Tuesday against the Marlins. The 30-year-old allowed four runs on eight hits while striking out two and left after tossing 111 pitches in five-plus innings. The five-plus innings were the shortest Redding had gone since April 23 against the Mets -- also a five-inning outing.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez gave up three runs on seven hits with three walks and three strikeouts through 5 1/3 innings in his last start, against the Pirates on Tuesday. The 24-year-old right-hander didn't pitch badly, but he didn't pitch his best and was taken out after he was unable to retire the first three batters he faced in the sixth. He threw 96 pitches, and as has become customary with Volquez's overly active pitches, just 54 went for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League debut, Balester made his presence felt when he went up against the Marlins on Tuesday. The 6-foot-5 rookie, called up from Triple-A Columbus to take the place of Shawn Hill in the rotation, picked up the win after pitching five innings of one-hit, one-run ball. Balester, who left after throwing 95 pitches, had a no-hitter going until giving up a leadoff hit in the fifth inning. That fifth saw Balester walk the opposing pitcher on four straight pitches and give up the game's first run, but he worked out of a bases-loaded, one-out jam to preserve a one-run lead.

home_pitcher_note: Making his second start since coming off the disabled list after having left shoulder tendinitis, Perez retired the first 11 Marlins hitters in order and threw 21 of his 23 pitches for strikes in the first three innings. The 30-year-old left after allowing one run on five hits while striking out three in 6 2/3 innings. Perez's night ended after a 1-hour, 33-minute rain delay ensued with a runner on second and two outs in the seventh. He finished throwing 77 pitches -- 53 for strikes -- and lost his chance at the win when reliever Charlie Manning gave up a two-run homer to the first batter he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Webb was let off the hook in his last start by an unpredictable ninth-inning rally by the D-backs. The right-hander, just named to the National League All-Star team, allowed five earned runs in six innings to the Brewers. Webb, who is still tied for first in the Majors with 12 wins this season, is 3-2 with a 3.13 ERA in seven games in his career against the Nationals. In his first start against the Nationals on May 31, he threw a shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan put together another quality start, allowing three runs on five hits over six innings. The rookie left-hander struck out three and walked three for the no-decision as the Nationals' bullpen gave up two seventh-inning runs and Washington's offense couldn't close the gap in a 5-3 loss to the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Owings missed his last start on Wednesday against the Brewers because of an injured gluteus muscle suffered in his previous start while running to cover first base. Yusmeiro Petit filled in nicely against the Brewers, going six innings, allowing just two hits and one run in a no-decision. Through his last nine starts, Owings is 2-6. Against the Nationals, Owings is 1-1 with a 3.57 ERA in three starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann turned out yet another quality start, something becoming more commonplace among Nationals starters. He pitched six innings and gave up just three runs, two earned, striking out five. He threw 64 strikes in 104 pitches. However, the Nationals' offense couldn't get any runs across in a 3-0 loss to Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Haren, recently named to his second All-Star Game, was the NL Pitcher of the Month for June, during which he was 3-0 with a 1.32 ERA in six starts. He could easily have had more wins with better run support. He leads NL starters with a 5.15 strikeout-to-walk ratio and is tops in fewest walks per nine innings with 1.53 and WHIP at 0.98. In his five no-decisions this year, he has a 2.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Redding didn't allow hits to translate into runs in his last outing in Cincinnati. The veteran right-hander allowed eight hits but just one run in six innings of work in the Queen City, striking out four. The game turned into his ninth consecutive no-decision, however, in a 3-2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is slated to slide back in the rotation after missing two starts with a sore left hip. Oswalt's most recent outing against the Dodgers on June 30 was cut short because of the injury, which was too bad for the Astros, considering the ace righty looked better than he had all year. Oswalt struck out nine Dodgers during his six-inning, 79-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Balester struggled a bit more in his second Major League start than in his first, but he still turned in an efficient outing. The rookie right-hander gave up five runs and four hits over 5 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out three. He threw 102 pitches, 59 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Assuming Sampson goes back to the 'pen and Roy Oswalt isn't ready to return to the mound, Rodriguez will remain on his regular schedule and open the series in Washington. The left-hander yielded three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings in his most recent outing in Atlanta. Rodriguez allowed seven earned runs over 5 1/3 innings in a start versus the Nationals last year. Lifetime against the franchise, he's 2-1 with a 5.34 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perez didn't last long in his last start against the D-backs -- he was ejected after 2 2/2 innings for arguing a second balk called against him. The southpaw had just given up a run prior to the second balk that was directly related to the first balk. During the start, Perez walked one and struck out two. The Nationals bullpen pitched 6 1/3 innings of relief and allowed just one unearned run, but Brandon Webb shut down Washington's offense for a 2-0 Arizona win.
away_pitcher_note: Backe will get the nod for the final game before the All-Star break, and he should be well-rested. He threw only 48 pitches in his last start versus the Pirates, which was cut short when the game was delayed, twice. Backe pitched three scoreless innings in that game. He's 1-1 with a 3.85 ERA over two career games versus the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson held the Dodgers without a hit for four innings on July 9 but was saddled with a loss, his seventh of the season, when the Braves could produce just one run off Derek Lowe. Hudson scattered four hits and two runs over seven strong innings and trimmed his ERA to 3.16. In 11 career starts against the Nationals, Hudson is 7-1 with a 1.13 ERA. He is 1-0 against them this season, allowing three runs on 13 hits in 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Redding picked up his first win in 10 starts on July 11 against Houston, snapping a streak of nine straight no-decisions. He pitched six innings, allowing no runs and striking out six. The seasoned right-hander said after the game that he felt comfortable with his fastball, which helped him get ahead of hitters routinely in the Nationals 10-0 win over Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens capped off the first half of his rookie season with a resounding victory, pitching six innings and striking out six in a 9-3 Braves win over the Dodgers on July 8. It was Jurrjens' ninth win of the season, as the 22-year-old entered the All-Star break with loads of confidence. Jurrjens will be returning from the All-Star break to face the Nationals, against whom he has had success this season. He gave up just two hits and one run in seven innings on April 30 but did not factor in the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan threw his 13th quality start July 9 in a 5-0 victory against Arizona, his first win since May 18. Long suffering from poor run support, Lannan got more than enough against the D-backs, as Jesus Flores' three-run homer packed away the game in the sixth. Though he admitted he didn't have his "best" stuff, Lannan still threw six shutout innings, inducing three double plays in the process.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes' final start before the All-Star break lasted only four innings, as he gave up two runs on five hits, including two triples, in a losing effort. Reyes struggled with his command and was taken out after throwing just 64 pitches. The 23-year-old left-hander has not reached the sixth inning in three of his past four starts. Reyes hasn't won since June 13, a span of five starts. He has never faced the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Perez got himself into trouble more than once against Houston in his last start before the break, allowing nine hits over six innings. However, thanks to six strikeouts and some cluth pitching, the left-hander allowed just three runs to cross the plate. It would not be enough, however, as the Nationals fell to Houston, 5-0, at home.

home_pitcher_note: Zito technically didn't record a "quality start" when he faced Washington on June 8, but he still recorded a victory on a sweltering afternoon, interrupting his season-opening skid of nine loss in 10 decisions. Zito worked five innings that day, surrendering three runs and seven hits while walking four and striking out two. Zito trailed 3-0 in that game before the Giants rallied for four runs in the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann pitched nearly lights-out for seven innings Thursday against Arizona. The right-hander didn't even allow a hit until the fourth, and he surrendered just two runs over the outing. He struck out three in his fifth straight quality start but picked up a no-decision, as the Nationals fell, 7-5, in the 11th after rallying from two down in the ninth and three down in the 10th.

home_pitcher_note: Correia has had a long time to contemplate what he called one of his worst outings in a long time. He yielded seven runs and nine hits in 3 2/3 innings on July 12 at Chicago. Correia confessed that he didn't feel right from the game's first pitch, and it showed. "When I've had my chances to turn an outing into a good one, I'm not making the pitches," Correia said after facing the Cubs. He owns a 1-1 record with a 2.55 ERA in eight career appearances against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Balester found the going rough in his third career outing, lasting just 4 2/3 innings and surrendering six runs, though just four were earned. The young right-hander struggled to keep runners off the basepaths against Houston, allowing 11 hits over his short outing. He exited in the fifth with the bases loaded, but Jesus Colome struck out Miguel Tejada to end the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Cain pitched capably in his previous start -- six innings, three earned runs -- but he walked as many (five) as he struck out. Through the season, the righty's problems have revolved around his control. He's walked at least three batters in his past four starts and occasionally struggles keeping the ball down in the zone. Because of his location issues, Cain needed 110 pitches in his last outing -- nearly 20 per inning.
away_pitcher_note: Redding was chased after allowing six runs on six hits in four innings Friday against the Braves, taking his first loss since May 9. Since then, the right-hander had nine no-decisions and a win, when he tossed six scoreless innings against the Astros on July 10 in his final start before the All-Star break. He said he wasn't rusty Friday, and threw a bullpen session earlier in the week to prepare for the start. His command with his fastball was good, but he missed his location with two offspeed pitches that cost him five runs. Redding is 0-4 with a 6.49 ERA in seven career games (five starts) against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley went into the break having won five of his last six decisions, but he fell to 0-3 against Arizona this year and really scuffled doing it. Maybe it was the extra rest during the five days off, but he allowed seven hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings and was taken deep in the first inning by Conor Jackson on a hanging breaking ball. By the time he straightened out his timing, his pitch count was into triple digits.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan finally got some run support Saturday against the Braves, allowing one run in six strong innings and cruising to an 8-2 win. It was just the second time this season that Lannan had recorded back-to-back wins; the first coming on April 22 and 27. Lannan struck out four and walked three, escaping bases-loaded jams in the fourth and fifth innings with just one run allowed. Entering Saturday's start, Lannan had received the lowest run support -- 2.72 runs per start -- of any qualifying starter in the Majors this season. The 23-year-old lefty has never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe followed the trend in the series against Arizona with an awful first inning, allowing three runs, although there was a defensive breakdown involved. He didn't pick up a ball in his 10 days off going into and coming out of the All-Star break and had no command in the early innings. At a time when the Dodgers have really needed a veteran to step up and assume the role of ace, Lowe has been erratic. And his layoff was the result of avoiding having to start in Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Perez was far from perfect Sunday, but he didn't need to be. The Nationals scored 12 runs in the first four innings, and Perez cruised to his third win of the season after allowing five runs on nine hits in five innings. On a hot and muggy afternoon in Atlanta, Perez became tired after running from first to third in the fourth inning. He said his legs felt drained when he came out in the bottom half of the inning, and he gave up three runs. Perez will be facing his former team, the Dodgers, for the first time Saturday since he was traded to the Royals in the middle of the 2006 season. He last pitched against Los Angeles on May 11, 2001, as a member of the Braves. In that outing, Perez pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings, scattering five hits and getting the win. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in three career starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw became Coors Field's latest victim. Promoted to start against the Rockies, he was pounded for 10 hits, didn't retire a batter in the fourth inning and was charged with five earned runs. Perhaps a return to sea level will lead to his first Major League victory. He's been rushed to the big leagues and it hasn't been an easy adjustment. He threw only one changeup against the Rockies, after being sent down for three weeks to work on the pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann struggled to keep the ball in the park in his first post-All-Star break start, when he faced San Francisco. He gave up three home runs -- two to Bengie Molina and one on his first pitch to Fred Lewis -- that accounted for four of the Giants' five runs. Bergmann lasted five innings, striking out one batter and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Balester registered a solid outing in his last start in San Francisco. He pitched five innings, allowing just six hits and three runs for his second lowest total in four Major League starts. He also struck out two and walked two, and he threw 44 strikes in 74 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Myers allowed three runs in five innings in his return to action against the Mets on Wednesday after a three-week stint in the Minor Leagues. The 27-year-old got off to a rough start, walking four consecutive batters in the first inning. He eventually settled in, ultimately retiring the last six batters he faced. Another positive was that Myers did not allow a home run after allowing a Major-League-leading 24 before being optioned. Myers has faced Washington twice this season, recording an 0-1 record and allowing six earned runs in 11 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Despite being given an extra day of rest, Cueto did not have a good outing in a 5-4 loss to the Astros on Monday. home_pitcher_note: Cook has continued to push the Diamondbacks' Brandon Webb for most wins in the National League. away_pitcher_note: Redding struggled through one of his worst performances of the season last Wednesday against Philadelphia. away_pitcher_note: Balester lasted 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, another impressive start for the young right-hander. He throw 101 pitches, 63 for strikes, and fanned five batters. He allowed just one run -- on a solo homer in the sixth. He walked two and struck out one.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets looks to snap a five-start winless streak in which he's gone 0-3 with two no-decisions. away_pitcher_note: Lannan registered a positively dominant performance in Colorado on Tuesday, when he struck out eight over seven innings, using his curveball to keep hitters off balance. away_pitcher_note: Santana pitched well against the Padres on Thursday, but his 10th win eluded him again as the Mets' bullpen could not hold onto his lead. away_pitcher_note: Maine, fully healed from a strained right rotator cuff, will come off the disabled list in time for his next time around in the Mets' rotation, putting him back into the No. 2 starter role. home_pitcher_note: Balester turned in another good performance in his last start against the Brewers, allowing just four runs, three earned. He went five innings and struck out four, but the Nationals were shut down by Milwaukee hurler CC Sabathia and Balester picked up the loss, his fourth of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Perez threw seven scoreless innings Friday, holding the Marlins to two hits and striking out eight. His slider hit every spot he aimed for, starting it over the plate and having it slide in toward right-handed batters, and Perez's fastball showed a tremendous amount of life at 95 mph. On April 24, his first and only outing against Washington this year, he allowed five runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding struggled against Milwaukee last Saturday, allowing three home runs and five runs overall in just five innings. He struck out three, but got no offensive support as Washington got shut out for the second straight day in a 6-0 loss.

away_pitcher_note: Hernandez couldn't have gotten off to a worse start as a Rockie. home_pitcher_note: Perez started for Washington on Tuesday and pitched six solid innings, giving up three runs on eight hits against the Mets. away_pitcher_note: Redding pitched well in his last start but was plagued by a three-run fifth inning in which all of the runs that scored came with two outs in a 4-3 defeat against the Rockies. away_pitcher_note: Campillo seemed to right himself while delivering five solid innings and getting a no-decision against the Cardinals on Saturday. home_pitcher_note: Balester won his third game of the season last Tuesday, giving up a run in five-plus innings against the Dodgers. away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has thrown 16 more innings than he had during any of his previous professional seasons, and the fatigue is starting to show. away_pitcher_note: Kendrick lasted five-plus innings against the Mets on Wednesday, allowing two earned runs in earning the no-decision. away_pitcher_note: Though it's not reflected in wins and losses, Hamels has been spectacular for nearly two months, posting a 2.69 ERA in his previous 16 starts, spanning 113 2/3 innings. away_pitcher_note: Martis will make his Major League debut against the Braves. He is a keeper for Washington. home_pitcher_note: Hampton reached another milestone, in what has already been a comeback year, during a no-decision against the Marlins on Monday. Also impressive about Nolasco's 2008 season was the fact he struck out 186 while walking just 42. He has a goal of walking fewer than 25 this season. For his career, Nolasco is 5-1 with a 3.53 ERA lifetime vs. Washington, including 2-0 (2.08 ERA) last year.

He needed just 10 pitches to get through a 1-2-3 fourth inning, only allowed four runners in scoring position and struck out six batters through the first five. Through 15 2/3 innings this season -- including a start against the Nationals -- Johnson has given up just one run on 12 hits.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Cabrera gave up one earned run in five innings against the Phillies. It helped lower his ERA to 4.91, which is the best among the Nationals starters. Cabrera will face the Marlins for the second time this season. In that first game, Cabrera became the first Nationals starter to pitch past the third inning. But the bad news was that Washington lost to the Marlins, 6-4, at Dolphin Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: On April 8, Volstad worked five innings and allowed two runs on his way to a win over the Nationals at Dolphin Stadium. Now, the 22-year-old gets to face them in Washington. This will be the 6-foot-8 right-hander's first start at Nationals Park. He struck out a career-high seven on April 8. Volstad enters the contest fresh off one of his finest outings. Opening Florida's three-city, nine-game road trip in Atlanta, he worked seven innings, giving up only three hits and one run, which came on Kelly Johnson's homer.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will be called up from Triple-A Syracuse to make his Major League debut. Selected by the Nationals out of the University of Wisconsin - Stevens Point in the second round of the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Zimmerman went 10-3 in the Minors last year with a 2.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe struggled with his control while throwing 106 pitches and matching a career-high five walks in a five-inning effort against the Marlins on Tuesday night. His April 10 start against the Nationals was limited to three innings because of a lengthy rain delay. In his two starts against the Nationals last year, he worked 16 innings, surrendered seven hits and allowed just two earned runs. The 36-year-old sinkerballer began this season by allowing two hits in eight scoreless innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Martis pitched 6 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on five hits against the Phillies on Thursday. Of the 26 batters he faced, Martis threw 19 first-pitch strikes. Even more impressive, Martis held Jimmy Rollins, Chase Utley and Ryan Howard to a combined 1-for-6. Martis is a guy who is often overshadowed. It was believed that right-hander Jordan Zimmermann would be the fourth starter in the rotation, and Martis would start the season as the fifth starter and pitch in the Minor Leagues because of the off-days on April 9 and 14. But Martis outpitched Zimmermann in Spring Training, and now has helped the Nationals get the first victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see what kind of adjustments the Nationals make while getting their second look at Kawakami.  While winning his Major League debut against the Nationals on April 10, the 33-year-old Japanese right-hander allowed three earned runs and four hits in six innings. With an average fastball that occasionally sits up in the zone, he has already surrendered a pair of three-run homers in his young big league career. But with an effective slow curveball, he has also notched 15 strikeouts in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had his best outing of the young season last Friday. In his previous two outings, Lannan had allowed 10 runs in nine innings. He wasn't aggressive and was often behind in the count, but this time, Lannan lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on three hits against the Marlins. The southpaw trusted his fastball, and he was able to get it on the inside part of the plate a lot more often. Lannan cruised through the first three innings, but he had problems in the fourth inning after allowing a solo homer to Marlins catcher John Baker. He loaded the bags following Baker's blast, but he got out of the jam without allowing another run.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling with his control while winning his first two starts of the season, Jurrjens produced one of the strongest starts of his young career and suffered his first loss on Friday night at PNC Park. The 23-year-old right-hander limited the Pirates to one run and four hits in 6 2/3 innings. The two walks he issued were drawn by the final two batters he faced at the end of his career-high 120-pitch effort. Jurrjens allowed three earned runs while issuing five walks in an April 12 start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Santana leads the National League and is second in the Majors with a 0.46 ERA. Still, the Mets ace is 2-1 and has received a total of four runs of offensive support. Saturday's win was typical Johan -- seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts -- and the Mets' one run was enough for the win. Santana has been unstoppable this season and didn't allow a Brewers batter past first base in his most recent start.
away_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Olsen was given a five-run cushion after one inning against the Marlins, but he struggled in the top of the second inning, when Ronny Paulino hit a two-run homer. After that, it was smooth sailing. The lefty lasted seven innings and gave up three runs (two earned) on six hits. It was the Nationals' third straight quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey will be making his first start since April 13 after being scratched from his last start because of tendinitis in his right forearm. He was anything but spectacular in his first two starts, giving up four earned runs in five innings against the Reds followed by five earned runs in five innings against the Padres. He combined to give up 13 hits, including three home runs, and six walks during his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, Cabrera has given up a combined three earned runs in 10 innings, but doesn't have a win to show for it. When he left the game in the top of the sixth inning on Sunday against the Marlins, Cabrera had a 3-2 lead before the watching the bullpen blow it. The Nationals ended up losing the game, 7-4.

home_pitcher_note: Perez breezed through four innings against the Cardinals on Tuesday before falling apart in the fifth, when he allowed four runs on three hits and two walks to tie the game and end his day. Perez was roughed up for eight earned runs in just 4 1/3 innings in his first start of the season against Cincinnati but followed that up against San Diego when he gave up just one run in six innings to earn his first win of the year. If the pattern of bad start, good start continues for Perez, he should be in line for a good outing on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: After a two-hour, 10-minute rain delay, Zimmermann threw his first big league pitch on Monday. He was solid as the Nationals edged the Braves, 3-2, at Nationals Park. Zimmermann, the team's best prospect entering this season, went six innings and gave up two runs on six hits. He threw 72 pitches, 51 of them for strikes. Manager Manny Acta thought about letting Zimmermann pitch another inning, but the Nationals started a rally in the bottom of the sixth, so Acta decided to have Alex Cintron pinch-hit.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is still searching for his first victory of 2009. In three starts, the right-hander has given up 25 hits and 13 earned runs. Blanton was effective against the Brewers in his last start, on Wednesday, allowing eight hits and three earned runs in six innings. In his previous start against the Nationals, he also surrendered eight hits and three earned runs. He's been keeping the Phillies in the game, but one pitch here and there has hurt. Against the Brewers, it was a solo homer to J.J. Hardy in the fifth inning. Against the Nationals, it was a three-run shot to Adam Dunn in the first.
away_pitcher_note: Martis threw six innings and gave up three runs -- two earned -- on six hits against the Braves on Tuesday. All three runs were scored in the first inning. Martis was able to get two quick outs, but then he walked Chipper Jones and Brian McCann. Casey Kotchman followed and doubled to right-center field to bring home Jones. Jeff Francoeur came to the plate and hit a ground ball to shortstop Alberto Gonzalez, who threw the ball past first baseman Nick Johnson to score McCann and Kotchman. It was smooth sailing after that. Martis blanked the Braves and gave up four hits over the next five innings.

home_pitcher_note: So far, 2009 hasn't been kind to Hamels. He missed time in March because of inflammation in his left eblow, then carried an 11.17 ERA into Thursday's start against the Milwaukee Brewers. But in the top of the fourth inning, Brewers first baseman Prince Fielder ripped a line drive off the back of Hamels' right shoulder, forcing him to leave the game. Hamels said he is fine and that he won't have any problems starting next Tuesday. The Phillies hope he is right. They need their ace to start pitching effectively again.
away_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, Lannan has given up one run in his last 13 1/3 innings. He also has seen his ERA drop from 18.00 to 4.43. On Tuesday, he will face the Phillies for the fifth time in his career. He is 0-3 with a 6.43 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is still looking for that first dominant performance of 2009, although his last two starts have been quality starts. But home runs continue to hurt him. In his start Friday against the Florida Marlins at Dolphin Stadium, he allowed a three-run home run to Dan Uggla in the first inning. It would be the only three runs he would allow in six innings. Myers has allowed 26 hits this season. Eight of them have been home runs.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday against the Mets, Olsen pitched well enough for his second consecutive quality start, but he ended up losing his third game of the season because of some shoddy defense. Olsen lasted six innings and gave up three runs, two of which were earned.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets, Cabrera retired the first two batters he faced. Then the problems started. After Carlos Beltran singled and Carlos Delgado walked, David Wright hit what looked like a routine fly ball to center fielder Elijah Dukes. But Dukes, who had his sunglasses on the top of his head, lost the ball in the sun as it dropped in for a two-base error, which allowed two runs to score. By the time he left the game in the third inning, Cabrera threw 86 pitches, and the Mets had a 5-0 lead. Cabrera said he was not rattled by Dukes' error. He felt he should have been able to give the Nationals a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs earned this start by pitching very well five days earlier. He showed against the Cubs just what he needs to be effective: keep his sinking fastball down in the strike zone, and get chases with his breaking ball. Those things won't always both be there for him, but when they are, he's well-equipped to get Major League hitters out. He won't blow many people away, but he has good enough stuff to get outs.

home_pitcher_note: Call Jordan Zimmermann the Nationals' stopper. The right-hander tossed another great game and helped the Nationals defeat the Mets, 8-1, on Sunday to snap a three-game losing streak. There were 40,023 at Citi Field, and Zimmerman had never pitched in front of a large crowd before. But there were no signs of nervousness on his part. Zimmermann pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on six hits. He didn't go any further because he threw 103 pitches. But even more impressive was how he handled the heart of the Mets' order, as Carlos Beltran, Carlos Delgado and David Wright went a combined 2-for-9 with six strikeouts against the right-hander. The game plan was to mix his pitches against the trio.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's season has been frustrating to him and the Cardinals. After it appeared that he was getting straightened out, he turned in two more disappointing starts his past two times out. Wellemeyer's mechanics remain a bit out of whack, and he's also given up more than his share of bloops, flares, rollers and the like for hits. He finally started missing bats in the last couple of innings on Sunday, an indication that maybe he found something.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, the offense gave Martis a 6-2 lead after 4 1/2 innings against the Phillies. But the Phillies came back and tied the score in the bottom of the fifth. The bases were loaded when Ryan Howard drilled a 1-2 pitch for a grand slam to tie the score at 6-6. Martis pitched five-plus innings and gave up seven runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Statistically, it's been a very odd season for Pineiro. He has almost as many wins (four) as strikeouts (six), a ratio that it's just about impossible to keep up. Still, he's getting deep into games and throwing strikes, so as long as his defense keeps converting balls in play into outs, he has a chance to keep being effective. He really would do well to start getting at least a few strikeouts here and there, though.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Lannan had one bad inning and it proved costly. The contest was scoreless until the third. After Shane Victorino singled with one out, Chase Utley drove an 0-2 pitch over the right-field wall for a two-run homer. Lannan tried to throw the pitch in the dirt, but it stayed up in the zone. Lannan was able to get the second out of the inning, but found himself in trouble again. Jayson Werth reached on an error by shortstop Alberto Gonzalez. Lannan said the shoddy defense didn't rattle him, but he continued to have problems on the mound. After Raul Ibanez walked to put runners on first and second, Pedro Feliz hit a three-run homer to make it 5-0. Two innings later, Utley hit his second homer of the game, a solo shot over the right-field wall to give Philadelphia a 6-0 lead. Lannan pitched five innings and gave up six runs (three earned) on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler slides back into the rotation after missing nearly three weeks with a sprained right knee. The right-hander made two rehab starts, reaching 90 pitches in his most recent outing at Double-A Frisco on April 29. Moehler has faced the Nationals 12 times in his career, including seven starts. He has a 2-4 record and a 5.95 ERA vs. Washington, allowing 26 earned runs over 39 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: MacDougal may not be used. When the game resumes in the bottom of the 11th inning tied at 10-10, the Nationals will have a runner on first with one out and can win the game. However, if the game continues into the 12th, MacDougal will take the mound. Manager Manny Acta said that he will have six of seven relievers available, with the exception being Julian Tavarez.
away_pitcher_note: LaTroy Hawkins was on the mound for the Astros when their May 5 game against Washington was halted by rain and the Astros see fit for him to continue his outing when the game resumes. Pitchers Roy Oswalt, Chris Sampson and Tim Byrdak are not eligible to pitch because they were used and removed from the game on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw rebounded from his worst start in Colorado with one of his best. He matched Jake Peavy for seven scoreless innings, allowing four singles and two walks. Kershaw was able to work his way out of four jams with runners in scoring position. Kershaw relied on his 94-mph fastball and was able to pitch deep enough to give the tired bullpen a bit of a break one night after James McDonald's 1 2/3-inning start.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera set a team record by uncorking four wild pitches on Thursday night against the Cardinals. Cabrera's first two wild pitches were thrown in the first inning. With Cardinals first baseman Albert Pujols at the plate, Cabrera tossed a wild pitch that allowed Colby Rasmus to advance to second base. On the next pitch, Cabrera threw another wild pitch, sending Rasmus to third. In the second inning, after Jason LaRue singled, Cabrera uncorked his third wild pitch, allowing LaRue to advance to second base. The wild pitch tied former Nationals right-hander John Patterson for the team record. In fifth inning, Cabrera set the record by throwing his fourth wild pitch, allowing Skip Schumaker to advance to third. Cabrera ended up having a quality start, pitching six innings while giving up three runs on four hits in a 9-4 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf was impressive on Saturday as he allowed just two hits and one run over 5 1/3 innings against the Padres on Saturday. But the left-hander was saddled with the no-decision because one of the hits was a solo home run by Edgar Gonzalez in the first inning, and Wolf exited in the sixth with the game tied, 1-1. He also struck out four and walked four. Wolf is 9-4 with a 4.58 ERA against the Nationals in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Although Zimmermann gave up a season-high five runs in a 6-2 loss to the Cardinals at Nationals Park on Friday night, manager Manny Acta was happy with his performance. After serving up three homers, Zimmermann didn't get rattled and continued to throw strikes. In fact, he didn't walk a batter in the game. Too many times this season, Acta has watched his pitchers not named Zimmermann try to nibble around the plate and end up walking batters.

home_pitcher_note: Petit didn't bounce back resoundingly after three starts' worth of struggle in the early going, but he did enjoy better results Sunday in Milwaukee. The right-hander allowed three runs -- two on back-to-back homers and another on a two-out infield single -- on four hits in five innings. Manager Bob Melvin said he never suggested Petit's starting spot was in jeopardy prior to the outing, so it seems probable that the young hurler will get more opportunities with Brandon Webb on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Martis threw a complete game and gave up one run his last time out. It was the first nine-inning complete game by a Nationals pitcher since Pedro Astacio went the distance against the Braves on Aug. 15, 2006. It was also the first by a Washington hurler at Nationals Park. Martis' only blemish was giving up a solo home run to Colby Rasmus in the seventh inning. Before the home run, Martis was nearly perfect. In fact, he didn't give up a hit for 4 2/3 innings, and allowed just five hits and no walks overall, while striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Davis did not have one of his better outings in his last start against the Dodgers on Monday. The left-hander allowed four runs on five hits in 4 1/3 innings. Davis walked four in the game. Afterwards he said he felt like he was trying to be too fine with his pitches, which led to him falling behind in counts and putting hitters on. He was helped out in the second inning by a triple play, the second in franchise history, when Casey Blake hit a liner to shortstop Josh Wilson, who started the 6-4-3 triple play. Davis is in the final year of a three-year extension he signed after being traded to Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: After picking up his fist win of the season on Monday against the Astros, Lannan admitted to not having his best stuff. But a win is a win. Lannan allowed four runs -- three earned --  on nine hits over six innings. After struggling to get through the fifth inning, he came back out the sixth and got the Astros' sixth, seventh and eighth hitters on consecutive groundouts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has been the victim of poor run support in his short big league career. In five starts this year, the D-backs have scored a total of six runs for him. It was more of the same his last time out against the Dodgers on Monday, when his teammates managed just one run for him. Scherzer allowed three runs (two earned) in the first inning of what turned out to be a 3-1 loss. The former No. 1 pick is now winless in 21 games (12 starts) dating back to last year when he made his debut by striking out seven Astros in 4 1/3 perfect innings. Scherzer started the year on the disabled list after experiencing shoulder stiffness in January that required a cortisone shot.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen started for the Nationals on Tuesday afternoon at Nationals Park, and by the time he left the game after five innings, the Astros had a 5-2 lead. It was the first time since April 7 that Olsen didn't have a quality start. On Sunday, Olsen will face the Diamondbacks for the fourth time in his career. He is 0-2 with an 8.47 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: If Johnson's pattern holds true, he'll pitch a gem in this one. He allowed seven runs and eight hits in 5 2/3 innings in his last outing at Colorado, but that followed seven scoreless innings on May 1 against the Rockies in San Francisco. Before that, he walked seven in 3 1/3 innings in his April 25 Arizona homecoming. But that contrasted with the seven innings of one-hit ball he threw against the Diamondbacks in his previous outing. This followed a seven-run, 3 2/3-inning struggle at Los Angeles. Johnson himself warned that at age 45, he might be subject to this sort of inconsistency.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, it looked like Cabrera was on his way to having a solid outing, but things unraveled in the fifth inning. With the bases loaded, Cabrera walked Andre Ethier to force home Rafael Furcal and give Los Angeles a 2-1 lead. Cabrera's control problems continued in the next inning. He walked two batters and left the game with the bases loaded. Then it was the bullpen's turn to stop the bleeding. It never happened. The Dodgers blew the game open with seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: All but one of Cain's six outings has been a quality start. Last Thursday at Colorado, he walked four of the first six batters he faced but settled down and lasted six innings, allowing one hit. It marked the ninth time in Cain's career -- including starts of varying lengths -- that he had yielded just one hit. Cain pitched one of his best games against Washington last July 24, when he spun a four-hit shutout in a 1-0 Giants triumph. He's 3-2 with a 2.36 ERA in six lifetime outings against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann started the game on Thursday for Washington and had serious problems in the first inning against the Dodgers. After striking out leadoff hitter Rafael Furcal, Zimmermann couldn't get the next six hitters out. The first run scored on an RBI single by James Loney. Four batters later, Matt Kemp hit a grand slam over the right-center-field wall. Casey Blake followed and hit what looked like a routine fly ball to right-center field, but center fielder Elijah Dukes and right fielder Adam Dunn did not communicate on who was catching the ball, which dropped in for a triple. Dunn said that a fan in the stands called for the ball, and Dunn and Dukes thought the other called for the ball. Blake then scored on a sacrifice fly by Dodgers starter Randy Wolf. After that, Zimmermann retired the next nine hitters he faced. He went on to pitch six innings and give up six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Not long ago, a strong outing from Zito would be regarded as an aberration. Now it's considered almost routine. Zito has thrived in his last four starts, posting a 1.37 ERA in that span. More importantly, the Giants have won each of those games, though Zito earned the decision just once. Zito's resurgence bodes well for him and the Giants, since he's typically a second-half pitcher. Entering this year he was 53-57 with a 4.14 ERA lifetime before the All-Star break and 70-36, 3.47 afterward.
away_pitcher_note: Six days after pitching the first complete game of his career, Martis lasted only 5 1/3 innings on Friday, but it was good enough to help the Nationals defeat the Diamondbacks, 5-4, at Chase Field. Martis allowed three of the four runs on nine hits, while striking out six batters and walking two. What made this start impressive was that Martis was able to get out of jams. For example, after Chris Young tripled home Felipe Lopez to cut the lead to 4-2 with no outs in the fifth inning, Young was left stranded at third. Martis struck out Justin Upton and Mark Reynolds and got Josh Whitesell to fly out to right fielder Austin Kearns. The entire season has been good for Martis, 22. He now leads the Nationals with four wins, which ranks second in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Lannan threw six shutout innings, but struggled throughout the game. He walked six batters but was able to get out of the jams. In the third inning, Arizona had the bases loaded with one out, but Josh Whitesell hit into a double play. Three innings later, the D-backs had the bases loaded with two outs, but pinch-hitter Conor Jackson grounded out to Guzman at shortstop.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton became the first Phillies starter to pitch eight innings in a game Saturday against the Braves. The problem is that Blanton allowed two home runs and six runs overall in a 6-2 loss. This will be Blanton's third start against the Nationals this season. He went 0-1 with a 7.84 ERA in his first two outings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen left Sunday's game against the Diamondbacks in the bottom of the fifth inning after being hit on the left ankle by a line drive off the bat of Ryan Roberts. Olsen fell to his knees, got up and bent over in pain. Head athletic trainer Lee Kuntz came to his aid, and a minute later, Olsen was taken out of the game and replaced by right-hander Garrett Mock. Olsen also fouled a ball off his right shin in the fourth.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off his best start of the season Sunday against the Atlanta Braves at Citizens Bank Park, where he allowed just one run in six innings. Unfortunately for him, the bullpen couldn't hold the lead in a 4-2 loss. Myers is 9-9 with a 4.30 ERA in 31 career appearances against the Nationals/Expos.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera, still winless, came apart at the seams in the fifth inning on Monday against the San Francisco Giants but will remain in the rotation and is expected to pitch the second game of the double header. The day after his meltdown, Cabrera had a long meeting with manager Manny Acta and pitching coach Randy St. Claire. The hard-throwing righty allowed eight runs -- three earned -- on eight hits while issuing six walks in just 4 2/3 innings. At one point in the fifth inning, Cabrera walked four consecutive batters before being yanked with the bases loaded. Cabrera would have been out of the fifth inning relatively unscathed had Josh Willingham not missed a routine fly ball with two outs in the inning.
away_pitcher_note: A very late "Plan B," Carpenter was penciled into the starting slot in Saturday's day-night doubleheader nightcap when scheduled starter, left-hander J.A. Happ, was used in emergency relief in Friday night's 12-inning win against Washington. The right-hander, who will make the start two days before his 24th birthday, made his brief big league debut last summer, pitching one scoreless inning on Aug. 27. At Triple-A Lehigh Valley this season, he had a 4.72 ERA in six starts, most recently pitching May 8.
summary: 2009-05-16 - Philadelphia Phillies @ Washington Nationals (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: This past Tuesday, Zimmermann did what he could through six innings, allowing five runs and striking out eight batters. Zimmermann pitched well for the most part, but he was hurt by two bad innings in which the Giants scored a combined five runs. In the first inning, after hitting Edgar Renteria with a pitch, Zimmermann got Sandoval to ground out, but walked Bengie Molina to set the table for Randy Winn, who hit a double to right-center field, scoring both runners. In the fifth inning, Zimmermann gave up RBI singles to Travis Ishikawa and Renteria. Renteria's single came with two outs to knock in two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Park appears to have saved his job in the rotation with consecutive quality starts. He threw six shutout innings against the Mets on May 6 and allowed two runs in six innings Tuesday against the Dodgers at Citizens Bank Park. Park has a 1.50 ERA in his last two starts. The difference? He said he has been more aggressive.

home_pitcher_note: Because of the off-day this past Thursday and Saturday's doubleheader against the Phillies, the Nationals need an extra pitcher to start on Monday against the Pirates. MLB.com has learned that left-hander Ross Detwiler will likely make the start for Washington. He is currently with Double-A Harrisburg and was scheduled to start against Reading on Saturday, but he was scratched from that outing. Detwiler, the Nationals' No. 1 pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, is having the best season of his professional career. He is 0-3 with a 2.96 ERA. Even more impressive is that Detwiler has 28 strikeouts over 27 1/3 innings and opponents are hitting .257 against him.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against St. Louis on May 13, Ohlendorf surrendered two hits and one run in six innings as the Bucs won 5-2. Ohlendorf mostly cruised against a Cardinals lineup, the Cards only run off Ohlendorf came on a Skip Schumaker home run. Ohlendorf who has relied on his sinker -- mixed things up with a four seam fastball, slider and a very effective changeup. This will be Ohlendorf's first appearance against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday, Martis improved his record to 5-0 against the Giants, the team that signed him as a Minor League free agent in 2004 then traded him to Washington two years later. Martis pitched seven innings, allowing one run on just two hits. He walked four and struck out two.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' No. 5 starter is coming off of his most encouraging two-start stretch of the year. He didn't get a win in either case, but the right-hander went six innings each against the Mets and Cardinals, allowing five runs over the 12 innings (3.75 ERA). Perhaps more importantly, he didn't walk a batter in either outing. He has never faced Washington in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta has a policy of having his young starters leave games on a positive note. In this case, on Friday against the Phillies, left-hander John Lannan left the game with a 4-2 lead after 5 2/3 innings. Right-hander Garrett Mock entered the game and gave up an RBI single to Carlos Ruiz, but Ron Villone was able to end the frame by getting Eric Bruntlett to fly out to center fielder Elijah Dukes. Nationals fans were hoping the bullpen could hold the Phillies in the seventh inning, but it didn't happen.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm didn't get the win in his last start, but it was still very encouraging. The lefty tossed seven shutout innings against the Rockies on Friday night, giving up just five hits and a walk while striking out four. It was a nice bounce-back from his previous outing when he got hit hard for seven earned runs in 5 1/3 IP against the Mets, the third time in four starts he'd given up at least four earned runs. He has not fared well against the Nationals in the past, going 0-2 with a 6.12 ERA over four starts. The Nats have hit .343 off of him in those outings.

home_pitcher_note: With Daniel Cabrera out of the rotation, right-hander Craig Stammen will get the start against the Pirates on Thursday. It will be his Major League debut. Stammen, one of the team's top pitching prospects, was 4-2 with a 1.80 ERA with Triple-A Syracuse. Stammen, 25, has been impressive because he developed a two-seam fastball during Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: An hour and 37 minute rain delay put an early end to Snell's last start against Colorado on May 16. Snell received a no-decision after two rather ineffective innings -- he gave up two runs in the first on Ryan Spilborghs' double and one more in the second on Clint Barmes' solo homer. Snell is 1-1 in his career against the Nationals with a 3.86 ERA in seven appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's struggles on the mound continued in his last start. He lasted five innings, giving up five runs on seven hits. The Phillies scored three runs in the first inning to take an early lead. It marked the fifth consecutive game Zimmermann allowed at least one run in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Hill made his long-awaited Orioles debut a memorable one last Saturday, when he worked 5 2/3 innings and picked up a 3-2  win in Kansas City. Hill allowed seven hits and two runs while fanning six and walking two. His sweeping curve impressed the Royals' hitters and Orioles manager Dave Trembley lauded the poise shown by Hill. Trembley called Hill's performance the best by a Baltimore starting pitcher this year.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals decided on Tuesday to give left-hander Ross Detwiler another big-league start on Saturday night against the Orioles. The news came a day after Detwiler pitched five quality innings in his first career start against the Pirates. After the game, Detwiler was scheduled to be sent down to Triple-A Syracuse for more seasoning, but Nationals manager Manny Acta and acting general manager Mike Rizzo had other plans. There is now a possibility that Detwiler could stay with the club as long as left-hander Scott Olsen is on the disabled list. Olsen is not scheduled to come off the DL until June 1.
away_pitcher_note: Uehara was strong through five innings in his last start at Kansas City, but wobbled in the sixth when he failed to retire any of the four hitters he faced. Uehara said he didn't think fatigue was an issue in that rocky sixth, when he left trailing, 4-3. Uehara felt he was rushing his pitches after getting ahead in some counts and will strive to make that adjustment moving forward. The Kansas City outing snapped Uehara's streak of five consecutive quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Martis rebounded from a tough start to turn in a decent outing against the Pirates, earning a no-decision and remaining unbeaten. He had problems keeping the ball down and he paid the price in the first and third innings. In the first inning, eight Pirates came to the plate and three runs scored in the process. Brandon Moss highlighted the scoring with a two-run double. Two innings later, Andy LaRoche hit a two-run homer to make it a 5-0 game. However, Martis retired the next 10 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen worked deep into the game in his last start and has now completed six innings in half of his six starts. The right-hander has also lost two straight starts and gone five outings without a victory. Bergesen has made a habit of giving up a lot of hits and stranding the runners on base, but he's also allowed four earned runs in two straight starts against Tampa Bay and New York.

home_pitcher_note: Though Maine escaped one critical jam last Tuesday against the Dodgers, loading the bases with no outs but wriggling his way out of it unscathed, he could not avoid further trouble later in the evening. Casey Blake's three-run home run was the big blow, plating the fourth and fifth runs and ensuring that Maine would not extend his three-game winning streak. But for Maine, there is good news. His next start comes against the Nationals, a team he beat three times in three tries last season with a 1.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Pirates, Lannan pitched seven innings and gave up one run on seven hits. It was his fifth quality start of the season, but he ended up with his fourth no-decision. The run Lannan gave up was scored in the fourth inning, but it wasn't entirely his fault -- it was the result of a throwing error by Adam Dunn.

home_pitcher_note: Though Hernandez again pitched quite well, holding the National League's top-ranked offense to one run in seven innings, he could not win a third straight game last Wednesday against the Dodgers. Instead, he left that game locked in a tie, ultimately taking a no-decision. Against his next opponent, the Nationals, Hernandez won twice in two starts last year, allowing a combined seven runs in 13 innings. Nationals hitters Austin Kearns, Ryan Zimmerman and Josh Willingham are a combined 23-for-58 (.397) against him.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen made his Major League debut in his last start, and it was a successful start for the most part. He lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up four runs, throwing 95 pitches, 57 of which went for strikes. Stammen didn't reach a three-ball count until the 21st batter he faced and got off to a promising start, tossing a perfect game through four innings. Catcher Josh Bard drove in two of the Nats' three runs, but it wasn't the RBIs that made Stammen comfortable on the mound -- it was having Bard behind the plate. The two formerly worked together at Triple-A Syracuse.

home_pitcher_note: Allowing three runs -- two earned -- to the Red Sox on Friday, Santana won his second consecutive start. He has now served up nine runs over his past two outings and won both of them, after allowing merely eight runs over his first seven starts combined. And his next matchup, at home against the Nationals, is far more favorable than his last one. Santana has already beaten the Nats once this year, and he was 3-0 with a 2.57 ERA against them last season.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's last start was his best one in almost a month. Having allowed 13 first-inning runs in his previous five starts, Zimmermann threw a simulated game in the bullpen before his last start, pretending it was the first inning. The exercise helped, as Zimmermann didn't allow a run in the first inning and proceeded give up just two runs in seven innings. The right-hander struck out seven batters and walked only one.

home_pitcher_note: Happ returned to the rotation on Saturday against the Yankees at Yankee Stadium and showed that he belonged. He allowed just four hits and two runs, striking out four in six innings in a game he had hoped to pitch four or five innings because of a pitch count. But Happ kept his pitch count down -- he threw 75 pitches, 50 for strikes -- to go an extra inning. The Phillies were hoping for Happ to pitch like this after he replaced Chan Ho Park in the rotation. Now, they just hope he can keep it up.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler, the Nationals' first-round pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, made his second Major League start his last time out, and it was much better than his first one. He lasted six innings and gave up one run on just one hit. The only time Detwiler was in trouble came in the third inning, when he walked three batters -- including Orioles pitcher Koji Uehara -- to load the bases. Detwiler acknowledged that he lost his focus in that inning, but the damage was minimal.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed two runs in six innings in a 5-4 victory in 11 innings over the Yankees at Yankee Stadium. He was in line for the win until Brad Lidge blew a save in the ninth. Hamels has been throwing the ball well lately. He is 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in his his last five starts. He pitched 4 1/3 scoreless innings against the Nationals on April 28. He left that game in the fifth inning after spraining his left ankle.
away_pitcher_note: Martis started for the Nationals on Sunday and didn't have his best outing, lasting six-plus innings and giving up five runs. He had problems with his command throughout the game. In fact, Martis went into the fifth inning having thrown only 50 percent of his pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Jamie Moyer is still looking for the 250th win of his career. He is winless in his last five starts, which includes Monday's loss to the Marlins at Citizens Bank Park. Moyer, who entered Monday with a 12-1 career mark against Florida, allowed four runs in six innings to take the loss. Moyer is 0-4 with a 9.62 ERA in his last five starts. Moyer allowed eight hits and four runs in six innings in a 9-8 victory over the Nationals on April 13 at Nationals Park.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, Lannan was solid for the first five innings, but a Gary Sheffield home run proved costly, and the Nationals lost to the Mets, 5-2. The game was tied at 1-1 when New York took the lead in the bottom of the sixth inning. After Luis Castillo led off with a double and Carlos Beltran walked, Sheffield came to the plate, swung at the first pitch and hit a three-run homer over the left-field wall. Lannan ended up pitching five-plus innings and gave up five runs. He walked four batters, and three of them scored.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen, making his second career start, lasted five innings and gave up three runs on seven hits his last time out. It was in the second inning when, with two outs, Ramon Martinez doubled to right to score Omir Santos for the first run. The Mets added two more runs in the next inning. Fernando Tatis and Fernando Martinez drove in a run with a hit and groundout, respectively. Stammen said his pitching mechanics were off and he had problems throwing his sinker for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum pitched like the ace he is on Tuesday, throwing eight scoreless innings against the Atlanta Braves. He allowed just five hits while striking out eight, leaving him just one 'K' short of 500 for his career. The diminutive right-hander has allowed three earned runs or less in eight of his 10 starts this season. He is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA all-time vs. the Washington Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander should be glad May is over, as he allowed five runs or more in all but one of his six starts during the month. His last time out, he allowed five runs in five innings of work on eight hits, as he took the loss against the Mets in a 7-4 contest at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson's quest for 300 career wins is back on track. Johnson allowed one run over six innings on Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves and, on his third try, secured his 299th career victory. Johnson struck out Chipper Jones three times and walked none in his 79-pitch effort. The veteran is 0-2 with an 8.50 ERA in four road starts this season and has never faced the Washington Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals' first-round pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft made his third Major League start his last time out, and it was a rude awakening for the young lefty. He lasted just four innings against the Phillies at Citizens Bank Park, in which he gave up five runs on 10 hits, including four doubles -- two by leadoff hitter Jimmy Rollins -- and a triple by Pedro Feliz.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson's quest for 300 career wins is back on track. Johnson allowed one run over six innings on Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves and, on his third try, secured his 299th career victory. Johnson struck out Chipper Jones three times and walked none in his 79-pitch effort. The veteran is 0-2 with an 8.50 ERA in four road starts this season. away_pitcher_note: Giants hitters gave Matt Cain four runs in his last start Friday against the Cardinals, and that was all he needed. In 6 1/3 innings, Cain allowed two runs (one earned) and struck out five. In a rotation that includes Tim Lincecum and Randy Johnson, it's Cain who Giants manager Bruce Bochy likes to call his "horse." Cain has pitched six or more innings in each of his 10 starts this season. He is 3-2 with a 2.36 ERA against the Washington Nationals in his brief career.
summary: 2009-06-04 - San Francisco Giants @ Washington Nationals (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Shairon Martis' troubles with his command finally cost him with his first loss of the season Saturday against the Phillies. Martis took a 3-1 lead into the third inning, but gave up two hits and a walk to load the bases and then surrendered a grand slam to Ryan Howard. Martis finished the night with two walks and one strikeout in four innings, allowing seven runs. He threw just 42 strikes in 71 pitches. In Martis' last four starts, he's walked 10 batters with just seven strikeouts, and in his last 16 innings he's allowed 17 earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Redding had his second successive rough outing Saturday against the Marlins, allowing seven earned runs on eight hits in four innings-plus. After a solid six innings in his first start, Redding now has allowed 13 earned runs in his two subsequent starts, encompassing 8 2/3 innings. Now he returns to Washington, his baseball home for the 2007 and 2008 season. He produced a 6-7 record and 5.61 ERA in 18 starts and 94 2/3 inning in Nationals Park last season. Josh Willingham has a .385 average and two home runs in 13 career at-bats against Redding.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan allowed three runs in five innings, with seven strikeouts, in Sunday's 4-2 loss to the Phillies, but it was the four walks that were bothering him after the game. Lannan has walked eight batters in his past 10 innings. "Strikeouts, I don't care about. Walks, I care about. I shouldn't be walking that many guys," he said. In his past nine starts, Lannan has a 3.23 ERA with five quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maine had another excellent start Sunday against the Marlins, allowing three hits in six scoreless innings before leaving the game because of a stomach virus. Maine now has allowed three earned runs or fewer in five of his six, most recent starts and has yielded just one run on seven hits in his last 12 innings. That includes his last start against the Nationals, in which he allowed a run on four hits in six innings  en route to his fourth victory. Maine has a 6-2 record and 4.04 ERA in 10 career starts against the Nationals  He never has pitched in Nationals Park.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander Craig Stammen started for the Nationals on Tuesday and kept them in the game against the Giants. He lasted six innings and gave up five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits. He got off to a slow start by giving up a first-inning home run to leadoff hitter Aaron Rowand. After giving up a one-out double to Randy Winn in the same inning, Stammen retired 11 straight batters.
away_pitcher_note: If  not for a bullpen meltdown Monday, Hernandez would have entered this start with a 5-1 record and this additional glitter on his 2009 resume: The Mets would have won five of his six most recent starts. He's not complaining. He's on something of a roll, and now he faces an opponent he beat May 26 in a complete game. Hernandez allowed nine hits and a walk but only one run in that victory against the Nationals. His ERA in 35 innings on the road is 4.89. Right-handed hitters are batting .322 against him; left-handed hitters are batting .289. Austin Kearns is batting .444 with two home runs in 27 career at-bats against Hernandez.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler gets the start, replacing Jordan Zimmerman, who was originally slated to be on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto's streak of eight straight games of at least seven innings pitched ended vs. the Cardinals on Wednesday but he was more than good enough to earn a 9-3 win for the Reds. The 23-year-old right-hander pitched 6 1/3 innings and gave up one earned run and seven hits with no walks and three strikeouts. Once again he eliminated walks and lowered his pitch total by being aggressive and throwing strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Despite spotty control Friday night against the Mets, Martis' final line was adequate -- a three-hit, one-run no-decision. His four walks and general carefulness helped contribute to a 110-pitch count that ousted the hurler after just five innings. Martis struck out one batter, his 27th all year, making his walk to strikeout ratio 1:1 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Harang pitched an eight-inning complete game vs. the Cardinals but as good as he was, Chris Carpenter was better in his own complete game as the Reds were handed a 3-1 loss on Thursday at Busch Stadium. Harang gave up three earned runs and eight hits with two walks, four strikeouts and induced four inning-ending double plays. But he could not resist challenging Albert Pujols, who drove in all three runs with a two-run homer and a RBI double.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan pitched the game of his career Saturday against the Mets. It was his first career complete game, and if not for an Elijah Dukes error in right field, Lannan would have tossed a shutout. Inducing a franchise-high five double plays, Lannan neutralized some early control issues before he could get into any trouble. He struck out two batters and let his defense make plays behind him. Despite the losing record, Lannan has been the Nationals' most consistent pitcher. In his past 10 starts, he has given up more than three earned runs just once.
away_pitcher_note: Owings needed 33 pitches to get through the first inning on Friday night against the Cubs, walking three -- including Mike Fontenot with the bases loaded to force home Chicago's first run. He later allowed a solo home run by pitcher Carlos Zambrano. Owings lasted six innings, surrendering two runs on five hits while walking three and striking out six. In a 5-2 loss to the Brewers on Sunday, Owings pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed five earned runs on eight hits, with three walks and five strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: At age 25, Garza seems to be maturing on the mound, where he has experienced problems controlling his emotions in the past. In the past, Garza has lacked steadiness, but he has been Mr. Consistency in 2009, with eight quality starts in 12 outings. Garza went just five innings on Sunday against the Yankees, but he allowed only two hits while taking a no-decision. Garza will be making his first career start against the Nationals; he is 10-5 with a 3.06 ERA in 22 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen got himself into trouble right away on Sunday against the Mets, walking leadoff hitter Alex Cora, and he proceeded to give up five first-inning runs on three hits, two walks and two wild pitches. "I just didn't have any sink on my fastball," Stammen said. "I didn't make good pitches; anybody can hit those." The Nationals have placed an emphasis on their young pitchers throwing strikes, but Stammen deviated from that plan. On a positive note, he did pitch through the fifth inning without giving up any additional runs.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine allowed five earned runs -- all of which came through four Yankees homers -- in taking his sixth loss of the season Monday night. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. The right-hander's mantra is to dispatch of hitters one way or the other in three pitches, which allows him to get deeper into the games and save the bullpen. Sonnanstine will be making his first career start against the Nationals; he is 11-9 with a 5.07 ERA in 29 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann was scheduled to pitch against the Reds on Tuesday, but he was scratched because of right elbow fatigue. Zimmermann started having problems with his elbow during a bullpen session last Saturday, two days after pitching against the Giants. The team doesn't believe the injury is serious even though Zimmermann said he felt some pain in the elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Shields admitted he didn't have his best stuff on Tuesday, but he battled for 6 1/3 innings against the Angels and gave his team another good opportunity to win. He mostly scattered 10 hits, but the defense committed two errors that led to two runs in the first inning that put him in an early hole. Shields fell to 4-2 at home this season. The Rays will look for him to pitch deep again in this game vs. Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler picked up his third loss Tuesday in a six-inning five hit, three-run outing at Nationals Park. Detwiler showed the ability to miss bats, striking out six Reds, but his three walks were costly as two of those runners eventually scored. "The entire year it's been the same thing -- every time I walk people, they end up scoring," Detwiler said after the game.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia held the Red Sox to one run through seven innings on Thursday before it came unraveled in the eighth inning at Fenway Park, as he pushed to a season-high 123 pitches. Boston came back against Alfredo Aceves and tagged Sabathia with his first loss in seven starts, a four-run heartbreaker that left New York 0-8 vs. Boston this season. The left-handed ace faced the Nationals once last season on Aug. 8, hurling a complete-game shutout for the Brewers while allowing five hits and striking out nine with a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Martis' changeup and slider were working Wednesday against the Reds. Throwing 63 percent strikes, Martis was only at 81 pitches when he was taken out in favor of a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the seventh inning. His final line: seven innings, three hits, two runs, two walks, one strikeout and a no-decision. The runs came in the second inning when Jay Bruce tagged a high fastball for a two-run home run. "I threw more strikes, was aggressive, kept the ball down," Martis said. "Just one pitch I left up."

home_pitcher_note: This is a pivotal start for Wang, as the Yankees are allowing him one more try to prove that he belongs in a big league rotation. They didn't think much of his last effort, when he lasted only 2 2/3 innings on Wednesday at Fenway Park and took the loss, allowing four runs on six hits while walking three and striking out three. The problems have varied, but in basic terms, pitching coach Dave Eiland is befuddled that Wang's arm slot keeps changing and he isn't able to take his good bullpen sessions out to the mound. Wang has not faced Washington since 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Thursday was another solid start for Lannan, who went six innings, allowing five hits and two runs (one earned) against Cincinnati. Lannan trailed, 2-0, upon exiting the game, but the Nationals took the lead in the eighth inning to get him off the hook. It was the first of five Lannan no-decisions that the Nationals have won this season. "John is just doing what he did last year, going out every five days, giving us a chance to win," manager Manny Acta said.

home_pitcher_note: Usually, when a pitcher allows just one hit in a start, it means he pitched a great game. But not for Chamberlain in his last outing, when he surrendered one hit -- but five walks and two hit batsmen -- in just four innings against the Mets on Friday. Chamberlain gave up just two runs, but had to exit prematurely after throwing 100 pitches (52 strikes).
away_pitcher_note: Stammen left with a lead for the first time in his fifth Major League start Friday at Tampa Bay. That lead didn't last long as reliever Joel Hanrahan allowed a run-scoring double to tie the game, preventing Stammen from earning his first Major League victory. Still, it was the 25-year-old's best outing with the Nationals. He allowed two earned runs and struck out a career-best five. His inexperience showed, though, as he walked a career-worst three batters and had difficulty keeping Tampa Bay's aggressive baserunners close to the bag.

home_pitcher_note: After he was scratched from a start because of mild elbow soreness, the rookie came off his nine-day layoff with five strong innings Saturday against the Rays at Tropicana Field. He struck out six and allowed one run (on a Carlos Pena homer). The only drawback was his pitch count. Despite only allowing two walks, he reached 92 pitches through five innings and his day was done. He left with the lead, though, and the important thing for Washington was his elbow appeared to be fine. This is his first career appearance against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Tallet turned in his shortest outing as a starter since being moved out of the bullpen. The left-hander allowed eight runs on 10 hits over just 3 1/3 innings in an Interleague loss to the Marlins. Prior to that abbreviated performance, Tallet had logged at least six innings in eight consecutive starts. Tallet's poor showing came after he fashioned seven shutout innings en route to a victory over the Rangers on the road on June 9. In 12 turns as a starter this year, Tallet has gone 4-4 with a 4.73 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler fought hard against the Rays on Sunday, and the rookie pitched well until unraveling in the sixth. He said he didn't have command of his fastball, and it showed with his five walks. But he forced several double plays and battled through the top-scoring lineup in baseball, enough to draw praise from manager Manny Acta and maybe earn a few more starts in the big leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil, selected 38th overall in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, was summoned from Triple-A Las Vegas to take the place of ace Roy Halladay, who landed on the disabled list with a strained right groin on Thursday. Since being optioned back to Vegas on May 22, Cecil posted a 4.26 ERA over five Minor League starts, striking out 23 and walking 11 over 31 2/3 innings. The 22-year-old lefty's last start for the Jays came on May 20, when he allowed eight runs on 11 hits, including five home runs, over 4 2/3 innings of a loss at Boston. Prior to that outing, Cecil had gone 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA in his first three Major League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Martis had his sixth quality start of the season on Tuesday against the Yankees. He lasted six innings, gave up two runs -- one earned -- on four hits and five walks. Martis acknowledged that he walked that many batters because he was trying to pitch around great hitters such as Mark Teixeira, Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez and Jorge Posada. With a small-playing ballpark like Yankee Stadium, Martis did not want to give up the long ball.
away_pitcher_note: Romero is coming off a strong outing, in which he picked up a no-decision on the road against the Phillies on Friday. In seven innings, the left-handed rookie gave up three runs on six hits in his last start and finished with two walks and a career-high nine strikeouts. Romero also logged a career high in pitches with 109. Over his last three starts, Romero has gone 1-1 with a 3.10 ERA, tallying 20 strikeouts against six walks in 20 1/3 innings. That comes after a two-start stretch during which the lefty went 0-2 with a 9.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nationals left-hander John Lannan, who rooted for the Yankees while growing up on Long Beach, N.Y., admitted that he had to find a way to control his emotions when he faced his hometown team at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday. Lannan controlled his emotions, all right. The lefty lasted 8 1/3 innings, as the Nationals defeated the Yankees, 3-2, in front of 46,052 fans at Yankee Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Penny continues to be a source of consistency in the Red Sox rotation. His future with Boston remains to be seen, but in the interim, the 31-year-old right-hander is improving with every start. One week after holding the Yankees scoreless over six frames, Penny fired five impressive innings of one-run ball against the Marlins on Wednesday at Fenway Park. He has dominated the Montreal/Washington franchise in his career, sporting a 12-5 record and 2.54 ERA in 20 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Win No. 1 was quite impressive for Stammen, who went into Yankee Stadium last week and shut out the Bronx Bombers in 6 1/3 innings. A control pitcher, Stammen did not walk a batter and struck out two. Manager Manny Acta has mentioned that with the Nationals defense improving, a pitcher like Stammen can throw his sinker with more confidence. As he showed Thursday in New York, Stammen is at his best when he's pitching to contact, as long as that sinkerball is down in the zone.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a stretch in which he became the first lefty in Red Sox history to strike out 10 or more batters in three straight starts, Lester wasn't nearly as effective last Thursday against the Marlins at Fenway Park. Florida peppered the 25-year-old southpaw with eight hits over five-plus frames, including a pair of second-inning home runs by Ronny Paulino and Dan Uggla.
