Lester shined in one previous outing against the Nationals, fanning 10 over six innings of one-run ball in the third start of his Major League career.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's high pitch count of 106 led to an exit after 5 2/3 innnings against Toronto Friday. But Zimmermann was solid in that time, giving up five hits and one run in a no-decision. Being a strikeout pitcher (the right-hander leads NL rookies with 63 this season), he is prone to high pitch counts. Zimmermann has pitched more than six innings just once in 11 starts. After a rough May, he is sporting a 2.16 ERA in three June starts.
away_pitcher_note: Smoltz makes his long-awaited Red Sox debut after spending the first 20 seasons of his Major League career in Atlanta. The 42-year-old right-hander underwent a deliberate rehabilitation program with Boston following shoulder surgery last June. A 210-game winner and likely future Hall of Famer, Smoltz is 21-12 lifetime with a 2.55 ERA in 68 appearances against the Montreal/Washington franchise.

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen pitched six scoreless innings against the Phillies before tiring and giving up four runs in the seventh. The Orioles came back to win and get him off the hook, so Bergesen still hasn't lost since May 19. He's 3-0 in his last five starts with a 2.35 ERA, allowing just 33 baserunners in 38 1/3 innings. He didn't walk a batter in his last start, and has not issued a walk in four of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his seventh start, Detwiler was oh-so-close to earning his first career win, but the bullpen could not hold the two-run lead the Nationals had when the southpaw exited the game Saturday's game against the Blue Jays. But as Detwiler said after the game, "It's a win for the team, so you can't go wrong with that." Detwiler was integral in that win, tossing seven innings, allowing six hits and two runs against Toronto. He was locating his fastball and changeup and only walked one batter after giving away five free passes the previous game.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie carried a road record of 1-3 with a 8.53 ERA into his last start in Philadelphia, but he was brilliant in winning a 2-1 pitchers' duel, his first win since May 25. He gave up just three hits and two walks in seven innings. Guthrie did not allow a runner to reach second base after giving up a leadoff homer to Greg Dobbs in the second inning.
away_pitcher_note: Martis didn't have his best stuff on Sunday against the Blue Jays, throwing 38 pitches and allowing four runs in the first inning. After getting two quick outs, thanks to a double-play ball hit by Aaron Hill, Martis was unable to retire the next five hitters. Alex Rios and Lyle Overbay each drove in two runs, with a double and single, respectively. In the second inning, Martis gave up another run when Vernon Wells doubled near the left-field line to drive in Marco Scutaro. Martis lasted five innings and gave up six runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Koji Uehara was scheduled to make this start, but the Orioles scratched him due to fatigue in his pitching elbow and will send him to the disabled list for the second time this season. David Hernandez, who acquitted himself well in his first stint with the parent club, was pulled after four scoreless innings in his last start for Triple-A Norfolk just in case of this development.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan wasn't as good as he was against the Yankees at Yankee Stadium last week. He lasted 6 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on nine hits. He left the game against Boston because he threw 109 pitches. Lannan relied heavily on his changeup to get hitters out. He figured the Red Sox would be waiting on the fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco looked like the 2008 version of himself in his last start. The right-hander won his second consecutive start after allowing just two runs none earned on seven hits over seven innings while striking out seven and walking just one Orioles hitter, Aubrey Huff.  The 26-year-old has pitched well since he returned to the Majors on June 7th. Nolasco looks to continue his success against the Nationals after beating them on Opening Day.
away_pitcher_note: The team has decided that Craig Stammen, 25, will be a reliever once Olsen is activated from the disabled list on Monday. Olsen has missed a little over a month because of a left shoulder injury. Manager Manny Acta said Olsen is strong enough to throw 100 pitches against the Marlins on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: West won his third game of the season after throwing six shutout innings against the Orioles in his last start. The left-hander allowed just four hits while walking three and striking out two. The 22-year-old West allowed a runner to reach in each of his six innings but was able to get out of jams all night by remaining calm and making his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Following an impressive outing in Yankee Stadium, Stammen struggled against the Red Sox at Nationals Park, giving up six runs in 5 1/3 innings. It didn't help that he didn't throw enough first-pitch strikes.
summary: 2009-06-30 - Washington Nationals @ Florida Marlins (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Considering the high standards Johnson has set for himself this season, his no-decision against the Rays on Friday wasn't exactly on par. But he still gave up just three runs in six innings to get his 14th quality start and left the game tied. The 25-year-old right-hander was hurt when he threw 27 pitches in the first inning and was dealing with a high pitch count his entire outing. Johnson, who gave up seven hits and walked three while striking out six, left after throwing 105 pitches (66 strikes). It was just the fourth time in 16 starts this year that Johnson didn't go more than six innings. For his career, he is 4-0 with a 3.49 ERA in seven appearances (six starts) against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann gave up one run in seven innings against the Red Sox on Thursday. His only blemish against Boston came in the sixth inning, when he allowed a sacrifice fly to David Ortiz. It was Zimmermann's first win since April 26 against the Mets at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: Last Friday, the game between the Nationals and Orioles was tied at 1 after three innings, but things started to unravel for Detwiler in the fourth. With a runner on first, Nolan Reimold doubled to left fielder Josh Willingham, who didn't field the ball cleanly and allowed Aubrey Huff to score all the way from first base to give Baltimore a 2-1 lead. After Luke Scott singled, Melvin Mora made it a two-run game when he singled to right field to drive in Reimold. Detwiler ended up pitching five-plus innings, giving up five runs on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami didn't last long on Wednesday against the Yankees, but it wasn't because of the way he was pitching. The 33-year-old righty was struck on the right side of the base of his neck by a Joba Chamberlain line drive in the third inning. He ended up with a contusion and was forced out of the game. Before suffering the injury, Kawakami had retired all nine Yankees he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan continues to show he is the leader of the Washington rotation. He picked up his fifth straight quality start and helped the Nationals defeat the Orioles, 5-3, at Camden Yards on Sunday afternoon. Lannan pitched 7 1/3 innings and gave up three runs on six hits. Early on, Lannan had problems with his two-seam fastball, and it showed in the second inning. After Nolan Reimold walked, Luke Scott doubled to put runners on second and third. Oscar Salazar then singled to left to send Reimold home and give Baltimore a 1-0 lead. But in typical Lannan fashion, he battled back and was able to get out of the inning. Matt Wieters then hit into a double play, and Robert Andino grounded out. Lannan cruised until the eighth inning, when he gave up a pair of hits.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson may have had the flu while pitching on Sunday against the Red Sox, but he made the Boston hitters feel just as sick. Hanson fought through his illness to throw six scoreless innings of two-hit ball. On a hot, muggy day at Turner Field, Hanson threw 97 pitches despite barely feeling well enough to start. For the second straight outing, Hanson silenced a potent AL East lineup. The Braves rookie shut out the Yankees on June 23 and has now thrown 20 consecutive scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen returned from injury in top form Monday, throwing seven quality innings against his old team, the Marlins. The left-hander, who had been on the disabled list since May with left shoulder tendinitis, held Florida to two runs on six hits while striking out seven and walking none. Despite a solid pitching performance, Olsen took a no-decision but showed he was fully recovered from his shoulder injury.
away_pitcher_note: After looking shaky in two of his previous three starts, Lowe righted the ship against the Phillies on Tuesday. He went six innings, allowing two runs on seven hits. When he left after the sixth inning, he was in line for his eighth win of the season but saw the Atlanta bullpen surrender the lead.

home_pitcher_note: The efficiency of Marquis' 3-0 shutout of the Dodgers on Tuesday night was stunning. He threw strikes on 66 of his 86 pitches, didn't walk anyone and held the Dodgers to two hits. He's had strong games pitching without his secondary pitches, like an 8 2/3-inning beating of the Pirates earlier in the season at Coors. But against the Dodgers, he had a cutter to go with the sinker. Marquis will meet the Nationals at Coors, where he is 4-2 with a 4.34 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Through five innings against the Marlins on Tuesday, Stammen was on his game, giving up one unearned run on three hits and retiring eight of nine batters at one point. But sporting a 5-1 lead in the sixth, the 25-year-old rookie gave up a run on a wild pitch, then allowed a two-run homer to Hanley Ramirez to make it a one-run game. After that, a bullpen that came in with the most losses and highest ERA in the big leagues allowed the Marlins to take the lead and gave him a no-decision. Stammen finished having allowed four runs (three earned) on six hits with no walks and two strikeouts while throwing 73 pitches (47 strikes). This will be his first career appearance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel has set career highs for innings pitched in a game in his last two starts -- 7 1/3 innings in a win over the Athletics, and an eight-inning complete game in a 1-0 loss to the Dodgers on Wednesday afternoon. Hammel's new two-seam fastball gives him a pitch low in the zone. He has had more flyballs than groundballs in the last two starts and that could be dangerous at Coors, but much of the contact has been weak.
away_pitcher_note: As has been the case since close to the start of June, Zimmermann was solid against the Marlins on Wednesday, but he didn't end up with a win to show for it. The 23-year-old rookie gave up just two runs on six hits with six strikeouts and one walk before leaving with 100 pitches under his belt through six innings -- right before a 19-minute rain delay. Zimmermann left with a 2-1 lead, but the Major Leagues' worst bullpen -- statistically -- allowed Florida to come back in an eventual loss. Zimmermann sports a 2.12 ERA since the start of June, but he only has one win. This will be his first career appearance against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is riding a career-high three-game winning streak and arguably had his finest outing of the season as he threw eight shutout innings of four-hit ball with four walks and six strikeouts in a 5-0 win over the D-backs. Arizona didn't have a player reach second base until the sixth inning and had only three players overall accomplish such a feat. De La Rosa showed the tantalizing promise he always had as he had complete command of all four of pitches -- fastball, slider, curveball and change. In his last six starts, De La Rosa is 5-1 with a 4.67 ERA after beginning April and May winless.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler started against the Braves on Friday and lasted 3 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on 10 hits. He said he had a good bullpen session before the game. By the time the game started, however, it was clear to Detwiler that he had a problem with his release point. Most of his pitches were up in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: MacDougal may not be used. When the game resumes in the bottom of the 11th inning tied at 10-10, the Nationals will have a runner on first with one out and can win the game. However, if the game continues into the 12th, MacDougal will take the mound. Manager Manny Acta said that he will have six of seven relievers available, with the exception being Julian Tavarez.
away_pitcher_note: LaTroy Hawkins was on the mound for the Astros when their May 5 game against Washington was halted by rain and the Astros see fit for him to continue his outing when the game resumes. Pitchers Roy Oswalt, Chris Sampson and Tim Byrdak are not eligible to pitch because they were used and removed from the game on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz gave up nine eights and eight runs in his most recent start, last Saturday against the Giants. He was cruising through 4 2/3 innings before unraveling quickly and losing for the second time in three starts. He hasn't won a game as a starter since back-to-back wins on April 21 and 26. Ortiz is 11-6 with a 3.11 ERA in 18 career starts against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan ended up being the winning pitcher on Saturday, yielding three runs on nine hits over eight innings against the Braves. At 6-5, it's the first time since Aug. 1, 2007, that Lannan has a record over .500 during the season. The first run scored in the third inning when Nate McLouth singled up the middle to drive in Brooks Conrad. In the sixth, Chipper Jones and Garret Anderson had RBI singles, but Lannan was able to get out of the inning when Yunel Escobar hit into a double play.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has regained his dominating form, going 3-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his past five starts. He threw a two-hitter on June 29 at San Diego and allowed one run on a wild pitch, then he held the Giants to three hits and one run in his last start, on Sunday in San Francisco. Oswalt is 3-1 with a 2.97 ERA in 11 career games (nine starts) against the Nationals. He allowed four runs on four hits in five innings in Washington, D.C., on May 5 in a game that was postponed because of inclement weather.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen came within one out of pitching the first complete game of his career and helped the Nationals defeat the Braves, 5-3, at Nationals Park on Sunday. Olsen gave up three runs on eight hits in 8 2/3 innings. He also went 2-for-3 and drove in a run. With two outs in the ninth inning, the Braves' Nate McLouth hit a two-run homer that knocked Olsen from the game after 116 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton was masterful once again against the Pirates. In his fourth start of year against Pittsburgh, Hampton allowed one run on three hits and struck out three over seven innings, improving to 4-0 with a 1.00 ERA versus the Bucs this season. Hampton as faced the Washington franchise 18 times in his career, the majority of his appearances coming when the organization was in Montreal. Since the move to the nation's capital in 2005, Hampton is 1-0 with a 2.37 ERA in three starts. His last start against the Nationals came last year. He gave up five runs (four earned) on eight hits and struck out five over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Despite pitching in a hitter's park such as Coors Field, Stammen more than held his own as he used his sinker to hold the Rockies to one run in a career-high seven innings. Unfortunately, he was the hard-luck loser as he was outpitched by All-Star Jason Marquis in a 1-0 loss. Stammen has only two quality starts in nine outings this season, but both have come in his last four starts. As a result, he has lowered his ERA by almost a full run (from 5.86 on June 12 to 4.88). He will be making his start against the Astros Saturday at Minute Maid Park -- another hitter's paradise.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler turned in another quality outing last time out against the Pirates but lost for the first time in his last five outings. The right-hander went 6 1/3 innings on Tuesday, allowing four runs on three hits and striking out four. After giving up a two-run home run in the third inning, he promptly sat down the next 10 Pirates batters in order. He faced Washington once this season, receiving a no-decision after allowing two runs on eight hits and striking out five in five innings. He is 2-4 with a 5.68 ERA in 13 career games against the Nationals, including eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's run of five good-to-great starts came to an end in his last outing against the Rockies on Tuesday. The rookie had compiled a 1-1 record with a 2.12 ERA during that span but gave four runs, two earned, on seven hits with four walks in four innings against Colorado. Zimmermann showed a lack of command and couldn't locate his pitches. He has never faced the Astros, which he will face in the final game before the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: In his final outing before the break, against the Astros, Lannan had one of his worst starts of the season. He gave up five runs on 11 hits over five-plus innings. He was staked to a 4-2 lead, but things started to unravel in the sixth. After Ivan Rodriguez led off with a double, Geoff Blum singled off the glove of shortstop Cristian Guzman to put runners on first and third. Jeff Keppinger followed and tripled to right-center field to drive in Rodriguez and Blum and tie the score at 4.
away_pitcher_note: Harden was not sharp in his last start before the break. Against the Cardinals, he gave up four runs on seven hits and four walks over five innings. Among the hits were Albert Pujols' 32nd home run. The problem was both command and location, and that's not going to get it done. Harden was pitching on extra rest, too. Maybe being on the road will be better. He has not won at Wrigley Field since May 12, a span of five starts, and has an 8.63 ERA in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Scott Olsen was scratched from this start, so Stammen will get the nod instead. Stammen seems to finally be "getting it" as a Major League pitcher. Following a hard-luck loss in which he allowed just one run in seven innings at Coors Field, the rookie right-hander pitched a complete game at Houston for his second victory of the season. Stammen scattered nine hits and walked one while allowing two runs to the Astros in a 13-2 blowout. Stammen has gone deep into games recently because of his ability to throw his sinker for strikes early in the count.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano picked up his first win since June 5 in his last start, July 12 against the Cardinals. Big Z gave up three runs on five hits and two walks over six innings while striking out seven. He also hit his third homer of the year, and 19th of his career. Zambrano is 1-1 with a 1.86 ERA in three July starts.

home_pitcher_note: Since the start of June, Zimmermann has pitched like a steady, middle-of-the-rotation pitcher, with a 2.70 ERA in seven starts. The Nationals have struggled to give him run support. though, as he has only won once during that time. His most recent outing was a perfect example. Zimmermann gave up one run through six innings against the Astros, but the Nationals offense couldn't muster a run. In the seventh, he broke down a bit and gave up three runs before being pulled with one out.
away_pitcher_note: Wells will sub for All-Star Ted Lilly, who is bothered by inflammation in his left knee. Wells has definitely provided a huge boost to the team this year. The rookie is coming off a loss to the Braves on July 12 in which he gave up four runs over seven innings. The four runs matched his season high, done once before. He's 2-1 with a 3.15 ERA in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Mock struggled as a reliever for the Nationals before being sent down to the Minors in mid-May. Mock had a 5-1 record and 2.56 ERA in eight starts for Triple-A Syracuse. He will be making his first Major League start of the season, after being promoted in favor of struggling rookie Ross Detwiler.
away_pitcher_note: Hart will be recalled for the series finale. The right-hander was optioned to the Minor Leagues after his start July 8 so he could get a start in during All-Star week. For Class A Peoria on Monday, Hart went four-plus innings. He's made one start, stepping in July 8 against the Braves. In that game, he gave up one run on four hits and five walks over five innings. Obviously, he's got to reduce the number of walks.

home_pitcher_note: Martin will step on a big league mound for the first time in his nine-year professional career Monday against the Mets. In Triple-A this season, the 26-year-old has been the Syracuse Chiefs' most consistent starter, going 8-3 with a 2.66 ERA in 15 starts. Martin throws his fastball in the mid to high 80's and also offers a cutter and a changeup. His command is what has made him successful in Triple-A this season, as he's struck out 66 batters compared to 10 walks issued.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez has lost his last four starts, and the Mets have lost his last six. But before he allowed seven and eight runs in his two most recent games, he produced a 3.00 ERA in three successive starts. He pitched merely seven innings total in his July losses to the Phillies and Dodgers, allowing 21 hits and eight walks. But his next opponent is the team he has beaten twice in two starts this season. Hernandez pitched the Mets' only complete game against the Nationals at Citi Field on May 26, allowing one run. Twelve days later, he pitched seven scoreless innings against them. Ronnie Belliard, Corey Patterson, Austin Kearns, Josh Willingham and Cristian Guzman have a composite .442 average in 95 at-bats against Hernandez.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan continues to give the Nationals one good performance after another, but a lack of run support has led to his sub-.500 record. Again, Lannan threw a quality start last Thursday against the Cubs, hurling 6 2/3 innings and giving up three runs (two earned). But the Nationals could only spot him one run during that time, and the bullpen made sure that the Nats offense couldn't come back. Lannan has allowed three earned runs in 15 of his last 17 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Given to dramatic swings in performance, Perez produced a middle-of-the-road start in his most recent appearance Thursday in Atlanta. His six innings qualified as a quality start -- for those who accept that ultra-forgiving category. He allowed three runs, nine baserunners, four on walks, and bases-empty home runs to two successive batters. Two of the critical hits were produced by left-handed hitters. Those figures might have resulted in a victory, but the Mets scored three, so they resulted in Perez's third no-decision in seven starts. Now he faces an opponent that has troubled him over the years. Since the beginning of the 2006 season, Perez has started eight games against the Nationals, winning twice, losing four times, producing a 7.53 ERA and allowing 72 baserunners in 40 2/3 innings. Austin Kearns has a .345 average and four home runs in 29 career at-bats against Perez.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen posted his third straight quality start on Friday against the Cubs, but he absorbed the loss. A couple of mistakes did in the rookie right-hander. With two on and two out in the second inning, he allowed Cubs pitcher Carlos Zambrano to belt a two-run double down the right-field line. An inning later, again with two outs, he threw a sinker that didn't sink to Aramis Ramirez, who deposited it into the bleachers for a solo home run. Stammen got through six innings, giving up those three runs while striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was absolutely ineffective Friday night against the Braves. "I don't think I hit a spot all night," he said. "I feel bad for the people who had to play behind me. It was embarrassing." He lost for the third time in five starts, allowing the nine runs on nine hits, two of them home runs, and a walk. Pelfrey had allowed merely six home runs in his first 100 2/3 innings this season, then two in a three-batter sequence. He allowed three runs in two innings and four in another. Now he faces the Nationals, a team he beat once this season -- two runs in 5 2/3 innings at Citi Field on April 25. He had a 2-3 record and 3.68 ERA against them before this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jordan Zimmermann was scheduled to pitch against the Cardinals on Thursday, but he has right elbow discomfort. Right-hander Collin Balester will get the nod instead. Balester, 23, went 6-4 with a 3.38 ERA in his last 12 starts with Syracuse. Over that period he posted 41 strikeouts and a .274 opponent's batting average in 69 1/3 innings. Overall, he went 7-9 with a 4.35 ERA in 19 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was a tough-luck loser on Saturday night when he gave up two runs and five hits in seven innings but fell to Arizona ace Dan Haren. Wainwright pitched well, giving up his first run on a bloop single to center and his second on a wind-aided home run to the right-field corner. The workhorse has gone at least seven innings in five straight starts and the Cardinals are 3-2 in that span. He has not faced Washington this year.
summary: 2009-07-23 - St. Louis Cardinals @ Washington Nationals (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Mock came back from the Minor Leagues with a reputation of being a solid starter with Triple-A Syracuse, going 5-1 with a 2.65 ERA. Against the Cubs on Sunday, he looked like the same pitcher who was hit hard as a reliever. Mock lasted 3 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs -- only four of which were earned.
away_pitcher_note: Latos, a 6-foot-6, 225-pound 21-year-old rookie, was impressive in his Major League debut against the Rockies on Sunday. He went four innings, allowing two runs on three hits. He walked one and struck out four. He threw 75 pitches, 51 for strikes. He gave up a home run to Ian Stewart on a 3-2 pitch, but was happy with the rest of his performance. Padres manager Bud Black said that Latos would be monitored closely as to his pitch count and innings pitched. His fastball was in the mid-to-upper 90s on Sunday. Latos said he was very nervous, but hopes to be more at ease when he takes the mound for his second start against the Nationals. He was the fifth-youngest Padre to make his Major League debut in team history.

home_pitcher_note: After eight-plus seasons in the Minor Leagues, Martin made his Major League debut on Monday night, and it was a rough one as the Nationals lost to the Mets, 6-2, at Nationals Park. Martin went just four innings and gave up five runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer tossed six innings in his second start for the Padres this season, a 3-2 loss to the Marlins at PETCO Park. He allowed one run on three hits with two walks and four strikeouts. Padres manager Bud Black said Stauffer wasn't as "crisp" as in his first start of the season but that he showed a strong will to battle through. The only run Stauffer allowed was a homer to shortstop Hanley Ramirez in the first inning. Black said he was especially impressed with Stauffer's use of his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Call Lannan the stopper. On Tuesday night, he helped the Nationals break their six-game losing streak by pitching a complete-game shutout in a 4-0 victory over the Mets at Nationals Park. Lannan joined Pedro Astacio (Aug. 15, 2006) and John Patterson (Aug. 4, 2005) as the only Nationals hurlers to hold opponents scoreless in a complete-game win. It was Lannan's second complete game of the season. The first one also came against the Mets on June 6 at Nationals Park.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Gaudin was his own worst critic after his last start, a 3-2 loss to the Marlins at PETCO Park. "I didn't have great stuff," he said. "I was average." He allowed three runs on nine hits in six innings for a quality start, an outing of six innings with three or fewer earned runs. Gaudin struck out three and walked only two, controlling what had been his Achilles' heel. Padres manager Bud Black said Gaudin "hung in there," avoiding stressful situations effectively and working his way out of several jams.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan gave up four home runs in 3 1/3 innings to get a no-decision against the Pirates in his last start. It was his shortest outing of the season and he trailed 5-2 upon leaving. The Brewers eventually took the lead, but lost, 8-7. Suppan has yet to face Washington this year, but is 3-4 with a 3.32 ERA in 10 starts against the franchise in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen put up his fourth consecutive quality start, and it helped the Nationals defeat the Mets, 3-1, at Nationals Park on Wednesday night. Stammen (3-5) was perfect through the first four innings, but David Wright broke it up in the fifth with a single to center.

home_pitcher_note: Even with Triple-A starter Tim Dillard in the fold after a Sunday promotion from Nashville, the Brewers are giving the start to Villanueva, who has made his last 81 appearances in relief since last May and has struggled over the past six weeks. Villanueva has been excellent against the Nationals in his career, going 2-0 with a 1.46 ERA in five appearances, all in relief. He has allowed nine earned runs in his last three outings at home, spanning just 1 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Balester started for Washington on Thursday night against the Cardinals and gave up three runs -- two earned -- in three-plus innings. The defense behind Balester ended up hurting him in a 4-1 loss. He left the game because of a rain delay.

home_pitcher_note: Parra practiced damage control on Friday against Atlanta, when he worked around 13 baserunners (10 hits and three walks) in five innings, but limited the Braves to four runs. Still, it was a step back from his first two starts after returning from a demotion to the Minors. In those games, Parra limited the Cardinals and Reds to one earned run and eight hits in 13 innings of work. He didn't receive a decision in either of his two starts against the Nationals last season.
away_pitcher_note: It appeared that Mock wasn't ready to pitch against the Padres on Friday night at Nationals Park. He has yet to show that he is the type of starter that he was at Triple-A Syracuse. He gave up five runs -- three earned -- in 5 1/3 innings and committed an error in the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo delivered just what the manager ordered on Saturday, when he pitched 7 1/3 innings and drove in the go-ahead run in the Brewers' 4-0 win over phenom Tommy Hanson and the Braves at Miller Park. It was Gallardo's first win since June 26 -- he had three losses and a no-decision in the interim, and the Brewers lost all four games -- and his third win in which he accounted for the game-winning RBI. Gallardo beat Randy Johnson and the Giants with a three-run home run in his season debut, belted a home run in a 1-0 win over Ian Snell and the Pirates on April 29 and then singled off Hanson to snap a scoreless tie in the fifth inning on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Martin threw two scoreless innings before rain intervened on his last outing Saturday against the Padres. After a three-hour, 11-minute delay, Martin did not resume pitching. He did however take his at-bat following the delay. Martin drew a 10-pitch walk, which keyed a four-run, two-out rally in the Nationals' win. After throwing four innings in his debut, Martin has pitched just six innings in his two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf kept his pitch count low -- something he's struggled to do all year -- in his last start, but without his command, it didn't matter all that much. Ohlendorf struggled with his location in allowing six hits (five for extra bases) and two earned runs in six innings. Still, he showed impressive poise in getting out of a number of jams. Ohlendorf is still looking for some consistency with his pitches, especially his slider, as it has been rare that he has command of all his pitches on the same night.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan's ERA continued to creep lower with his eight-inning, one-run outing on Sunday against the Padres. He was unable to earn the victory, as closer Mike MacDougal blew the save in the ninth. Lannan needed just 81 pitches to get through eight innings before the Nationals opted to use a pinch-hitter for him. His accuracy was there again, walking just one batter, and throwing more than 72 percent of his pitches for strikes. Lannan has walked four batters in his past five starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: Whether Vasquez is still in the rotation when his turn comes around remains to be seen. The righty was knocked out of his last start after only three innings. He allowed four runs on six hits and two walks. It was the second time in three starts that Vasquez was not able to pitch more than three innings. He has lost five straight and shown very little consistency with his command. The Pirates could decide to move Jeff Karstens from the bullpen back into the rotation. Otherwise Ian Snell or Tom Gorzelanny, both in Triple-A, could get a sniff.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen had one of his worst outings of the season on Monday, giving up five runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Brewers. However, he ended up with no decision, thanks to outfielder Josh Willingham, who hit two grand slams.

home_pitcher_note: A couple of wacky defensive sequences hurt Maholm in his last start despite the fact that he didn't pitch that poorly. He was up in the strike zone a little too much early, which did cost him a few early runs. He did find a way to settle into his rhythm late, though, and threw four scoreless innings to end the six-inning start. He also closed out his start by getting plenty of groundballs, a sign that he's on top of his command. Maholm is 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in five career starts against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Balester had one of his best outings of his career on Tuesday, lasting six innings and giving up two runs on five hits against the Brewers. In the second inning, he gave up an RBI single to J.J. Hardy that tied the score at 1-1. In the sixth inning, Ryan Braun hit a solo homer, but the Nationals already had a comfortable lead.

home_pitcher_note: Morton took the tough-luck loss in his last start despite allowing just two earned runs in six innings. On an encouraging note, he was more aggressive with his fastball for much of the night and maintained his velocity through his 107-pitch effort. The consistency is still a work in progress for Morton, but the Pirates continue to be enthralled by the movement of his pitches. This will be Morton's first career start against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Mock started for the Nationals on Wednesday and lasted five-plus innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. For weeks, the Nationals would often talk about how Mock dominated the Minor Leagues as a starter for Triple-A Syracuse. He was 5-1 with a 2.65 ERA there. But that success hasn't transferred to the big league level in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Martin pitched his best game as a member of the Nationals on Thursday afternoon at Miller Park, but it wasn't enough, as the Brewers won the game, 7-3. Martin pitched better than the box score indicated. He lasted six-plus innings and gave up five runs on seven hits. Martin said he felt more comfortable than he did in his previous two starts. He made only two mistakes in the game, giving up home runs to Craig Counsell and Prince Fielder. But shoddy defense by catcher Wil Nieves and second baseman Anderson Hernandez did Martin in.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson overcame some mistakes in his last start to pick up his tenth win of the season. The right-hander surrendered a home run to Casey Kotchman and another to Garret Anderson over six innings of work. The Braves were able score three runs on eight hits against the usually stingy Johnson. While his last start was not as good as some of his previous ones, Johnson continues to shut down opposing offenses. The right-hander has now allowed three or fewer earned runs in 18 straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Lannan had an outing he would like to forget as the Nationals were edged by the Pirates, 5-4, at PNC Park. Lannan pitched seven innings and gave up five runs on nine hits. In the second inning, Lannan was given a 1-0 lead, thanks to an RBI double by Willie Harris. By the fourth inning, however, the Pirates had a 4-1 lead.
away_pitcher_note: VandenHurk's last outing was filled with positives and negatives. The right-hander held the Braves to two runs on four hits over six innings while striking out a career-high nine. However, he struggled in the second inning after hitting Yunel Escobar on a 1-2 pitch. Casey Kotchman followed with a blast to center for a two-run double.  VandenHurk would recover to shut down the Braves the rest of the way and his team would tie the game late to help him avoid his first loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen started for Washington on Saturday, and he had nothing in the tank. He lasted three-plus innings and gave up six runs on eight hits. While Stammen was on the mound, outfielder Lastings Milledge burned his former team in the third inning by hitting a two-run double. Stammen didn't record an out in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad was perfect through four innings in his last start before surrendering a hit to Aramis Ramirez in the top of the fifth. The right-hander flustered Cubs hitters until the seventh inning, when Jake Fox clubbed a game-tying two-out, two-run homer. Volstad finished his start allowing two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out five. The 23-year-old has allowed a home runs in seven of his last 10 starts and 10 home runs over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Balester had another solid outing on Sunday, pitching 5 2/3 innings and giving up two runs on five hits against the Pirates. He ended up with a no-decision. Balester still needs to make improvements. He must attack the hitters more when the count is 0-2.
away_pitcher_note: Garland had one of his finest outings of the year last time out against the Mets. The right-hander allowed two runs in a complete-game 5-2 win at Citi Field. The key for Garland was his command and the fact that he was able to use all of his pitches. He has put together seven quality starts in a row -- six or more innings, three or fewer runs -- and has pitched better than his numbers would indicate. When Garland has been bad, he has been real bad, which has ballooned his ERA. Four times he has allowed six or more earned runs in a start. A potential free agent at the end of the year with the D-backs holding a $10 million option, Garland is pitching for his next contract.

home_pitcher_note: Mock started on Monday and was erratic against the Pirates. He lasted four-plus innings and gave up three runs -- two earned -- on seven hits. The three runs were scored in the bottom of the first. It didn't help that the Nats made two errors behind him. When Mock left the game in the fifth, the bases were loaded with no outs. Interim manager Jim Riggleman inserted Tyler Clippard to try to stop the bleeding. Clippard ended up being the pitching hero by not allowing a run to score.
away_pitcher_note: Haren did not have his best stuff last time out against the Mets at Citi Field. The offense staked him to a 6-0 lead, which usually is more than enough, but the right-hander had to hang on for a 6-5 win. The five runs allowed matched the most he has allowed in a start this year. He took the loss in his start before that against Philadelphia. He said that facing the Phillies' lineup was like pitching in the All-Star Game. The Phillies made him work hard, fouling off pitches and running the right-hander's pitch count up early. Haren left after five innings having already thrown 117 pitches. It was the second successive start in which he has lasted just five innings, the only two times that has happened to him this season.

home_pitcher_note: Martin struggled against the Marlins on Tuesday, lasting 4 1/3 innings and giving up three runs on six hits. Florida took a 1-0 lead in the first inning when Nick Johnson singled under the glove of Adam Dunn at first base to score Chris Coghlan. Three innings later, Cody Ross and Josh Johnson hit solo home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has had the two best games of his career in his last two outings. Against the Pirates last Tuesday in Pittsburgh, he had a no-hitter through seven innings before allowing a single to Ronny Cedeno in the eighth. It was the only hit he would allow in eight innings. In his start before that the right-hander handled the NL's best lineup in the Phillies and made it look easy. Philadelphia managed just two hits against him through the first six innings and he retired 13 in a row before allowing a pair of hits to open the seventh. Over his last two outings, Petit has combined to throw 14 scoreless innings and he has allowed just five hits over that span. Petit does not have overpowering stuff so he needs to hit his spots and keep the ball down.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson, who was the Rookie of the Month in the National League for June and fell off a bit in July, began August with a strong six-inning performance against the Padres, allowing two runs on five hits. He has pitched six or more innings in eight of his 12 Major League starts. In his two games prior to his 6-2 win over San Diego, the Braves were shut out while he allowed six runs over 13 innings. He entered the season as the fourth-best prospect in all of baseball according to Baseball America. On the road, he is 3-1, while he also has a 3-1 home record. He had a no-decision against the Nationals in Washington on July 4th when the Braves lost 5-3.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan started for Washington on Wednesday, and he ended up with his 15th quality start. Lannan lasted six innings and gave up two runs on seven hits against the Marlins. But Riggleman felt that Lannan wasn't as sharp as he has seen in the past. Lannan acknowledged that he had to battle on the mound and didn't use his best pitches. For example, he threw a fastball down the middle of the plate to Dan Uggla, who hit a solo home run in the second inning.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe isn't among the Major League hurlers who find comfort with the opportunity to face the Nationals. The Braves right-hander is 0-3 with a 4.03 ERA in his past four starts against them and 0-2 with a 5.02 ERA in three outings against them this year. Lowe is 4-0 with a 2.97 ERA in the six starts he's made since losing to the Nationals on July 5. His bid to win a fifth consecutive decision was erased on Thursday night, when the Braves blew a two-run, ninth-inning lead against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals were down, 6-0, after three innings against the Marlins on Thursday. It didn't help that Stammen had nothing in the tank, lasting 1 2/3 innings and giving up six runs -- five earned -- on six hits. The problem is that Stammen is leaving his pitches up in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday against the San Francisco Giants, Arroyo pitched seven solid innings, allowing three runs on seven hits. It was his third straight quality start, though he is 0-2 over that span. The next hurdle for the veteran right-hander: shrinking his ERA below 5.00. That will certainly occur if his current stretch holds up. Arroyo won his lone start against the Washington Nationals in 2008 by tossing six shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: It appeared as if it was going to be a bad night for Washington on Friday. Interim manager Jim Riggleman didn't want to use his bullpen early like he did on Thursday against the Marlins, but his wish didn't come true. Like right-hander Craig Stammen the previous day, Balester didn't have a good game. The team was down by five runs after 1 1/2 innings. Balester lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on eight hits. Three of those hits were home runs Mark Reynolds, Josh Whitesell and Stephen Drew -- all of them coming in the second inning.

home_pitcher_note: The monkey is off Aaron Harang's back. The Reds righty pitched seven solid innings on Sunday against the Giants, securing his first win in 14 starts. He had been mired in a nine-game losing streak. After allowing two runs on seven hits and whiffing seven Giants batters, Harang credited a change in his mechanics. It will be interesting to see if he can build on the success that those improvements helped bring. Facing the Nationals on June 10, Harang pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings, but a blown save cost him the victory.
away_pitcher_note: Mock pitched the game of his life on Saturday night, and it helped the Nationals defeat the D-backs, 5-2. Washington needed Mock to go deep into the game and give the overworked bullpen a rest. Mock lasted six innings and gave up two runs on five hits. It was the first quality start of his career and the second time he had ever gone past the fifth inning as a starter. The only time Mock had serious problems was in the fourth inning, when Mark Reynolds hit a two-run homer to give Arizona a 2-1 lead. But Mock regrouped and didn't allow another run.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto had to abort his last start on Monday vs. the Cardinals after only two innings because of what was called a tight left hip flexor. Fortunately, it was determined the next day to be just a cramp and it isn't expected to keep Cueto from pitching vs. the Nationals. In his two innings vs. St. Louis that went for a no-decision, Cueto gave up one earned run and one hit with one walk and two strikeouts. He threw 39 pitches. The 23-year-old is 0-5 over his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Martin earned his first career victory by going five innings and giving up one run on five hits on Sunday against the D-backs. That run was scored in the first inning, when leadoff hitter Trent Oeltjen hit his second home run of the season. It took eight-plus seasons before Martin made his Major League debut, against the Mets on July 20, as he underwent reconstructive surgery on his right elbow in 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Lehr has knocked off first-place teams, back-to-back. Coming off of a four-hit shutout of the Cubs, he followed up with a 5-4 win over the Cardinals on Tuesday. While the right-hander gave up 11 hits over six-plus innings, they were all singles and he managed to limit the Cardinals to just one run and left leading by a 4-1 score.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan struggled for the first time in over a month, going just 4 2/3 innings and allowing five earned runs while walking four against the Braves on Tuesday. He entered that start with a 3.32 career ERA against Atlanta, but fell victim to erratic control. He will try to rebound in his fourth career start against the Reds. Facing Cincinnati, he has a 3.06 career ERA in 17 2/3 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen had a solid outing against the Braves on Wednesday, but it wasn't enough to earn the victory. He went six innings and allowed just four hits on 79 pitches, but two of those hits were costly solo home runs. With the no-decision, Stammen remains winless in his last four starts. He turned in a brilliant outing against the Rockies on July 6 in Denver, going seven innings and allowing just one run on five hits. However, he took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez didn't have fastball command early, but threw enough good ones and used his improving breaking pitches to keep the Pirates at bay. When his best fastball arrived, he dominated. Jimenez held the Pirates to three hits in eight scoreless innings of an 8-0 victory at Coors Field. Jimenez is 1-1 with a 4.76 ERA in three career games against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Reds on Thursday, Balester pitched five innings and gave up five of the seven runs the Nationals surrendered. Four of the runs came on a pair of two-run homers by Jonny Gomes. The other was on a solo homer by Ryan Hanigan. One reason Balester has given up so many homers -- he has allowed nine in 24 innings -- is that his four-seam fastball has been too straight. Ironically, Balester said Thursday's start was the best his arm felt all season, but the box score tells a different story.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis' 13th win of the season against the Pirates Thursday marked a return to form for the All-Star pitcher and took him off a three-start schneid. He didn't have his best sinker working, but he was able to hold the Bucs to one run on three hits over seven innings. He worked ahead of hitters for much of the outing and benefited from excellent defensive play behind him. Marquis exploited the holes in the Pirates' swings, striking out six on the day, including three against cleanup hitter Garrett Jones.

home_pitcher_note: In fine form, Mock demonstrated the type of pitcher he is capable of becoming in his last start, on Friday night against the Reds. Mock pitched six strong innings as the Nationals won, 2-0, at Great American Ball Park. Mock dominated over the first four innings, striking out five batters, and he was able to get out of trouble in his final two frames.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel gave up only three runs in a loss to the Marlins on Friday, but constant trouble put his pitch count at 95 after just four innings and gave him a relatively short start. The 26-year-old put at least two runners on in each of his four frames and finished giving up six hits and four walks while throwing just 55 percent of his pitches for strikes. It was the sixth start this season in which Hammel pitched fewer than five innings. The South Carolina native did not talk to reporters after that start, as manager Jim Tracy said he took a flight out of Miami to deal with a death in his family. Tracy said Hammel knew about the matter before his start and that he was "OK to pitch." Hammel is scheduled to make his next start and will meet back with the team in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Martin received plenty of run support in his last start, on Saturday night, as the Nationals downed the Reds, 10-6, at Great American Ball Park. Martin pitched six innings and gave up one unearned run on six hits, even going 2-for-4 with a run scored. Martin had only one clean inning, while the Reds had runners in scoring position in four out of the six frames he pitched. But the righty always found a way to get out of trouble. Martin also took advantage of at least one break he got in the first inning. After Chris Dickerson led off with a double, the next hitter, Willy Taveras, was called out on batter's interference. Martin managed to get out of the inning, leaving two runners on base.
away_pitcher_note: Looper pitched six innings in his last start, against the Astros, giving up four runs on four hits. Other than an RBI triple in the third inning, Looper's only blemish was a three-run homer by Geoff Blum in the sixth inning. Because of Thursday's off-day, Brewers manager Ken Macha said Looper will open the series against the Nationals on regular rest. The right-hander has never faced the Nationals, and he enters Sunday's outing against Houston with 10 quality starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had another unimpressive outing last Sunday against the Reds. He was given a two-run lead in the top of the fourth inning when Josh Willingham hit a two-run homer off Justin Lehr, but Cincinnati came back in the bottom of the sixth to take a two-run lead. After Joey Votto singled to drive in Ryan Hanigan, Jonny Gomes golfed a 2-2 pitch over the left field wall for a three-run homer. Lannan felt that the turning point of the inning was when he walked Drew Sutton with two outs before Votto came to the plate.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are going back to Burns over Carlos Villanueva, who surrendered six Pirates runs on a career-high 11 hits in four innings of work earlier in the week and was moved back to the bullpen. Burns pitched seven innings in a win over the Astros in his most recent start, on Aug. 15. If all goes according to plan, this should be Burns' last start. He and Villanueva have been filling in as starters while Dave Bush (triceps) and Jeff Suppan (oblique) work back from the disabled list, and both are expected to return to the rotation next week.

home_pitcher_note: A 25-year-old rookie, Stammen has shown good control, walking only 19 in 94 2/3 innings, but he has struck out only 43 batters. He did not win in any of his past five starts, but lost only one of them. He allowed two runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Rockies his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Parra beat the Nationals on July 29 at Miller Park despite allowing five runs on nine hits and five walks. "I don't care what their record is," Parra said a few days later. "That's not a last-place lineup. Those guys can hit." Parra is coming off a bad loss to the Pirates in which he surrendered two home runs, one on a 3-and-1 curveball to free-swinging outfielder Lastings Milledge. It was Parra's first loss in the big leagues since June 13. He had been 5-0 since returning from a demotion to Triple-A Nashville.

home_pitcher_note: Balester had a rough night on the mound as the Rockies defeated the Nationals, 5-4, at Nationals Park on Wednesday night. Things started going wrong with Balester during warmups in the bullpen before the game. Balester said he was working too fast and trying to slow down but couldn't. It was the same story in the game. Balester paid the price for working too fast, as he had trouble throwing strikes. He walked five in 1 1/3 innings. In the first frame alone, he walked four batters, with two scoring on a double by Troy Tulowitzki. The second inning was just as bad. Rockies starter Jason Marquis, a good hitting pitcher, doubled to start the inning. Two batters later, Dexter Fowler tripled to send Marquis home. Balester ended up leaving the game with one out in the frame.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo allowed three runs on four hits in six innings against the Pirates on Wednesday but it wasn't enough to avoid his third loss in four starts. Gallardo beat the Nationals on July 30 at Miller Park, when he allowed three runs on five hits in seven innings. He ranks among the National League leaders with 171 strikeouts and is bidding to become just the fourth pitcher in club history to reach the 200-strikeout plateau. His idol, Mexican-born right-hander Teddy Higuera, notched a pair of 200-strikeout seasons for the Brewers, in 1986 and 1987.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano is expected to be activated from the disabled list for this game. Big Z was sidelined because of back spasms, and vowed to be more devoted to doing his abdominal exercises. The Cubs needed their ace this month, but he has made one start, lasting three innings on Aug. 1. He hasn't been as dominating at home, posting a 2-2 record in nine starts with a 3.55 ERA. Zambrano is 5-2 with a 3.17 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Mock continues to get better as a pitcher, but he had some bad luck on Thursday night as the Nationals lost to the Rockies, 4-1, at Nationals Park. Mock cruised through the first four innings, allowing just one hit and striking out six batters. In the fifth inning, however, the Rockies scored two runs, and Mock became the losing pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Harden was stellar in his last start. The right-hander held the Padres to one hit over seven innings, striking out eight. He has fanned 55 in 44 innings since the All-Star break and held teams to eight runs in that stretch. Although he doesn't like to acknowledge the numbers, Harden is better at night and on the road. He is 3-5 with a 6.31 ERA at Wrigley Field. He beat Washington in D.C. on July 16.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals signed Hernandez to a Major League contract on Tuesday night, six days after the Mets gave the veteran his unconditional release. Hernandez will be in the rotation and serve as a mentor for Washington's young starting pitchers. In fact, he will start against the Cubs on Wednesday night, while right-hander J.D. Martin and left-hander John Lannan will be pushed back a day and pitch on Thursday and Friday respectively.

home_pitcher_note: Wells should have received his 10th win in his last start, but he didn't get any run support. Wells gave up two runs -- both unearned -- on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings, while the Cubs were held to one hit by the Dodgers. Wells said he lost his focus briefly, but it definitely was brief. It stung that the only runs off Wells were driven in by opposing pitcher Randy Wolf, who hit a two-run double.
away_pitcher_note: Martin's rookie season has been an up-and-down one, but he has proven to be adept at keeping the Nationals in ballgames and is beginning to build up some innings. He took the loss in his last outing, a 7-3 setback to the Brewers on Friday, but worked a career-best 6 2-3 innings and matched a career high with four strikeouts. In that game, Martin managed to record first-pitch strikes on 20 of his 28 hitters, but he also allowed two first-pitch homers, running up the total of home runs against him to seven in 34 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start -- his first as a member of the Cardinals -- Smoltz made a mechanical adjustment, getting his heel closer to the pitching rubber. The Cardinals claim he also stopped tipping his pitches. Oh, and also, he was facing the Padres at PETCO Park. Whatever the reason, his first start back in the National League was excellent, and exciting. The right-hander will try to make it 2-for-2 when he goes up against the Nationals at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals overcame a poor outing by Lannan, who took a no-decision on Saturday. By the time Lannan left the game in the bottom of the second inning, the Brewers had a 6-0 lead. The Nationals ended up using five relievers -- Saul Rivera, Jason Bergmann, Ron Villone, Jorge Sosa and Mike MacDougal -- to stop the bleeding. The month of August has been a rough one for Lannan, who has given up 19 runs in 18 innings. He has watched his ERA climb from 3.41 to 4.03. Right now, Lannan doesn't have any answers as to why he has been ineffective this month.

home_pitcher_note: Boggs has been riding the Memphis shuttle, and this time he wasn't even down the requisite 10 days. Kyle Lohse's trip to the disabled list allowed the Cardinals to call Boggs back up before he even made a start at Triple-A. There's plenty to like and plenty not to like about what he's shown as a starter in the bigs. Boggs has decent stuff and has handled tough situations well. But his command deserts him at times, which is why he gets in those tough situations in the first place. He needs to improve his command, and thus his efficiency.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals' bullpen needed a break on Sunday afternoon, and Stammen gave it to them. The right-hander delivered a quality start and helped Washington defeat Milwaukee, 8-3, at Nationals Park. The bullpen had been overworked of late. Interim manager Jim Riggleman went so far as to say that Stammen may have to take one for the team, but it didn't turn out that way. Stammen pitched 6 1/3 innings and gave up three runs on five hits. He retired the first seven batters, then got into a minor jam, allowing an RBI single to Felipe Lopez in the third inning. Stammen said he was successful on the mound because he was able to have the hitters back away from the plate with his fastball. He also was able to do what he wanted with his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is strengthening his case for his first Cy Young Award with each passing start as he became the NL's first 15-game winner on Tuesday, throwing eight shutout innings against the Astros while allowing only three hits. Wainwright hasn't walked a batter in four of his past five starts and has gone 12 straight without allowing more than two runs. The Cardinals are 12-4 in Wainwright's last 16 starts, and he has a 1.98 ERA in his last 18 trips to the hill. Wainwright had all of his pitches working on Tuesday, striking out Jason Michaels on pitch number 114 with the tying run at third and two outs in the eighth to keep Houston scoreless.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals gave Mock a lot of runs support in a 15-6 victory over the Cubs on Tuesday night. Mock pitched 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on seven hits. Riggleman still felt that Mock had an impressive outing because he cruised through the first five innings.

home_pitcher_note: For the fifth straight game, Stauffer lasted just five innings. However, he was fairly effective against the Braves on Wednesday after a rocky first inning. He surrendered a three-run home run to Braves catcher Brian McCann on an 0-2 count to give the Braves an early lead but pitched four scoreless innings afterward. Stauffer was pinch hit for in the sixth when the Padres had two runners in scoring position. The win was Stauffer's first since July 30.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez made his second go-round with the Nationals on Wednesday. It was a typical ballgame the organization is used to. He went deep into the game against the Cubs, pitching six innings and giving up two runs on five hits. He looked like the Hernandez of old, mixing in his breaking stuff with his 85-mph fastball and fielding his position better than any pitcher in baseball.

home_pitcher_note: Richard is coming off of his worst outing since joining the Padres. On Thursday, he surrendered six runs in just 2 1/3 innings against the Braves. He allowed nine hits and walked two on his way to suffering his first loss since being acquired from the White Sox. Before Thursday's rough outing, Richard had compiled a 3.67 ERA since joining the Padres. He has never faced the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Last Thursday, Martin was given a 5-0 lead against the Cubs after three innings, and he did just enough on the mound to earn his third victory of the season. He lasted five innings and gave up three runs on four hits. During the month of August, Martin went 3-1 with a 3.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't Correia's best outing, but thanks in large part to a five-run cushion going into the bottom of the second against the Marlins on Friday, he picked up his team-leading and career-high ninth win of the season. The 29-year-old finished giving up four runs on 11 hits and one walk in 6 2/3 innings. Correia was one out away from getting out of the seventh inning and likely finishing with his club-leading 17th quality start, but he gave up an RBI double to Wes Helms and left with his pitch count at 97. Over his past seven starts, Correia is 3-2 with a 3.58 ERA. He is 1-1 with a 3.09 ERA in nine career games (two starts) against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty returned to form against the Cardinals on Friday, giving up two runs in eight innings. But one of the runs was a big one, a solo homer by pinch-hitter Khalil Greene in the eighth that tied the game at 2. The Cardinals won the game in the bottom of the ninth and Lannan took a no-decision. He had given up 23 earned runs in his last 25 innings but dominated the Cardinals to the tune of 17 ground-ball outs. He kept the ball down and was cruising towards his third complete game of the season when he fell behind Greene, 3-1, and served up a fastball that barely reached the seats in left. Despite not getting the win, it looks like the dominating Lannan that the Nationals saw for much of the season has returned.

home_pitcher_note: Mock pitched well against the first-place Cardinals on Sunday afternoon, allowing two runs in six innings and striking out five. But he made one big mistake, serving up an RBI hit by Albert Pujols in the sixth inning with first base open to allow the Cardinals to break a 1-1 tie and slip past Washington, 2-1. Mock has won three of his past five starts and has looked impressive since returning to the starting rotation on July 19. He made 13 relief appearances in April before being sent to Triple-A Syracuse to become a starter. "Whoever decided to put Mock in the rotation, it was a good decision," said Cardinals manager Tony La Russa. "Boy, he was very good."
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old West has put together a nice stretch of starts. Four of his past six outings have been quality starts, including his past two, both wins. The left-hander beat the Padres on Aug. 30, giving up three runs (two earned) in six innings. He struck out seven, which matched a season high. West has one previous appearance against the Nationals. On June 30, he worked 4 1/3 innings, giving up five runs in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez took the loss on Monday in San Diego despite a second solid showing since the Nationals signed him on August 26. He pitched a complete game, but allowed three runs on seven hits as Washington mustered little offense. The defeat moved his record at PETCO Park to 0-5, although he owns 12 career wins against San Diego, second most to the team he'll face next, the Florida Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson pitched brilliantly in his last start, no-hitting the Braves for 5 2/3 innings. But things fell apart with two outs in the seventh inning. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out eight and walking three. Johnson will have a chance to bounce back against the Nationals, who scored all four of their runs against him in the eighth inning the last time he faced them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Martin posted just the second quality start of his young career, holding the Padres to three runs (two earned) in six innings during a losing effort. Martin has opposed the Marlins just once in his career, on Aug. 4, when the righty allowed three runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez struggled with his command at times in his last start, throwing 93 pitches over five innings. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits while striking out four and walking two. Sanchez will look to pick up his first win since August 21 when he faces the Nationals in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan held the San Diego offense in check through four scoreless innings, but a five-run fifth spelled the end of Lannan's day and gave the Padres the cushion they would need to complete the three-game sweep. Lannan got two quick outs to start the fifth, but Everth Cabrera and David Eckstein reached base with ground-ball singles before Adrian Gonzalez hit a line drive that tailed away from left-fielder Willie Harris and landed just beyond his reach, scoring two runs. Chase Headley's two-run double was the other big blow in the frame that added to the San Diego lead.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez turned in best outing since joining the Phillies when he outdueled fellow Cy Young winner Tim Lincecum in a victory over the Giants. The right-hander allowed one run on five hits over seven innings and struck out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Mock had nothing in the tank, giving up six runs in his three frames against the Marlins. The long ball was the main culprit. In the first inning, Jorge Cantu took an 0-2 pitch and hit a two-run homer, while John Baker hit another two-run shot two innings later. Mock said he had mechanical issues on the mound. Most of his pitches were up in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has been bounced around in his last two starts, giving up 12 earned runs in only eight innings, both losses. Lee is coming off a three-inning effort at Houston in which he gave up six earned runs in a 7-0 loss to the Astros. It was quite a departure for Lee, who began his stint with the Phillies by winning five straight games. It will be the first career appearance against Washington for Lee.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had his worst outing since returning to the Nationals, and they paid for it in a 9-5 loss to the Marlins at Nationals Park on Saturday night. Hernandez, who lasted five innings and allowed six runs on eight hits, found himself in trouble starting in the first inning. Six of the eight batters he faced reached base, and three of them scored. In that inning, Hernandez threw 34 pitches, just 14 for strikes. It appeared he was settling down, holding Florida scoreless the next two innings, but Hernandez was hit hard in the fourth, as Florida scored four runs in the frame. Hanley Ramirez highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer to make it a 6-1 game.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton continues to pitch well. His 3.80 ERA is the lowest of any Phillies right-hander since Brett Myers' 3.72 ERA in 2005. The only other Phillies right-handers this decade to have better ERAs are Vicente Padilla (3.28 ERA in 2002 and 3.62 ERA in 2003) and Robert Person (3.63 ERA in 2000). Blanton allowed six hits and three runs in six innings in a 5-4 loss to Houston on Saturday, when Brad Lidge blew his Major League-leading 10th save.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Johnson will be facing the Nationals, a team that's given him some trouble. Last Sunday at Washington, Johnson collected his 14th win, giving up one run on two hits in five innings. He struck out one. The team is monitoring the 24-year-old's innings. He has 183 1/3 on the season, already a career high. He threw 82 pitches at Washington. Johnson's ERA at home is 2.39.
away_pitcher_note: Martin started on Sept. 6 and gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings, making few mistakes. The first was a big one, however, when Hanley Ramirez hit an 0-1 pitch in the fourth inning for his 21st home run -- and 100th of his career. In the seventh, Martin was able to get two quick outs, but he walked Cameron Maybin and gave up a single to Ross Gload to put runners on first and third. Reliever Ron Villone entered the game and gave up an RBI single to Chris Coghlan. Interim manager Jim Riggleman acknowledged that he was concerned about Martin at the beginning of the game because the velocity on his fastball was down. But Martin picked it up as the game wore on.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez gets a rematch with the Nationals after a great six-inning effort against Washington last Sunday. He gave up only four hits but lost a chance at the victory when the Nats rallied to win on Ryan Zimmerman's two-run homer in the ninth inning. Sanchez did a good job of harnessing his control, staying ahead in the count, striking out five and walking only two. It was one of his best performances of this season.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada will make his first big-league start against the Marlins. This is Estrada's second stint with the Nationals. He made his Major League debut last season, playing in 11 games as a reliever and giving up 11 runs in 12 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Rick VandenHurk's back still bothering him, the Marlins chose to put Volstad back in the rotation for Sunday's start against the Nationals, but manager Fredi Gonzalez did not indicate if the youngster would hold onto it moving forward. The 22-year-old from Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., was a key cog in the Marlins' rotation as a rookie last year, going 6-4 with a 2.88 ERA in 15 games (14 starts). But inconsistencies and problems with the home-run ball -- he's surrendered 27 in 152 innings, which was tied for fourth in the National League going into Friday -- sent him down to Triple-A New Orleans on Aug. 29. Volstad gave up three runs in four innings in his only Minor League start on Sunday. In five August starts, he sports a 9.61 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies played home run derby with Lannan and defeated the Nationals, 5-3, at Nationals Park on Tuesday night. Lannan was cruising for four innings and was given a 2-0 lead against right-hander Pedro Martinez. But Philadelphia used the long ball to take the lead. In the top of the fifth, Raul Ibanez homered to cut the lead in half. In the top of the seventh, Jayson Werth and Ibanez hit back-to-back home runs to give the Phillies a 3-2 lead. Two batters later, Carlos Ruiz hit another solo shot over the left-field wall.
summary: 2009-09-13 - Washington Nationals @ Florida Marlins (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Lee went 5-0 with a 0.68 ERA in his first five starts with the Phillies, but is 1-2 with a 9.60 ERA in his last three. He allowed 10 hits, five runs, four earned runs and struck out four in seven-plus innings Wednesday in a victory over the Nationals at Nationals Park. Lee suffered some bad luck in that game. A missed double play cost him a run in the seventh, and an error cost him a run in the eighth. Regardless, the Phillies are hoping Lee gets back on track against the same team that got 10 hits against him last week.
away_pitcher_note: Mock couldn't hold a 1-0 lead after an inning as Philadelphia scored three runs in the top of the second. Jayson Werth highlighted the scoring with an RBI single. Philadelphia made it a 4-1 game in the fifth, when Ryan Howard scored all the way from first on a double by Raul Ibanez. Mock, who lasted five innings and gave up four runs, has not looked good in his past two outings. He has kept the ball up most of the time.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton hopes to return to form after struggling Thursday in a loss to the Nationals at Nationals Park. He allowed seven hits and eight runs in 4 2/3 innings. "I [stunk]," Blanton said. Blanton had been much better for several months. He was 7-3 with a 2.59 ERA in 18 starts from May 26 through Sept. 5. His ERA ranked eighth best in the Majors and sixth best in the NL in that stretch. His 11 consecutive quality starts before Thursday were a career high. The problem Thursday? Simple: command. He threw hanging breaking balls and fastballs over the heart of the plate, and the Nationals didn't miss.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez, the beneficiary of a lot of run support, won his first game as a member of the Nationals this season last Thursday. He pitched 7 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on six hits. It was Hernandez's first win for Washington since Aug. 1, 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has pitched very well in three of his past four starts, having allowed one run in 6 2/3 innings against the Mets on Monday. The left-hander did not have his best fastball, instead relying on changeups and curveballs. His one recent blip was a six-inning, four-run performance against the Pirates on Sept. 1. Still, Hamels is 3-1 with a 1.51 ERA since Aug. 26. He has struck out 28 and walked six over those 29 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided to start Detwiler on Thursday night against the Phillies, pushing right-hander J.D. Martin back to face the Mets at Citi Field on Friday night. The original plan was to let Detwiler pitch out of the bullpen because he was close to his innings limit, but Washington wants to see him get two more starts before the season is over.

home_pitcher_note: The best thing Pelfrey did in his most recent start, Saturday against the Phillies, he said, was spit the hook. He understood he should have emerged from this 28th start with his 11th loss. But the Mets' 11th-hour rally spared him in a game in which he allowed 10 hits -- three of them home runs in an eight-batter sequence that spanned the second and third innings -- and eight runs in six innings. The club now has won 15 of his 28 starts, but that ratio is inconsistent with Pelfrey's recent performance. A return to Citi Field favors him. He has a 6-3 record and 3.56 ERA in 15 starts at home, compared with 4-7 and 6.55 in 12 starts elsewhere. He defeated the Nationals at home in April and lost to them in D.C. in June. Josh Willingham has a .429 average and two home runs in 14 career at-bats against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: Martin turned in another quality performance against the Marlins on Friday. Five days after taking a no-decision in a 5-4 Nationals win, the right-hander earned a victory by holding Florida to two runs on two hits over five innings while striking out four and walking four. Martin has now won two of his last four starts and pitched five or more innings in his last seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding's continued dominance of the Phillies did little for the Mets, who could not score against Pedro Martinez last Sunday in Philly. The result was a second straight defeat for Redding, who allowed merely one run in six innings. Redding now holds a 2.00 ERA in 18 innings against the Phillies this season, and a 6.29 mark against everybody else. Yet he did submit a fine start against his former team, the Nationals, back in June, limiting them to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan picked up his ninth win of the year after holding the Marlins to one run on six hits over five innings while striking out three and walking one. The left-hander kept Florida's offense off balance and did not give up an extra-base hit in his entire outing. He will take on the Mets in his next outing, a team that he threw a shutout against when he last faced them.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start back from the disabled list, Maine will up his pitch count to 75, roughly 15 more than he was allowed last Sunday in Philadelphia. Once again, the top priority for Maine will be the health of his right shoulder, which forced him out of three months worth of starts earlier this season. But Maine will also be seeking his first win since May 31. Certainly, he will take nothing for granted against the Nationals, a team that battered him for seven runs over four innings on June 6, in his final start before hitting the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Mock got off to a slow start on Tuesday night, and it proved costly as the Nationals were blanked by the Phillies, 5-0, at Citizens Bank Park. Mock lasted six innings and gave up five runs on seven hits. The five runs were scored in the first two innings. Chase Utley drove in the first run in the first, when he singled to right field to drive in Jimmy Rollins. In the second, Mock kept the ball up as Philadelphia scored four runs. With the bases loaded, Carlos Ruiz sent three runners home with a double that went over the head of third baseman Ryan Zimmerman. Ruiz would later score on a single by Rollins. Mock was able to blank Philadelphia the rest of the way, but the game was out of reach by the time Mock was able to get it together.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez continues to show that he wants to play for the Nationals next year. He already has four quality starts. In his last outing, Hernandez gave up two runs in six innings against the Phillies on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda has looked like his old self in his three starts back from a mild concussion. Against the Pirates, Kuroda allowed only one run on six hits in six innings. The right-hander relied heavily on his fastball against the Pirates but kept the ball down and struck out seven. That start followed up an eight-inning gem in San Francisco in which he allowed only two runs on three hits. With those outings, Kuroda is reestablishing his place in the pecking order of the Dodgers' starting rotation. This will be Kuroda's first career start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler gave the Nationals some good news during Thursday's 4-2 loss to the Phillies. He lasted five innings and gave up one run on four hits. The lone run scored in the fifth inning, when Pedro Feliz came home on a double by Jimmy Rollins. It was Detwiler's first start since pitching for Triple-A Syracuse in early September. Catcher Josh Bard said that Detwiler cleaned up his mechanics after he returned to the big leagues. There isn't much body movement when he is throwing to the plate these days.
