away_pitcher_note: To say Billingsley is currently struggling on the mound would be an understatement. Billingsley made a relief appearance against the Giants on Friday, and the results were not good. In the eighth, Billingsley gave up a solo home run to Aaron Rowand to make the game 7-4. He then allowed an infield single to Nate Schierholtz and a laser to right field off the bat of Eugenio Velez that Andre Ethier caught for the inning's final out. Then, in the ninth, Billingsley gave up a two-out single, an RBI single and walk before Dodgers manager Joe Torre mercifully pulled the plug on his night. Billingsley is 3-0 with a 2.61 ERA in his career against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Martin is turning out to be the second best pitcher in the Nationals' rotation. Last Friday, he pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on seven hits against the Mets. Martin is second on the team in wins with five.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla suffered through his worst start with the Dodgers on Friday against the Giants. He looked out of rhythm from the get-go as he gave up a leadoff home run and then allowed three more runs in the third. In all, Padilla lasted five innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. His other four starts with the Dodgers have gone much smoother. In those outings, Padilla managed to keep the ball low in the zone and produce quality starts, allowing no more than two runs in any of the four times on the mound. Padilla is 4-4 with a 3.98 ERA in his career against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, right fielder Ian Desmond made a costly mistake in the seventh inning and it would spoil a great outing by John Lannan, who found himself in a pitchers' duel with former Nationals hurler Tim Redding. Lannan lasted seven innings and gave up three runs on five hits. He threw just 74 pitches and should have allowed fewer than the three runs he gave up.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the first of Vazquez's final three chances to gain the two wins he'd need to match the career-best win total that he set in 2001. The veteran right-hander has gone 3-0 and surrendered just two earned runs in the 23 innings that he's completed during his past three starts. His latest stellar effort came on Saturday, when he limited the Phillies to three hits in seven scoreless innings. This will be his first start against the Nationals since 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Mock has lost four decisions in his past five starts. He didn't get a decision in the other one. He's allowed 21 runs in 27 innings over those starts. He yielded four runs on nine hits over seven innings in his last outing, a 7-2 loss to the Mets. Mock's first two appearances this season were in relief against the Braves. He gave up the only run in a 1-0 Atlanta win on April 22.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson encountered some rare struggles on Sunday, when he surrendered four runs and seven hits in five innings against the Phillies. The 23-year-old right-hander entered the game with 17 consecutive scoreless innings. In addition, during his previous four starts combined he had surrendered just two runs. Having already thrown 42 more innings than he completed last year, the rookie hurler is nearing the portion of the season when fatigue could prove to be a factor. He has allowed just two runs in the 13 2/3 innings he's completed against Washington this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez is 1-4 with a 5.75 ERA in six starts since the Nationals signed him on Aug. 25, six days after he was released by the Mets. He allowed eight runs on eight hits and four walks in 3 2/3 innings last time out, a 14-2 blowout against the Dodgers. He beat the Braves on May 5 while with the Mets, holding Atlanta to one run in 6 /13 innings in a 4-3 New York victory.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has halted some of his frustrations while winning three of his past four decisions. The veteran right-hander doesn't seem too concerned about the scratch he developed on his right thumb while limiting the Mets to three runs in five innings on Monday night. He has surrendered 12 homers on the season and four of those have been during the course of his past five starts.  His lone win in four starts against the Nationals this year occurred on Aug. 12, when he allowed two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler will make his 13th career Major League start still in search of his first career Major League win. He has allowed 109 baserunners (79 hits, 28 walks, two hit batsmen) in 64 2/3 innings. His past two outings have been better than previous ones: He held the Phillies to one run in five innings (and took the loss) and the Dodgers to three runs in 5 2/3 innings his last time out in a game the Nationals eventually won, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: Figueroa threw a career-high 126 pitches in limiting the Braves to two runs on two hits in seven innings on Tuesday, but he still suffered his seventh loss of the season. Figueroa was victimized by a two-out, two-run single by Yunel Escobar in the fourth inning that proved the difference. Figueroa has yet to start against the Nationals this season, and he is 1-2 with a 3.29 ERA in seven career games (six starts) against them. He has never started a game at Nationals Park. Washington can't boast of much success against him: Outside of Ryan Zimmerman's 2-for-6, the current roster is 0-for-19 off Figueroa.

home_pitcher_note: Martin started for the Nationals on Thursday and wasn't effective, allowing four runs in the first inning. It didn't help that he didn't have much of a breaking ball. Matt Kemp highlighted the scoring with a three-run homer. Martin allowed five runs in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: It was another inconsistent outing from Pelfrey, who labored through six innings in a 5-2 loss to the Braves. Pelfrey allowed four runs (three earned) on nine hits, with three of those runs coming in the second. Pelfrey is 1-2 with a 4.12 ERA in three starts this season versus the Nationals. One of those losses came in his lone outing at Nationals Park, where he gave up three runs on six hits in seven innings back on July 22. Pelfrey's had the most trouble with Elijah Dukes (6-for-9, HR) and Josh Willingham (7-for-17, 2 HR) while limiting Adam Dunn to three hits in 15 career at-bats against him.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan, who is two-thirds of an inning shy of his first 200-inning season, didn't give up any earned runs in seven solid innings against the Braves on Friday, but he was hit with bad luck on defense and it's the reason he lost his 11th game of the season.
away_pitcher_note: A three-run, first-pitch home run by Hanley Ramirez essentially denied Redding a chance to beat the Marlins Friday night in Miami. Other that the home run and the unforgivable four-pitch walk to Nick Johnson that preceded it, he pitched effectively enough for six-plus innings. Redding walked four and allowed six hits. But now he has one victory in five starts, though the Mets have won twice in that sequence. He faces the Nationals, the team he defeated Sept. 19, allowing one earned run in seven innings plus.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson will be making the final start of his stellar rookie season and attempting to win at home for the first time since Aug. 22. The 23-year-old right-hander has allowed four earned runs during his past two starts. In Saturday's outing against the Nationals, he was perfect during five of the seven innings that he completed and was primarily damaged by a three-run fifth-inning homer. His improved control has been evidenced through the fact that he has worked at least seven innings in three starts this month and thrown fewer than 100 pitches in each of those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Mock continued to struggle on the mound on Saturday, giving up six runs (four earned) over five innings in an 11-5 loss to the Braves. It didn't help that he had shaky defense behind him. Mock didn't harp on that, though. In fact, Mock said the turning point of the game was when he missed fielding a single hit by Chipper Jones, which put runners on first and second in the first inning. Had he fielded the ball, Mock believed the team could have turned a double play.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe provided six solid innings after allowing the Nationals to score twice during the first inning of Sunday's game. The veteran sinkerballer hasn't regained the dominance he possessed at the end of the 2008 season and during the early weeks of this season. But he has allowed three earned runs or fewer in five of his past six starts.   Lowe is 1-2 with a 4.28 ERA in five starts against the Nationals this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez is making his last start of the season. He believes he has six years left in his baseball career and wants those years to be with the Nationals. It's not a secret how much he loves the city of Washington and respects the Nationals -- so much so that he wanted to be on the team in 2008, so he could pitch the first Opening Day at Nationals Park like he did in 2005 in Robert F. Kennedy Stadium. Hernandez didn't achieve his goal last year, because the two sides couldn't reach an agreement. But being back with Washington this season is good enough for him.

home_pitcher_note: In winning his past four starts, Jurrjens has surrendered just two runs and completed 29 innings. In his next start, the 23-year-old right-hander will be bidding to reach his goal to notch a 15-win season and possibly send the Braves closer to a potential postseason berth. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 25 of his 33 starts. One of Jurrjens' tough-luck no-decisions occurred on April 22, when he allowed six hits in 7 2/3 scoreless innings against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler's season is not over. He will start Saturday afternoon's game against the Braves. On Monday, Detwiler pitched six solid innings and won his first Major League game against the Mets. It appeared he was done at a combined 147 1/3 innings, but the Nationals thought he had enough innings left in him to get a another start. The Nationals also wanted to respect the Braves and the Rockies, who were battling for the National League Wild Card. Washington planned to put its best players on the field that day. However, Colorado won Thursday afternoon to eliminate Atlanta from the playoff race. Don't look for the Nationals to change their minds when it comes to Detwiler.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson struggled with his command against the Marlins on Tuesday and paid the consequences via a pair of home runs that marred his five-inning stint. The veteran right-hander admitted this was the most uncomfortable that he'd felt during any of the six starts that he's made since returning from Tommy John surgery. Entering the game, the only two homers he'd allowed in 30 1/3 innings came off Ryan Howard's bat. Despite allowing five earned runs in his most recent start against them last year, Hudson is  8-1 with a 1.57 ERA in 12 career starts against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Martin started for the Nationals on Tuesday and got off to a slow start in the first two innings, as the Mets took a 3-0 lead. In the first inning, Martin didn't have the best control of his pitches. With no outs and the bases loaded, Martin walked Carlos Beltran to force in Pagan. The Mets should have scored more runs that inning, but Daniel Murphy, Jeff Francoeur and Brian Schneider couldn't get another runner home.

home_pitcher_note: Of the five starters named by manager Jim Riggleman, Stammen appeared to be a longshot when Spring Training began. Stammen had bone ships removed from his right elbow last September and it appeared he would start the season in the bullpen or be sent down to the Minor Leagues. Stammen allowed five earned runs in 14 1/3 innings and struck out 10 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield will make the start for Boston, with righty Daisuke Matsuzaka coming out of the bullpen for three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan will be making back-to-back Opening Day starts for Washington. Last year, he lasted three innings and gave up six runs on six hits against the Marlins on the road. Lannan is hoping that things will be different when he faces Phillies ace Roy Halladay. Last season, Lannan was clearly the Nationals' best pitcher. Although he is getting the Opening Day nod, Lannan made it clear that Jason Marquis is the leader of the Nationals' pitching staff. Marquis leads by example, Lannan said. Lannan is expected to pitch twice during the first week of the regular season. Besides Opening Day, Lannan will face the Mets on April 10.
away_pitcher_note: This is the debut Phillies fans eagerly have been waiting for. Halladay joined the Phillies in December as arguably the best pitcher in baseball. Fans liked what they have seen in Spring Training, but now it matters. Halladay waived his no-trade clause to join the Phillies because he wants to play for a team that has a chance to win the World Series. If Halladay is healthy and is as effective as he has been in the past, he could win 20 or more games pitching in the National League with one of the game's best lineups behind him.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis, 31, is coming off one of his best seasons, going 15-13 with a 4.04 ERA with the Rockies. He also represented Colorado in the All-Star Game. During his 10-year career -- which has included stints with the Braves, Cardinals, Cubs and Rockies -- Marquis has won 94 games and posted a 4.48 ERA. He is a groundball-type pitcher and relies heavily on a sinker. Marquis has had three seasons of 200 innings or more. Washington also signed Marquis because he is an above-average hitting pitcher. He has a career .202 batting average with five home runs and 48 RBIs. Marquis also is considered a good baserunner.
away_pitcher_note: One of the reasons the Phillies felt they could trade left-hander Cliff Lee to Seattle is that they were confident Hamels will bounce back following a disappointing 2009. Hamels rededicated himself in the offseason, throwing more than he ever has before. He entered camp in great shape, throwing well and working on establishing a more effective curveball and introducing a cutter. Hamels had a lot of success in the past as a fastball-changeup pitcher. He hopes being able to throw four pitches keeps hitters guessing and gets him back to being the dominant pitcher he had been in the past.

home_pitcher_note: Of the five starters named by manager Jim Riggleman, Stammen appeared to be a longshot when Spring Training began. Stammen had bone ships removed from his right elbow last September and it appeared he would start the season in the bullpen or be sent down to the Minor Leagues. It turned out he was the second-best pitcher behind right-hander Stephen Strasburg. Stammen allowed five earned runs in 14 1/3 innings and struck out 10 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick battled left-hander Jamie Moyer for the fifth spot in the rotation and ultimately lost to start the season in the bullpen. Except that Kendrick will start the season in the rotation because right-hander Joe Blanton has opened the season on the 15-day disabled list with a strained left oblique. Blanton could miss anywhere from three to six weeks, but this is going to be a good opportunity for Kendrick to show the Phillies that he deserves to keep a spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey ducked his least favorite opponent when the sequence of the rotation was changed. Now the Marlins have been replaced by the Nationals as his first 2010 opponent. He has a 3-5 record is 12 career starts against the Nationals, but his ERA in 75 2.3 innings aganust them is 3.72. He has a 4-3 record and 5.92 ERA in 10 starts in April and a 16-18 record in 45 starts in Shea and Citi Field. Pelfrey's performance in spring training was ragged. He has allowed 37 home runs in his career; He allowed seven in a 10 1/3 inning sequence in exhibition games. Josh Willingham, who relishes playing the Mets, has a .412 batting average and two home runs in 17-career at-bats against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals decided Saturday that Mock will be their fifth starter to begin the 2010 season. Mock won the job even though he was hit hard in his last two spring starts, including a game against the Astros' Minor League team. He will pitch against the Mets on Friday at Citi Field in his regular-season debut. General manager Mike Rizzo said Mock was picked because of his potential as a starter. The team believes he will one day become a No. 3 starter. Mock was told that he was on a short leash and the club would quickly call up left-hander Scott Olsen if he didn't produce on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Perez opposed only nine National League opponents last season. The Nationals were one of four teams to face him twice and the only team to beat him twice. He allowed 13 hits and nine walks and hit two batters in only 10 1/3 innings against them. Ollie is not a fast starter. His career ERA in April, 5.92, is higher than his ERA in any other month. He has a 10-15 record in 34 starts in the season's first month. Perez's career record in home starts in 32-35. He won three of five decisions in seven starts at Citi Field last season. Josh Willingham and Adam Dunn have hit three home runs each in 25 and 31 respective career at-bats against Perez.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan is 3-4 with a 3.62 ERA against the Mets during his career. He is looking to atone for his last start, which occurred Monday against the Phillies. It appeared Lannan was going to make up for last year's disappointing Opening Day start against the Marlins. In that game, Lannan lasted three innings and gave up six runs on six hits on the road. But in the top of fourth Monday, Lannan looked like the pitcher who struggled against Florida in last year's opener. Philadelphia batted around and scored five runs. It was Philadelphia's lefty hitters who started things off against Lannan. Chase Utley led off with a walk. On the first pitch Ryan Howard saw from Lannan -- a slider -- he hit a two-run homer over the right-field fence. Lannan faced eight more hitters and allowed three more runs in the inning before he was replaced by left-hander Jesse English, who didn't allow a base runner in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Santana routinely picks on the Nationals, as his 6-1 record and 2.62 ERA against them suggests. Those numbers have been created in a seven-start sequence that has produced 48 innings or almost seven innings per start. Santana has won his five most recent starts against the Nationals, striking out 10 and his 11 in two starts last year. He pitched well enough against the Marlins on Opening Day, allowing one run on four hits and two walks in six innings. His final two innings were not challenging. But the first required 68 pitches. Despite his success against the Nats, Santana has not fared so well against Adam Dunn. The lefthanded-hitting first baseman has four hits in seven career at-bats against Santana, two of them home runs and one of the homers a mammoth jolt that nearly struck what now is the Shea Bridge beyond right center field last season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez -- who has been working out at the Nationals' complex in Viera, Fla. -- is expected to be activated on Sunday and pitch against the Mets that same day at Citi Field. Hernandez said he will arrive in New York on Saturday. With Hernandez expected to be on the 25-man roster, a reliever must be taken off. The Nationals currently have eight relievers, and manager Jim Riggleman said performance will determine who stays and who goes before Hernandez's arrival on the team.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is hoping to finetune his command in time for Monday's home opener against the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park. He threw 103 pitches, just 63 strikes, in Wednesday's 8-4 victory over the Nationals at Nationals Park. In five innings, he allowed five hits, three runs (two earned runs) and four walks. He struck out five. It was just the fourth time since his rookie season in 2006 that he had walked four or more batters.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis will be facing the Phillies for the second time in less than a week. This past Wednesday, Marquis, making his Nationals debut, looked like the player who had serious control problems early in Spring Training. In the first inning, Marquis threw 28 pitches, walked three batters and allowed two runs. After walking his third batter in the inning, however, Marquis retired eight of the next nine hitters he faced, but he got himself into trouble again in the fourth. With one out, Marquis allowed an RBI single to Phillies starter Cole Hamels. In the next inning, with the game tied at 3, Marquis didn't retire a batter. With a runner on second, Chase Utley singled to left to drive in Placido Polanco, giving Philly the lead. Then, Ryan Howard came to the plate and hit a two-run homer, effectively putting the game out of reach. Marquis, who left the game after the Howard homer, pitched four-plus innings, giving up six runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick followed a fantastic Spring Training with a disappointing season debut Thursday against the Nationals at Nationals Park. He allowed six hits, five runs and one home run in just four innings. He struck out two. Kendrick left too many balls over the plate in the first inning. He retired nine consecutive batters at one point, but Willie Harris hit a hanging changeup in the fourth inning to ruin any thoughts of a nice recovery.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen didn't figure in the decision last week against the Phillies as the Nationals won the game, 6-5. Stammen, who was victimized by sloppy defense, allowed four runs in five innings. If there was good news in the game, it was that Stammen was 100-percent healthy. He was in pain all last year because of bone chips in his right elbow. The injury was the reason he was unable to throw his breaking pitches effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Happ threw five scoreless innings Friday against the Houston Astros at Minute Park. He allowed six hits and two walks and struck out five. But he wasn't as efficient as he would like to be, throwing 103 pitches in the process. Happ is hoping to be a little more economical in the series finale against the Nationals. If he does that, he should pitch deeper and give the bullpen a rest.
away_pitcher_note: With Garrett Mock optioned to Triple-A Syracuse, the Nationals will promote Olsen in time for this game. Olsen didn't make the 25-man roster because the team wanted him to build arm strength after having shoulder surgery last summer. In his first start for Syracuse, Olsen pitched 6 1/3 innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. He didn't figure in the decision. While the numbers didn't look great, it appears that Olsen's fastball is back where it should be. It was clocked in the low 90s in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan has struggled so far this season. After getting hit hard in his Opening Day start against the Phillies, Lannan allowed three runs in a five-inning start against the Mets to secure his first win. The Brewers likely aren't Lannan's choice for which team to face when his club needs a quality outing. The lefty has struggled against Milwaukee in his career, going 0-1 with a 7.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo's first start after signing a five-year, $30.1 million contract didn't go as planned. He surrendered six Cardinals runs on five hits including Yadier Molina's second-inning, three-run homer, and Gallardo remains winless through his first two starts of the season. It continued Gallardo's career struggles against St. Louis, but he's had much better luck against the Nationals, going 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts and one relief stint. Gallardo has struck out 21 Nationals batters in his brief career versus only four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez limited the Mets to five hits and allowed only two runners to reach scoring position on Sunday. He threw just 88 pitches, but acknowledged that he didn't have anything left after the seventh inning. It's amazing that Hernandez, who didn't have much of a Spring Training, went as far as he did in the game. He pitched in only two Grapefruit League games, because he was trying to get into pitching shape after signing a Minor League contract with the club in late February. Hernandez didn't go more than five innings in a Spring Training game. When the regular season started, Hernandez was left behind in order for the team to carry eight relievers. Washington didn't need a fifth starter until this past Sunday. Hernandez spent most of his down time in Miami, where he lives, but had bullpen sessions and pitched in an intrasquad game in the team's complex in Viera, Fla.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf has pitched into the seventh inning in both of his Brewers starts but was denied his second win on Sunday when Trevor Hoffman blew a save. For the second straight outing Wolf surrendered four runs, but this time only two of them were earned, the result of an error charged to shortstop Alcides Escobar. Wolf is 9-4 with a 4.43 ERA in 20 career starts against Washington's franchise, tying his second-best win total against any team. He has 12 wins against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis made his second start for Washington Monday, and as he did in his first one, he struggled. He lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs (six earned) on seven hits. Marquis got off to a great start, throwing no-hit ball through three innings. He even helped himself with the bat, hitting a two-run double in the top of the fourth to give Washington a 4-0 lead. But things started to unravel as he gave up seven runs in two innings. Marquis' worst inning was the fifth, when Philadelphia batted around and scored five runs. Chase Utley highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer.
away_pitcher_note: Free-agent pick-up Doug Davis was supposed to be Mr. Reliable in the middle of the Brewers' starting rotation. So far he's been anything but. Five days after he lasted only four innings in his season debut against the Rockies, Davis was touched for six runs and seven hits in just 3 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Monday. Most of the damage came in the third inning, when Davis surrendered a three-run homer to Xavier Nady and a two-run homer to Jeff Baker, both with two outs. Twenty-two of Davis' 34 outings last season qualified as "quality starts" of at least six innings with three or fewer earned runs. He hasn't met that threshold in either of his starts so far.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday, the Nats gave Stammen a 3-0 lead off starter Kyle Kendrick after one inning, but the Phils would come right back and take a 4-3 lead. Ryan Howard highlighted the scoring with a two-run single. Stammen gave up seven runs in the game and lasted 1 1/3 innings. Stammen didn't have any excuse for his disappointing outing. But he continues to have problems with his breaking pitches. He couldn't get them to work in his last start against Philadelphia at Nationals Park.

Olsen started for the Nationals on Thursday and kept them in the ballgame against the Phillies. He was solid during the first five innings, allowing just one run. But things started to unravel in the sixth. With the game tied at 1 and a runner on first with two outs, Olsen had problems throwing strikes. Olsen walked Jayson Werth and Raul Ibanez to load the bases. Juan Castro came to the plate and singled to right to drive in Placido Polanco and Werth. Olsen left the game in favor of Tyler Clippard. After Carlos Ruiz was walked intentionally, Clippard walked Greg Dobbs to force home Ibanez and make it a 4-1 game. Olsen pitched 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching one of the best games of his career in Colorado's home opener, a seven-inning, one-hit shutout, De La Rosa had one of his worst outings in almost a year Thursday, falling to the Mets, 5-0.  His 17-3 record since June 1, 2009, entering Thursday's game was a product, in part, of his pinpoint command.  His command was elusive, to say the least, against the Mets. He walked five and threw two wild pitches, all contributing to run-scoring rallies.  While yielding eight hits and five runs (four earned) over six innings, De La Rosa kept the game from getting out of hand, bailing his team out of jams while minimizing the damage on a day when none of his pitches were working for him.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Lannan had his best start of the season, pitching seven innings and giving up two runs on seven hits, but didn't figure in the decision in a 5-3 victory over the Brewers. Lannan gave up a solo homer to Casey McGehee in the second and an RBI single to Corey Hart in the fifth, but nothing else.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had no fastball command and no secondary pitches in his last start. The result was a seven-run, eight-hit effort in 1 2/3 innings against the Braves. As a result, a decent offensive performance went to waste and the Rockies lost, 9-5. But he can rebound. Last year, Hammel gave up five runs and seven hits in 1 1/3 innings against the Mets, then beat the Phillies in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Hernandez taught the Brewers about the science of pitching. The 35-year-old right-hander handcuffed the Brewers by changing speeds and location. He moved the ball in and out, up and down, but kept it mostly down. Hernandez threw very slow and then much faster, or fast and then much slower. He threw a four-hit shutout as the Nationals stretched their winning streak to three with an 8-0 victory over the Brewers. It was Hernandez's first shutout since 2004, the eighth of his career and his 48th complete game. Hernandez struck out only three and walked two while facing just 33 batters in the nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: How does the right-hander follow up on his last start? Jimenez threw the first no-hitter of his career and the first in team history in a 4-0 victory in Atlanta. He threw a career-high 128 pitches and became the fourth Dominican-born player to toss a no-hitter in the Major Leagues. Jimenez did it despite some control troubles that caused him to walk six. But he struck out seven and set down the final 12 batters he faced to finish the job. And just for fun, guess what he did the next morning? He ran six miles to run off some of his leftover energy. Colorado manager Jim Tracy said he just loves Jimenez's work ethic and how much the right-hander wants to get better.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano was to be recalled from Triple-A Syracuse to make this start in place of Jason Marquis, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list Wednesday with bone chips in his right elbow. This will be Atilano's Major League debut. The 24-year-old has pitched in two games for Syracuse, giving up two runs in 11 innings. He was acquired from the Braves in 2006 for first baseman Daryle Ward. At the time of the trade, Atilano was recovering from elbow reconstruction, but he went a combined 9-8 with a 4.01 ERA for Double-A Harrisburg and Syracuse last season.
away_pitcher_note: Haeger, the Dodgers' resident workhorse, might've run out of steam during Saturday's outing against the Giants. Haeger lasted just three innings, allowing seven runs, five earned, on seven hits. He walked five and struck out three. Haeger was coming off a relief appearance on Wednesday, three days after he made a stellar season debut, striking out 12 Marlins in six innings, the most strikeouts to open a season by a Dodgers starter since Don Drysdale fanned 14 in 1960. Haeger has quickly earned the reliance of manager Joe Torre because of his resilience, but also because he's been effective.

home_pitcher_note: A conversation with teammate Livan Hernandez helped Stammen make up for his previous two starts, and the Nationals defeated the Rockies, 5-2, at Nationals Park on Monday night. Stammen pitched a combined 6 1/3 innings and gave up 11 runs on 16 hits in those previous two starts. After his second start against the Phillies, in which he lasted only 1 1/3 innings, Stammen had a talk with Hernandez, who pitched a shutout Saturday against the Brewers. Hernandez told Stammen to relax, just like he would on the golf course, and work on his pitches in the bullpen. The advice Stammen received must have paid off. The young right-hander pitched eight innings, allowing two runs on five hits, striking out five batters and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Dodgers fans have seen the best and worst of Kershaw this season. The 22-year old left-hander has had better command of his fastball and appears to be comfortable on the mound these days. But, then there's the walks. Lots of them. Kershaw issued four free passes in his last start on Sunday. He has issued 15 walks in three starts, comprising 17 total innings. But he's managed to keep his games under control. Kershaw owns a 3.18 ERA, and in Sunday's outing he allowed just one earned run on four hits with nine strikeouts in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen had an outing he would like to forget in his last start. He lasted two-plus innings -- including four batters in the third -- and gave up six runs on seven hits. Olsen got off to a good start, retiring the side in order in the first inning, but it went downhill after that. His pitches were up in the strike zone. In the second inning, Troy Tulowitzki led off by hitting his first homer of the season. Miguel Olivo then scored on a double by Ian Stewart. In the next frame, 12 batters came to the plate for Colorado as it scored eight runs. Olsen faced four hitters and didn't retire a single one. Olsen insisted there was nothing wrong with his left shoulder, which was surgically repaired last summer.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley lasted just three innings in Tuesday night's 11-9 loss at Cincinnati. He allowed seven runs, four earned, on seven hits, struck out two and did not walk a batter. His throwing error on Homer Bailey's sacrifice bunt attempt helped ignite a six-run second inning for the Reds. Although it was his second consecutive rough outing, Billingsley insists he feels fine physically and is pleased with the location of his pitches. Dodgers manager Joe Torre, who met  with Billingsley on Wednesday, said poor location has been his primary issue. Pitching coach Rick Honeycutt said it's possible Billingsley is trying to be too fine with his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Silva has been stellar so far. The right-hander has given up two earned runs over 19 innings for a 0.95 ERA, and opponents are batting just .152 against him. He also was efficient in his last start, throwing 87 pitches over six innings. If there's been one problem it's hitting. Silva has spent the last six seasons in the American League and he injured his right wrist in his first at-bat of his last start Wednesday against the Mets. He says he'll be fine to face the Nationals, but don't expect him swinging too much.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan kept the Nationals in the game in his last start on Wednesday. However, he continued to have problems against left-handed hitters, who went 7-for-9 against him. Carlos Gonzalez had four of the hits, while Brad Hawpe had two and Jason Giambi collected a knock. Lannan threw 107 pitches. Asked why he has been having a tough time getting left-handers out, Lannan said his off-speed pitches are not working. If the pitches are not working, the left-handed hitters are not going to have problems getting on base.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny deserved better in his last start. Against the Mets, the lefty did not give up a hit until there was one out in the fifth. He retired the first 10 batters and should've been able to go deeper, but an error in the sixth led to two runs and that was it. For the game, Gorzelanny struck out seven. He has made only one start at Wrigley this year and that was April 17 against the Astros, when he was hit on the left arm by a line drive and knocked out after three innings.
away_pitcher_note: It was the long ball that did in Hernandez against the Rockies on Thursday. He gave up a homer to Miguel Olivo in the second inning and another to Ian Stewart five innings later. Hernandez lasted eight innings and gave up the two runs on five hits. Rockies manager Jim Tracy was impressed with Hernandez's performance. To Tracy, it looked as if Hernandez and catcher Ivan Rodriguez were playing catch in the backyard.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a win over the Brewers in which he held Milwaukee to one run on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings. The right-hander did not face the Nationals last year, but does know Adam Dunn very well. Dunn has a .364 lifetime average against Dempster, including one home run. So far, Dempster has posted a better ERA on the road than at home. At Wrigley, he's given up six earned runs over 14 innings; on the road, he's been charged with two over 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Atilano became the 42nd player to make his Major League debut in a Nationals uniform, and it was a great first game for him as the Nats defeated the Dodgers, 5-1, at Nationals Park. Atilano, who was called up from Triple-A Syracuse to replace the injured Jason Marquis, pitched six innings, allowing one run on five hits. After the game ended, Atilano received two pies in the face -- one from John Lannan and a second one from Livan Hernandez. It was worth it, according to Atilano.

home_pitcher_note: Outstanding in his past two starts, Nolasco will look to keep building on his past success. In road games at Philadelphia and Colorado, the right-hander went 2-0, allowing one run in 19 innings, striking out 13 and walking three. Because of off-days and a rainout, he will be throwing six days after beating the Rockies. In those two games, he threw 68 percent of his 214 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen atoned for a tough outing in his previous start on Sunday afternoon, pitching seven shutout innings in the Nationals' 1-0 win over the Dodgers at Nationals Park. On Tuesday, Olsen lasted two-plus innings and gave up six runs on seven hits against Rockies. It looked like the lefty would have a similar outing against Los Angeles, as he was in serious trouble in the first inning. The Dodgers loaded the bases with one out, but Casey Blake struck out and Ronnie Belliard flied out to center field to end the threat. Including Blake and Belliard, Olsen retired 13 out of the next 14 hitters he faced. It helped that his slider was his out pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Through three innings of his last start, Volstad was pretty effective, even though he allowed a solo homer in the second to Colorado's Seth Smith. In the fourth inning, the game slipped away from him. The 23-year-old threw 35 pitches in the fourth, and he was out of the game after a season-low 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Rockies. Volstad seeks his second win of the season, and first since April 14 against the Reds. He had gone at least six innings in his first three starts prior to the rough outing in Denver.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen had his second straight quality start on Saturday, but didn't figure in the decision against the Dodgers. Stammen lasted seven innings and gave up three runs on six hits, but it was the long ball that did him in. The Nats were ahead, 1-0, when Casey Blake hit a two-run homer to give Los Angeles a 2-1 lead in the top of the second inning. Blake hit his second home run -- a solo shot -- off Stammen in the top of the seventh.

home_pitcher_note: So, how does Johnson improve on his last outing? On Monday, Johnson turned in the start of his life, hurling going the distance and driving in three runs in a 10-1 win over the Padres. He Johnson allowed as many hits -- three -- as he had himself. He struck out a career-high 12 batters, allowed just four baserunners -- the other on his only walk -- and was two innings away from the first shutout of his career, until Matt Stairs hit a sacrifice fly in the eighth inning. Still, Johnson will settle for the fourth complete game of his career. That came to fruition when he struck out Chase Headley to end it on his 117th pitch. Johnson came into the game with an uncharacteristic 4.09 ERA and hadn't pitched past the sixth in any of his previous four starts. For his career against the Nationals, the 26-year-old is 5-0 with a 3.51 ERA in 11 games (10 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Lannan will try to get back to pitching more efficiently when he faces the Marlins in the series finale. Lannan admittedly labored over his last two starts, yielding 22 runners and seven runs over 12 innings against the Rockies and Cubs -- even though he was able to keep his team in both games. He looked more in control in an earlier game against the Brewers, holding them to two runs over seven innings. Despite his travails with the strike zone against the Cubs in his last game, he held them to three runs in an eventual 4-3 loss. Still, Lannan noted that he was "sick" of doing things the hard way. Against the Marlins, he has pitched well on occasion and is a career 2-1 with a 4.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez, who tossed seven-plus innings of one-run ball against the Cubs on Tuesday, entered the season on a mission: He had a lot to prove because he felt teams had forgotten about him this past offseason. Hernandez didn't sign with Washington until Feb. 24 and wasn't happy that other free agents signed before him. It didn't help that he was coming off a season in which he was a combined 9-12 with a 5.44 ERA for the Mets and Nationals. Hernandez said that he was still recovering from a right knee injury that he suffered back in 2005. For the next four years, Hernandez never went on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami hasn't yet lived up to the expectations he produced while posting a 3.42 ERA in his final 21 starts last year. While he hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of his first four starts, he has been unable to provide a solid outing since proving efficient during a 65-pitch, six-inning, season debut against the Giants.   High pitch counts have prevented Kawakami from pitching beyond the sixth inning in any of his past three starts.  He issued four walks and surrendered five hits in just 4 1/3 innings against the Cardinals on Wednesday. Kawakami went 1-1 with a 5.28 ERA in three starts against the Nationals last year.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano had another solid outing, and it helped the Nationals edge the Cubs, 3-2, at Wrigley Field on Wednesday afternoon. He lasted six innings and gave up two runs on six hits. It marked the seventh straight game in a which a Nats pitcher had a quality outing. Atilano showed that he could get out of tough jams in a big way. In the fifth, Chicago had the bases loaded with one out, but Marlon Byrd popped up to first baseman Adam Dunn, and Mike Fontenot hit a ground ball to Dunn, who threw to Atilano for the third out of the inning.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his strongest outing of the season, Hanson will look to continue his dominance against the Nationals. While going 2-0 with a 2.28 ERA in four starts against them last year, the 23-year-old right-hander surrendered just one earned run in three of those outings. While pitching a season-high eight innings on Friday night, Hanson allowed the Astros just two runs and utilized an aggressive approach that helped him  throw first-pitch strikes to 22 of the 28 batters he faced. High pitch counts had prevented Hanson from pitching into the seventh inning in any of his previous four starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: After Olsen gave up six runs in two innings against the Rockies in an early season game, it looked as if his season was headed south. But over the last two games, he's shown that there's plenty of productivity remaining in his left arm. He's pitched a combined 13 shutout innings against the Dodgers and Marlins to drop his ERA to a more respectable 4.36. Six of those innings came last Friday at the Marlins as the Nationals finished their most successful April since the franchise moved from Montreal, and gave Olsen his first victory over his former team. Olsen understands well that he does not have the consistent velocity to be a strikeout pitcher, so he thrives mainly when he can mix up his pitches and keep the ball down in the strike zone. He also knows he must use his offspeed pitch in surprise situations. That's been the formula that's worked so well for the last two games.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson battled through some early discomfort with his mechanics and off-speed pitches before righting himself and limiting the Astros to just one run in 6 2/3 innings on Saturday. The veteran right-hander retired 10 of the final 12 batters he faced and would have pitched longer had he not been affected by some of the cramping issues he occasionally experiences amid humid settings.   Hudson is 8-1 with 1.55 ERA in 13 career starts against the Nationals. He has allowed one run or fewer in 10 of these outings and the only outing that he surrendered more than two runs came on July 18, 2008, five days before he was sidelined by the elbow discomfort that forced him to undergo Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Operating on a week's rest, Stammen had trouble controlling his fastball and soft slider in a forgettable outing Saturday night against the Marlins. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits and two walks in four-plus innings in the loss. The effort broke a string of eight consecutive games where Nationals pitchers had quality starts. Now Stammen gets a rematch, this time on his home field. He expects to be sharper in what shapes up as a chance for redemption. He can recall that one of the hits against him last time is hard to be duplicated -- an outside pitch that John Baker nearly golfed off the ground -- and he's mindful that a crucial run-producing two-strike single by Cody Ross came on the same type of pitch that Ross couldn't handle earlier in the at-bat.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad meets the Nationals again. It may be difficult to repeat his previous showing. On Saturday at Sun Life Stadium, Volstad threw a four-hit complete game in a 7-1 win. It was his second career complete game. He walked one and struck out eight. Volstad also had two hits, marking his first career multihit game. On the road this season, Volstad is 0-1 with an 8.71 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Left-hander John Lannan was scheduled to pitch against the Marlins, but he will miss the start because of elbow discomfort. Instead, Chico will make his first big league appearance since May 21, 2008. Not too long after that start, Chico had Tommy John surgery and missed almost two years of action. This season, Chico has pitched in five games for Harrisburg and is 1-2 with a respectable 3.12 ERA. The most impressive stat is that Chico has struck out 17 batters in 26 innings and walked just seven batters. Prior to this season, Chico was known to walked a lot of hitters.
away_pitcher_note: In un-Johnson-like fashion, the Marlins ace rolled to his third straight decision in his last outing. J.J. matched a season high with four walks, and allowed two runs in the second inning. He was at 98 pitches through six, and out of the game. Still, Johnson was effective enough to strike out eight, and allow just two runs in beating the Nationals. Now, he faces Washington for the second straight start, this time on the road. Johnson is 6-0 in his career against the Nationals, including 2-0 with a 3.82 ERA in 2009. He has 42 strikeouts in 37 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez won his fourth game of the year on Tuesday, but he wasn't as sharp as he was in his previous four starts. He lasted 5 1/3 innings, gave up two runs (one earned) and walked five batters. Hernandez threw 123 pitches and 41 of them came in the first inning, when Atlanta scored the first run of the game. Nate McLouth scored on a sacrifice fly by Troy Glaus. Hernandez said pitching on seven days' rest had an effect on him.
away_pitcher_note: In a no decision against the Giants, Sanchez turned in his third straight quality start. In six innings, he gave up three runs (two earned) and logged 90 pitches while squaring off against Tim Lincecum. In all five of his starts, the right-hander has thrown six or more innings. His lone victory came on April 22 at Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Though Maine continued to deal in the high 80s with his fastball last Tuesday in Cincinnati, he featured more late movement on the pitch than he has all season. That allowed him to torment lefties Joey Votto and Jay Bruce, generating swings and misses rather than hits. It's not yet perfect for Maine, but, in his words, its getting there. Over his last three starts (one of them shortened by injury), Maine is 1-0 with a 2.30 ERA. And that, certainly, qualifies as progress. He will look to continue the trend at home against the Nationals, the only team he beat twice last season.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano started Wednesday and had his worst outing of his young career. It was a game in which Atilano had a tough time finding the strike zone. He walked five hitters and gave up six runs in 5 1/3 innings. He was pitching on seven days' rest, but he didn't use that as an excuse for his disappointing outing. Instead, Atilano said he was too pumped up to face the Braves, the team that traded him to Washington on Aug. 31, 2006. The trade occurred while Atilano was still recovering from Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Though Niese served up 12 hits in six innings to the Reds last Wednesday in Cincinnati, he walked none and allowed only four of those runners to score. It was enough for a no-decision and nothing more, but that was hardly a step back for a rookie who has been one of the Mets' most consistent pitchers this season. Niese is the only Mets starter to last at least five innings in all six of his outings. His next start will come against the Nationals, the lone divisional opponent he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Livan Hernandez's re-emergence as a rotation stalwart has obscured an equally impressive comeback by Olsen, who was non-tendered in December, re-signed a day later, struggled with his velocity in Spring Training and started the season in the minors. Since being recalled from Triple-A Syracuse to start on April 15, the lanky lefty's stuff has gotten progressively better. In his last start on Thursday, Olsen took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Braves until his scoreless streak of 20 1/3 innings ended on a night when he allowed two runs on two hits in 7 1-3 innings. The fastball is back into the low 90s with movement and Olsen is using a tricky slider as an effective out pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey logged his longest start of the season against the Giants on Friday, pitching 7 1/3 innings while giving up eight hits and three earned runs. The big right-hander threw just 85 pitches against San Francisco, 61 of them strikes, surrendering no walks and striking out four batters. Pelfrey faced the Nationals in his first outing of the season, allowing two runs in six innings in a win. For his career, Pelfrey is 4-5 with a 3.86 ERA against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: On May 1, Stammen lasted four innings and gave up three earned runs on seven hits against the Marlins. On Friday, he faced the Marlins again and was much better, lasting 6 1/3 innings, while allowing an earned run on four hits. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked none. At one point during the game, he retired 14 straight batters.

Lannan may be on a pitch limit against the Rockies on Thursday. Manager Jim Riggleman said the team wouldn't want him to throw more than 100 pitches. It will be Lannan's first start since May 2 against the Marlins. He missed a start against Florida on Saturday because of left-elbow discomfort. Lannan threw a bullpen session on Monday without having any problems with his left elbow. He threw between 60 and 65 pitches. The team's trainers and pitching coach Steve McCatty were on hand to make sure Lannan was able to throw his full repertoire of pitches -- curveball, slider, fastball and changeup.
summary: 2010-05-13 - Washington Nationals @ Colorado Rockies (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez held the Dodgers to one run and two hits in seven innings of his last start, but wound up on the losing end of a 2-0 final. Jimenez could have prevented the run had he properly fielded a hard smash back to the mound on the play that drove home the winning run. Still, Jimenez has 49 strikeouts against 20 walks while being consistently dominant.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander did it again Sunday against the Marlins. Even though Hernandez got stuck with a no-decision, he gave up just one run on five hits in seven innings as Washington beat Florida, 3-2. Hernandez's ERA actually went up despite giving up just the one run in seven innings. That's how effective he's been all season long. Hernandez and catcher Ivan Rodriguez really have formed a good bond on the field and seem to be working well together. Hernandez continues his mastery at changing speeds and locations, something that's fooling opposing hitters in every start. Sometimes he'll leave pitches out over the plate, and that's when opposing hitters can hurt him, like when Hanley Ramirez hit a solo homer in Sunday's game. But that hasn't happened much this season. Hernandez rarely throws faster than the mid-80's, but he constantly keeps batters off-balance.
