Jimenez could have prevented the run had he properly fielded a hard smash back to the mound on the play that drove home the winning run. Still, Jimenez has 49 strikeouts against 20 walks while being consistently dominant.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander did it again Sunday against the Marlins. Even though Hernandez got stuck with a no-decision, he gave up just one run on five hits in seven innings as Washington beat Florida, 3-2. Hernandez's ERA actually went up despite giving up just the one run in seven innings. That's how effective he's been all season long. Hernandez and catcher Ivan Rodriguez really have formed a good bond on the field and seem to be working well together. Hernandez continues his mastery at changing speeds and locations, something that's fooling opposing hitters in every start. Sometimes he'll leave pitches out over the plate, and that's when opposing hitters can hurt him, like when Hanley Ramirez hit a solo homer in Sunday's game. But that hasn't happened much this season. Hernandez rarely throws faster than the mid-80's, but he constantly keeps batters off-balance.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was struggling before going on the disabled list on April 27 with a right groin strain. In many of his starts, Hammel cruised, only to be tripped up by one bad inning. There were mechanical issues with finishing off pitches. It's reminiscent of Hammel's start to 2009, but by midseason he had corrected himself. The Rockies hope the corrections happen earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano had the third strong outing of his young career, and it proved to be enough for his third win of the season. At first it looked as though Atilano was going to have a long night. In the first inning, the Mets had the bases loaded with one out. It didn't help that Atilano had a hard time gripping the ball because of the cold weather, but he managed to get out of the inning by striking out David Wright and Ike Davis. That marked the second time this season Atilano was able to get out of a bases-loaded jam. The first was against the Cubs in Wrigley Field. Atilano would go on to pitch 5 1/3 innings, allowing five hits, striking out a career-high five batters and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies have held off on announcing pitching plans. The fact Sunday is open could mean the Rockies intend to activate their former No. 1 pitcher, left-hander Jeff Francis, from the disabled list. He won 17 games and two in the playoffs in 2007, but his 2008 was marred by shoulder problems and he missed 2009 with shoulder surgery. Francis was supposed to begin the year in the rotation, but tightness set in just before Opening Day. However, Francis threw seven scoreless innings in his last rehab start for Double-A Tulsa and feels fully healthy.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen wasn't as effective against the Mets  on Tuesday as he was against the Braves on May 6, when he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Marlins. Olsen lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on nine hits, striking out two and walking one. The next day, Olsen apologized to Nationals manager Jim Riggleman on Wednesday morning for showing his emotions after being taken out of the game in the sixth inning Tuesday night. Olsen told the skipper that he didn't realize the television camera was panning on him as he was walking off the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse hasn't been the disaster this year that some fans seem to think he's been, but he also hasn't been as good as he or the club would like. He's had three solid starts out of seven, including two that were very good. It's just that when he's been off, he's been way off: including a nine-run performance his last time out. He's not in any jeopardy yet, if only because there are no really viable alternatives, but at some point if Lohse doesn't get straightened out, the Cardinals may have to begin to look at what else they can do. That time is not here yet, though, and probably won't arrive for a few more weeks if it does at all.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen picked up a no-decision this past Wednesday. He wasn't as effective as he was against the Marlins last week. He lasted five innings against the Mets, allowed four runs on seven hits, struck out two and walked two. However, Stammen had a great day at the plate, going 2-for-2 with three RBIs. The last pitcher in franchise history with three RBIs was right-hander Guillermo Mota against the Red Sox on June 9, 1999.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is pleased with the way he's coming along, feeling better and feeling stronger. But he also grants that this year has been more laborious than some. He's been working to find a consistent delivery, and searching for reliability with his cut fastball, usually a signature pitch. And yet Carpenter still has an ERA in the low 3s, and he's averaging just slightly under a strikeout per inning. The results have been outstanding. If he can in fact get better, look out.
away_pitcher_note: A day after his left flexor tendon stiffened up against the Rockies on Thursday night, Lannan played catch from 100 feet without any problems and is scheduled to make his next scheduled start against the Cardinals on Tuesday. Lannan even had a successful bullpen session on Saturday to make sure he could make the start. On Thursday, Lannan made his first start since May 2. There was good news and bad news when it came to Lannan's outing against the Rockies. He cruised through the first four innings. However, after sitting on the bench for a while in the top of the fifth inning, Lannan's left flexor tendon started to stiffen up. Suddenly, he couldn't get his pitches down in the strike zone. It didn't help that Lannan pitched in rainy, cold weather.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided that right-hander Livan Hernandez will pitch on three days' rest against the Mets on Wednesday night at Nationals Park. The Nationals were thinking about calling up a Minor Leaguer for that game, but after throwing 100 pitches in the first game of a day-night doubleheader against the Rockies, Hernandez went to manager Jim Riggleman's office and volunteered to take the ball. Washington needed a pitcher Wednesday because the day-night doubleheader messed up their rotation plans. Hernandez was originally scheduled to start Friday against the Rockies, but the game was postponed because of rain, and he had to pitch Saturday instead.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Mets have not yet announced who will step into the rotation in place of Oliver Perez, all signs point to the knuckleballer Dickey. In eight starts for Triple-A Buffalo, Dickey was 4-2 with a 2.33 ERA, numbers made better by a complete game one-hitter in late April. In his most recent start, Dickey fired eight innings of three-run ball in a victory. He will be making his first start since last August, and has not faced the Nationals since being blown out by them in June 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano started for Washington on Saturday, and Colorado played long ball with him in the third inning. Carlos Gonzalez hit a two-run homer on a curveball. Atilano said he should have thrown a changeup instead. Smith followed Gonzalez with a homer to give the Rockies a 3-0 lead. Atilano lasted five innings and allowed three runs on four hits. He threw 93 pitches, 59 for strikes. Atilano didn't like that he was often behind in the count.
away_pitcher_note: Twelve straight balls to open the game doomed Maine last Saturday in Miami, resulting in a 7-2 loss to the Marlins. Though Maine featured what he, pitching coach Dan Warthen and catcher Rod Barajas all considered some of his best stuff in the season warming up before the game, it did not translate onto the mound. As a result, Maine dropped his second straight decision. The first of those came against the Nationals, though Maine did not pitch particularly poorly in that one. He will look to rebound against the Nats in Washington, a city that has not been particularly kind to him over the years. Maine holds a 7.00 career ERA at Nationals Park, after posting a 5.56 lifetime mark at old RFK.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen continues to show that he is fully recovered from left shoulder surgery. On Sunday, he gave up one run in 6 2/3 innings and lowered his ERA to 3.15. In his last five starts, Olsen has allowed four earned runs in 32 1/3 innings for a 1.12 ERA in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing Tuesday's side session with no reported problems, the Orioles deemed Hernandez ready to go for Friday's start. The right-hander skipped Sunday's scheduled turn due to right shoulder discomfort that he said had been bothering him for the last two weeks. Hernandez confirmed on Tuesday that he doesn't feel any pinching in his shoulder and is ready to turn the tide on his season on Friday against Washington. He has lost his past 11 decisions, which is the longest active losing streak in the Major Leagues and the second-longest streak in O's history, behind Mike Boddicker's 13 in the late 1980s. Since winning the fifth-starter spot in the final week of Spring Training, Hernandez is 0-5 with a 5.84 ERA in seven starts. He is 0-1 in his only career start against the Nationals, allowing three runs over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In Stammen's last start, the Cardinals scored four runs with two outs in the first inning, the outburst starting with a two-out walk. Stammen rebounded to throw five scoreless innings afterward to give the Nats a chance, but the offense couldn't get enough going to take him off the hook.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off three consecutive wins and a pair of equally impressive performances, Bergesen admitted he didn't have his best stuff in Monday's loss to Kansas City. But the right-hander battled through 6 2/3 innings, to turn in a respectable four-run performance, three of which were earned. Since returning from a brief demotion to Triple-A, Bergesen has regained confidence in his pitches, most notably his sinker, and will look to pick up his fourth win across the Beltway on Saturday afternoon. He is a career 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in two starts against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan produced one of his best starts of the season last time out, allowing two runs on five hits over six innings against the Cardinals. Lannan, who said his arm felt great, made just one mistake, a pitch in the third inning that Felipe Lopez hit over the center-field wall for a two-run home run.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against Kansas City, Millwood threw eight innings while giving up 10 hits but just three runs in a 4-3 win, but did not earn the decision. In four starts on the road this year, he is 0-3 with a 4.15 ERA. Opponents are hitting .277 off Millwood with RISP but .462 with RISP and two outs. Millwood is 15-5 with a 3.59 ERA against the Nationals. That's his most victories against any team and six more than any other club. Millwood's run support is 2.34 per nine innings -- the lowest in the American League.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was pounded in his last outing, a 13-1 loss at Arizona in which he yielded five runs in five innings. Three of the four hits he surrendered were home runs. But he sparkled one start earlier, limiting Houston to two runs and five hits in 7 1/3 innings in an 8-2 win on May 14 in San Francisco. Statistics reflect Wellemeyer's preference for pitching at home, where he's 2-1 with a 3.04 ERA compared with 0-3, 9.35 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: In Hernandez's last start, pitching on only three days' rest, he picked up a no-decision after allowing two runs on four hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Mets. Angel Pagan's inside-the-park home run in the fourth inning put the Mets up 1-0 early, but the Nationals rallied for a 5-3 victory. Hernandez is 4-6 against the Giants in his career with a 3.95 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum had by far his worst performance of the season last Thursday at Arizona, allowing five runs and five hits while walking five in five innings. He did strike out six, hiking his National League-leading total to 75. Something to consider when evaluating Lincecum's victory total: San Francisco's bullpen has blown four leads they have inherited from him. Lincecum has recorded a 1-0 record with a 1.77 ERA in three career appearances against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: After beginning his professional career with a strong 3-0 start -- including a six inning, one run debut against the Dodgers -- Atilano struggled in his most recent outing against the Mets. He gave up seven runs on nine hits over 4 1/3 innings pitched in a 10-7 loss. David Wright put the Mets ahead early on his three-run double to right-center field. New York added five more runs in the fifth inning. One inning later, Rod Barajas crushed a two-run home run to left-center field. Atilano has never faced the Giants in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Zito, who's 2-2 with a 4.33 ERA in six career appearances against Washington, allowed a season-high six runs and nine hits in 6 2/3 innings last Friday in a 6-1 Giants loss at Oakland. Two of those hits, however, were back-to-back bloop doubles that fueled a three-run third inning and skewed Zito's numbers. Zito's success this year is partly due to avoiding the long ball. He has allowed one home run in 61 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In Stammen's last outing, he got a no-decision after allowing four earned runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Orioles.  He surrendered two home runs -- one an inside-the-park home run by Adam Jones in the fourth inning -- but the Nationals rallied to win, 7-6. Stammen has faced the Giants once in his career, taking a no-decision after giving up four earned runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Richard lowered his ERA to 2.72 by allowing seven hits with no walks in a victory over Seattle. He finished with six strikeouts and got five groundouts, none more important than a ground ball that third baseman Chase Headley turned into a 5-4-3 double play in the sixth inning when the Mariners scored their lone run. "That was huge," Headley said of the ball hit by Franklin Gutierrez. "In my opinion, that might have been the best I have seen him. He was tremendous, even when they got a few runners on." Richard has been working on throwing first-pitch strikes. It's certainly shown lately.
away_pitcher_note: After a month without registering a win, questions loomed over whether Lannan was healthy or needed to fix his elbow. He answered those critics on Sunday by going 5 1/3 innings against the Orioles, allowing one run on two hits, both in the first inning. Lannan has allowed three runs in 11 1/3 innings in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching with a migraine headache, Latos allowed one run over six innings in a victory over the Mariners in Interleague Play the last time out. Latos has now won three of his last four starts and has allowed a total of three earned runs over his last four starts covering 29 innings for an ERA of 0.93 ERA. Not bad for a pitcher who now has 19 career Major League starts. He allowed four hits with five strikeouts and two walks. "I talked about the changeup last year, how effective it was," Padres manager Bud Black said. "His slider, this year, has come into its own. I'm seeing the confidence develop along with his poise. He's a young pitcher but he's doing some good things."
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided that Martin or left-hander Matt Chico will get the start. It appears that Martin is the leading candidate because Chico pitched Tuesday for Triple-A Syracuse and allowed three runs in five innings against Toledo. If he were to get called up, Chico would pitch on three days' rest. Martin last pitched Saturday and would face the Padres on six days' rest. For the season, Martin is 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA for Syracuse.

home_pitcher_note: After a semi-rough start, for him at least, Garland eventually settled down to improve to 6-2 this season while lowering his ERA to 2.10, as he tossed seven scoreless innings in the Padres' victory over the Cardinals. Garland retired nine consecutive hitters at one point. He allowed one baserunner in the seventh inning, but he got Skip Schumaker on a 5-4-3 double-play ball started by third baseman Chase Headley to end the inning. Garland struck out seven and walked two. "I thought his last three innings were pretty solid," Padres manager Bud Black said. "As you get through the first couple innings, I think both pitchers felt like they had to match each other."
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, it looked like Hernandez was going to have one of his best games of the season, but one bad inning proved costly as the Nationals lost to the Giants at AT&T Park on Tuesday night. After allowing a leadoff double to Andres Torres in the bottom of the first inning, Hernandez retired 12 out of the next 14 hitters he faced. But it went downhill for Hernandez in the fifth, when the Giants scored four runs. During San Francisco's rally, Hernandez threw just 12 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Despite a 3-6 record, Oswalt has posted a quality start in each of his 10 outings. With one more against Washington, he'll tie the franchise record set by Dave Giusti in 1968. In his last trip to the mound, Oswalt pitched eight scoreless innings and allowed just four hits with nine strikeouts in a win in Milwaukee. Although he has started six games in the past four years against Washington, Oswalt hasn't earned a decision against the club since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano has pitched only seven games during his career, but he bested Tim Lincecum on Wednesday, lasting 5 1/3 innings and giving up two runs on four hits. Atilano cruised through the first four innings. San Francisco, however, was able to get to him in the fifth, when Juan Uribe hit a solo homer. An inning later, when Pablo Sandoval came to the plate, Atilano left the game in favor of left-hander Doug Slaten. Sandoval doubled, scoring Andres Torres. The run was charged to Atilano, who said he was pleased with his performance. He wasn't behind in the count like he was in his most recent start and threw fewer pitches -- 76.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has pitched at least six innings in each of his 10 starts this year. In his last five games, he is 2-1 with a 2.65 ERA, although the Astros have scored more than four runs in just one of those starts. Myers will make his 34th career appearance against Washington, which is more than any other opponent. He's 10-9 with a 4.18 ERA against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen was solid during the Nationals' loss to the Giants at AT&T Park on Thursday afternoon. Stammen lasted 6 1/3 innings, allowing two earned runs on five hits. It was his first quality start since May 7 against the Marlins. Stammen needed to have a good outing because he could be the odd man out of the rotation once right-hander Stephen Strasburg is called up next month. Before Thursday's game, Stammen was 1-2 with a 5.96 ERA. Manager Jim Riggleman did not indicate if Stammen is in danger of losing his spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had his roughest performance of the season his last time out, lasting just 3 1/3 innings and allowing eight runs in a 15-6 loss in Cincinnati. The left-hander said he is struggling with his curveball and needs to work on his command. The month of May was particularly rough for Rodriguez, as he went 1-5 with a 6.75 ERA after posting a 3.65 ERA in April.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan started for the Nationals and lasted seven innings, allowing two runs on seven hits. It was Lannan's first win since April 10 against the Mets. In his past three starts, Lannan has allowed four earned runs over 18 1/3 innings. His left elbow problems appear to be a thing of the past.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler began the season in the bullpen and made 12 relief appearances before making a spot start on Saturday in place of Bud Norris, who was placed on the disabled list with bursitis and biceps tendinitis. In that start, Moehler was rocked for 10 hits and eight earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, and he struggled with his location. He's 3-4 with a 4.87 ERA in 14 career games (nine starts) against the Nationals and is 10-14 with a 5.32 ERA in 67 career appearances (22 starts) at Minute Maid Park. Moehler is 80-99 with a 4.90 ERA in 245 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Martin made his first start of the season last Saturday at San Diego, allowing four hits and one earned run in six innings. He struck out five, walked none and gave up a home run, to Nick Hundley in his 88 pitches. He went 5-4 with a 4.44 ERA in 15 starts last year with Washington. Martin was called up last Friday from Triple-A Syracuse, where he was 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA, to replace outfielder Justin Maxwell on the Washington roster. It will be difficult for Martin to hold his spot in the rotation with left-hander Scott Olsen due back soon from a shoulder injury and right-hander Stephen Strasburg expected to debut between June 8 and 10 vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez keeps rolling along at age 35 in his second stint with Washington. He hasn't won since May 4 against Atlanta, but he has pitched well. He allowed Florida only one run in seven innings on May 9, but received a no-decision. He made his last start Sunday in San Diego. He went 6 1/3 innings, giving up eight hits but only two runs. He struck out four and walked none. He allowed a season-high four runs in a May 25 loss in San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Harang allowed his fewest runs of the season last time out, giving up one run and four hits in seven innings of a blowout win against Houston. The seven innings also tied for his longest start, and he's earned a win in back-to-back games for the first time since May 2009. Harang has never won in five career starts against the Nationals and is 0-2 with a 3.99 ERA. He allowed just two runs in 14 2/3 innings in two starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano outpitched Tim Lincecum and Roy Oswalt in his past two starts. Not bad. He lasted 6 2/3 innings Monday in Houston, giving up six hits and three earned runs, throwing 104 pitches. His only loss of the season was May 20 at home to the New York Mets, when he was knocked out after 4 1/3 innings, his shortest outing of the season. He's not a strikeout pitcher, with only 16 strikeouts in 44 innings this season. He has walked 21.
away_pitcher_note: Leake's impressive rookie season continues, but he hasn't picked up a win since May 15. In three no-decisions, Leake has allowed just four runs in 19 1/3 innings -- although he gave up a season-high 10 hits to Pittsburgh. After Leake pitched six scoreless innings against Houston on Sunday, Astros' first baseman Lance Berkman said he is having success through deceptive movement on his pitches, saying, "He's got a little movement probably than you give him credit for."

home_pitcher_note: Stammen barely survived the first inning in his last start on Tuesday in Houston. He gave up three hits, two walks and three runs in the first, then settled down. But he gave up another run in the third and a solo homer to Hunter Pence in the fifth, his final inning. Stammen won his only game of the season on April 19 vs. Colorado, when he gave up just five hits and two runs in eight innings. He never made it through seven innings in his six starts in May. He surrendered just one earned run in 6 2/3 innings when he received a no-decision in a May 7 start vs. Florida.
away_pitcher_note: After winning four in a row and going 5-0 in six starts, Arroyo's hot streak ended in St. Louis on Memorial Day. Pitching on both sides of a rain delay, he lasted 4 1/3 innings, giving up 10 hits and seven runs with five walks. The seven runs equaled the total he allowed in the previous four wins. Maybe facing Washington is exactly what he needs to bounce back. In one start against the Nationals in each of the Past two years, Arroyo didn't allow a run -- including a two-hit shutout in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided that Strasburg will make his Major League debut on June 8 against the Pirates -- provided that a rainout or injury doesn't stand in the way. Strasburg, 21, will become the fourth first-round Draft pick -- third baseman Ryan Zimmerman and pitchers Ross Detwiler and Drew Storen are the others -- in Nationals history to reach the big leagues. Strasburg, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2009 First-Year Player Draft, has been dominant in the Minors, going a combined 8-2 with a 1.30 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 55 1/3 innings for Double-A Harrisburg and Triple-A Syracuse.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens is the man called upon to face the highly touted Stephen Strasburg in the rookie's debut, though Wednesday's rainout against the Cubs made this more a matter of circumstance, since Zach Duke's start was pushed back to Friday. Regardless, Karstens hopes to be up for the challenge, though he has struggled against Washington in the past. In three appearances (one start) against the Nationals, Karstens has a no-decision and a 9.35 ERA over 8 2/3 innings pitched. He has given up nine runs on 15 hits while striking out six and walking three. But Pirates manager John Russell mentioned Karstens' performances in pressure situations when announcing him for Tuesday, citing his April 27 outing against the Brewers, when he pitched 6 2/3 innings and gave up just two earned runs to help the Pirates snap a 22-game skid at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: The last thing Lannan was seen throwing was a shaving-cream pie in the face of Stephen Strasburg, during the postgame interviews following Strasburg's debut on Tuesday night. There might be fewer people in the stands and fewer laptops in the press box, but Lannan is the one who will try to give the Nationals their back-to-back wins since May 22-23, when they took two straight Interleague games from the Orioles. After a rough start to the season, Lannan has seen his ERA steadily shrink from 6.51 to 4.79 across his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates promoted Lincoln to make his MLB debut. The Bucs' first pick -- and the fourth selection overall -- in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, the 25-year-old Texan right-hander sat out the 2007 season following Tommy John surgery. Lincoln is 6-2 with a 3.16 ERA in 11 starts for Triple-A Indianapolis this season. He has a 55-14 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 68 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This past Friday, Hernandez gave the Nationals another quality start by allowing just two runs in his six innings against the Reds. He has not win a game in more than a month. His last victory came in on May 4 against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball did in Duke in his last outing, when the southpaw gave up three home runs in a two-inning span to take the 6-4 loss. He gave up 10 hits and struck out five, and he has not won a game since out-dueling Philadelphia's Roy Halladay in a 2-1 win on May 18. Duke has given up 10 home runs on the season. In four career starts against the Nationals, Duke is 1-1 with a 5.11 ERA, giving up 29 hits in 24 2/3 innings while striking out eight and walking 11. His last start in Washington came May 1, 2008, when he recorded a no-decision in a seven-inning performance. He gave up two runs off five hits in a 3-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook struggled in his last start against the White Sox. Despite being staked to an early 6-2 lead on the strength of two early three-run innings, Westbrook fell apart in the fifth inning and got a no-decision in the Indians' 8-6 loss to the White Sox. "I just wasn't very consistent with either one of [my arm slots], over the top or dropping down," Westbrook said after his last start. "I was just very erratic today and didn't get the job done." In his only start against the Washington Nationals, Westbrook lost, giving up seven hits, no walks and three runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Last Saturday, Atilano pitched well enough to win, but the Nationals lost to the Reds, 5-1, at Nationals Park. Atilano had arguably his best-pitched game of the season, throwing seven innings, allowing two runs -- one earned -- on six hits. He struck out six batters and walked one, which pleased manager Jim Riggleman. Atilano ended up being outpitched by Reds right-hander and fellow rookie Mike Leake, who allowed one unearned run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona logged his ninth quality start of the season Monday, scattering five hits and six walks over six-plus innings of three-run ball in a 4-1 loss to the Red Sox at Progressive Field. Cleveland manager Manny Acta praised the right-hander after the game for maintaining his composure on the mound, which has been an issue for the Dominican sinkerballer in recent seasons. Three years removed from the 19-win season that gained him recognition around the Majors, Carmona has once again emerged as a reliable rotation option for the Tribe in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Since rejoining the Nationals in late May, Martin has walked one batter in 11 2/3 innings. His success on the mound is one of the reasons right-hander Craig Stammen was sent down to Triple-A Syracuse.

home_pitcher_note: Huff recovered from an abysmal outing against the Tigers (not to mention the beaning he took from an Alex Rodriguez liner one start earlier) to give the Indians six strong innings against the Red Sox on Tuesday night. If not for a two-out Trevor Crowe error in center field that opened the door to a three-run fourth inning for Boston, Huff would have been in line for a victory. He allowed just those three runs, all of which were unearned, on eight hits with a walk and six strikeouts. This was an important pick-me-up outing for Huff, who continues to have to prove himself in the Tribe rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Making his Major League debut after 11 sensational Minor League starts, Strasburg pitched seven innings of two-run ball against the Pirates on Tuesday, earning the win and striking out 14 in a 5-2 victory. Delwyn Young's two-run home run with two outs in the fourth was the only damage against Strasburg. A sellout crowd of 40,315 saw Strasburg allow just four hits. The 14 strikeouts established a club record and were one shy of the record in a debut set by Karl Spooner in 1954 and J.R. Richard in '71. Even more amazing was that he struck out no more than nine batters in a game when pitching in the Minor Leagues. Strasburg, who did the job without looking at scouting reports, threw 94 pitches, 65 for strikes, and didn't walk a batter. The righty retired his final 10 batters, striking out his last seven.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Max Scherzer continued to show that his short stint in Triple-A Toledo was extremely beneficial. Unfortunately, in his three starts since being recalled, his win-loss record hasn't indicated how much improvement he's made. Scherzer has posted a 1-2 record, but has only given up a combined eight earned runs in three starts. In his last start, Scherzer allowed three runs on five hits in 7 1/3 innings, while fanning seven batters. But the Tigers' offense was unable to provide any run support to back a solid outing -- a problem many of the Tigers' starters have dealt with of late.
away_pitcher_note: A day after Stephen Strasburg's dominating performance, Lannan went to the mound and had one of his worst outings on Wednesday night. However, the bullpen and the position players helped the Nationals defeat the Pirates, 7-5, in front of 18,876 fans at Nationals Park. Lannan lasted 4 2/3 innings and allowed five runs -- four earned -- on 10 hits. He said he didn't feel any pressure following up Strasburg's huge performance.

home_pitcher_note: Considering at least half of Verlander's four losses have come in part from low run support, he was due for a game in which offense and defense helped him out. Verlander called his fastball "horrible" in his previous outing. And while he ended up with more walks (four) than strikeouts (three), he still managed seven-plus innings of two-run ball against the Pirates for another Interleague victory. He's 10-1 with a 2.88 ERA lifetime against the National League, and he'll have at least three more meetings with the Senior Circuit before the Tigers close out Interleague Play.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez was solid on the mound as the Nationals defeated the Pirates, 4-2, and swept the three-game series. Hernandez pitched six innings and allowed two runs on five hits. It was his first win since May 4 against the Braves. He also picked up his 10th quality start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman owns four quality starts in his last five outings, the latest being seven innings of two-run ball last Saturday against the Pirates in just 91 pitches. At times, manager Jim Leyland says, he looks as good as at any point Leyland has been here, which dates back to 2006. All in all, the ingredients are there for a big summer if he can get just a little more run support, which he hopes he can find against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano started for Washington and lasted five-plus innings, allowing six runs -- three earned -- on seven hits against the Indians. The first three runs were scored in the first inning. With one out and Carlos Santana on first, Russell Branyan hit a perfect double-play ball to second baseman Adam Kennedy, who booted the ball for an error. Austin Kearns was the next hitter and hit a three-run homer to give Cleveland a 3-1 lead.

home_pitcher_note: It's safe to call Strasburg the stopper. He helped the Nationals end a modest two-game losing skid and defeat the Indians, 9-4, in front of 32,976 at Progressive Field on Sunday afternoon. It was Strasburg's second Major League start, and he picked up right where he left off in his debut before faltering in the sixth inning.  Strasburg struck out eight batters while allowing just two hits, including a solo home run by Travis Hafner, but he walked five of the last 12 batters he faced -- several while experiencing issues with the mound -- and exited with the bases loaded and a 6-1 lead in the bottom of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd's gem was overshadowed and went for naught Sunday. Pitching in front of a national television audience and going head-to-head with the crosstown rival Cubs, Floyd tossed 6 2/3 innings before allowing a hit. He went the distance, giving up just one run on three hits while walking three and striking out nine in a 1-0 loss. Counterpart Ted Lilly and closer Carlos Marmol one-hit the White Sox to doom Floyd, who has not won a decision since May 22 against the Marlins. Sunday marked the third time Floyd had carried a no-hitter that late in the game, having lost the bids within a one-month span in 2008 against the Tigers and Twins in the eighth and ninth innings, respectively. In four career appearances (two starts) against the Nationals, Floyd is 1-1 with a 4.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander J.D. Martin pitched 7 2/3 innings against the Indians, but he gave up seven runs, six of which were earned. Carlos Santana highlighted a four-run inning by hitting a two-run double. In the fifth inning, he hit a solo home run.
away_pitcher_note: Right arm soreness moved back Peavy to Saturday after he was scheduled to go Thursday against the Pirates. But an MRI revealed no structural damage for the right-hander, who will make his first start in eight days. His last outing, against the Cubs, earned him career win No. 100. He gave up just two runs on six hits in seven innings while striking out five, getting back to .500 in the process. In nine career starts against the Nationals, Peavy is 2-4 with a 4.18 ERA. He has never pitched in Nationals Park, despite spending the majority of 2008 and 2009 with the Padres in the National League.

away_pitcher_note: After Garcia's last start, manager Ozzie Guillen said he was the one thing his team felt good about. away_pitcher_note: Chen turned in a creditable outing in his last start, working 5 2/3 innings and allowing just five hits and four runs (three earned) against the Astros. away_pitcher_note: Bannister has lost his past two decisions after posting a five-game winning streak. away_pitcher_note: Dickey has a 5.60 ERA in three starts since giving up one unearned run in six innings during his first outing of 2011. Against the Nationals on April 8, the knuckleballer gave up three runs on six hits and five walks in five innings.

away_pitcher_note: Weakened by the flu in his previous two starts, Sanchez ought to be fit for this outing. Despite feeling subpar, he has averaged 10.6 strikeouts per nine innings and has limited opponents to a .214 batting average.

away_pitcher_note: Lannan suffered a hard-luck loss in his most recent outing vs. the Giants. He allowed six hits and three walks in 6 2/3 innings, but he issued a bases-loaded walk in the seventh and the Nats lost, 2-1.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco comes off an impressive win at Cincinnati, where he gave up three runs in seven frames. The righty is 8-3 with a 4.17 ERA vs. the Nats, and he's meeting them for the first time in '11. Nolasco has 27 K's and just five walks in 40 1/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann snapped a three-game losing streak by allowing two runs in six innings against San Francisco his last time out. In four of his six outings, he's allowed no more than two runs. He's allowed only seven walks and one homer in 35 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Lannan was roughed up by the Phils in his last start, giving up six runs over two innings. He will try to rebound vs. a team he has had a lot of success against, having won his last three starts vs. the Braves. He is 4-2 with a 3.60 ERA in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe is no longer battling the right foot blister that bothered him as he took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of Friday's win over the Phillies.  He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 11 of his past 13 starts.

away_pitcher_note: Volstad is facing the Nationals in back-to-back starts, and he looks to rebound from a loss. Volstad overcame a 35-pitch first to deliver six innings. He threw 102 pitches. This is his third meetings with Washington already.

away_pitcher_note: Oswalt allowed nine hits and one earned run in six innings Friday in a victory over the Mets at Citi Field. Oswalt is 0-1 with a 1.50 ERA in three starts since returning from the disabled list (lower back inflammation). He said he has felt fine.

away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann pitched seven solid innings and allowed one run on six hits against the D-backs in his last start. It marked the sixth consecutive game in which he allowed three runs or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Since starting the year 0-5 in his first six starts with a 4.86 ERA, Latos has gone 4-1 in his last five starts and lowered his ERA to 3.94.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis received a five-game suspension for hitting D-backs outfielder Justin Upton with a pitch. Marquis has appealed the suspension and will pitch against the Padres  on Friday.

away_pitcher_note: Lannan outdueled Tim Lincecum, allowing just four hits and one run over seven innings Monday. He struck out six, walked three and didn't allow a run until Giants outfielder Aaron Rowand led off the seventh with a home run to left.

away_pitcher_note: In his last seven starts, Zimmermann allowed three runs or fewer. On Tuesday, Zimmermann lasted seven innings and allowed the one run on five hits against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Maya pitched his best game of the season, allowing a run on four hits over six innings against the Giants. Maya ended up with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia dropped two of his last three outings after a string of four consecutive wins propelled him through the month of May. Garcia hasn't lasted more than five innings in three of his past four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez, by his own admission, said he didn't give the team a chance to win on Thursday. He lasted 5 1/3 innings and allowed six runs on nine hits against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: McClellan is expected to come off of the DL after coming off rehab for a hip injury and get right back to the mound. The right-hander last pitched May 30 and surrendered seven earned runs through four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had his best stretch of the season over the past four starts, when he allowed a combined two runs over 26 1/3 innings. He picked up a win against the Cardinals in April, pitching five innings of two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is coming off a five-inning outing, which was his shortest of the season. He has won four of his last five starts and looks to rebound after surrendering four earned runs to the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles roughed up Marquis in the teams' first Interleague meeting this season, but he escaped with a no-decision as the offense erupted for 17 runs. He is 2-0 with a 1.53 ERA in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Britton rebounded from two poor starts Wednesday to record his first win since May 1. The rookie southpaw struck out six through 6 1/3 innings while giving up just one earned run on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has a sub-.500 record, but he is establishing himself as the staff ace. He has eight straight quality starts -- including one against the O's -- and he's gone at least seven innings, allowing one run or less, in each of his past three.
away_pitcher_note: Matusz will make his fourth start of the season after being roughed up by the Rays his last time out. The 24-year-old left after 1 1/3 innings, allowing four runs on five hits and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny makes his first start after a trip to the 15-day disabled list with elbow soreness. He allowed four runs in four innings in a rehab start with Triple-A Syracuse and struggled before the DL stint.
away_pitcher_note: Jakubauskas makes his third start since joining the rotation in early June. He left after 5 1/3 innings his last time out against the Blue Jays, allowing four runs on seven hits. He has a 2.35 ERA in four career Interleague games.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez was his vintage self his last time out, throwing a three-hit shutout against the Cards on 105 pitches. It was the 50th complete game of Hernadez's career, and a nice recovery after he allowed six runs in 5 1/3 innings against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Fister allowed all four of his runs in an ugly first inning in Tuesday's 4-0 loss to the Angels, but pitched six scoreless innings thereafter. He'll be looking for his first win in June, as he's 0-3 with a 5.19 ERA this month.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan was excellent in a no-decision against the Cardinals on Thursday, allowing two earned runs on six hits and two walks while fanning two in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard continues to impress after coming back from an 18-month layoff. He has the lowest ERA in the AL since April 27 at 1.70 over his past nine starts and is coming off seven shutout innings of three-hit ball against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday against the Orioles, Marquis, who leads the Nationals in wins, battled his way through 5 1/3 innings with runners constantly on base. He allowed four runs on 12 hits.
away_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing 6-foot-7 rookie had a no-hitter for 5 2/3 innings Friday against the Phillies en route to a 4-2 win. He came out after six innings with two hits and one run for his 11th quality start in 14 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson has struggled out of the gate in his last two starts, and though he's calmed down and gone on to pitch at least six innings in each outing, he's walked away with a loss and a no-decision. He hasn't won a start since May 22.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann delivered a quality start in each of his past nine outings, and although he did not have his best stuff in his previous start against Baltimore, he showed something in battling through to hold the O's to two runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks took a line drive to the back of the head in his last outing, but stayed in the game and limited the D-backs to one earned run over seven innings for his third straight victory after starting 0-8.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny returns to his home state of Illinois, where the White Sox drafted him out of high school in 2000, but did not sign him. The left-hander struggled in his only start after a stint on the disabled list, allowing four runs in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Jake Peavy's return, Humber solidified his case to keep the six-man rotation in his last outing, allowing just two runs over 7 2/3 innings for the win. He hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of his 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday it looked as though Hernandez was going to take his ninth loss of the season, after he went just four-plus innings and allowing five runs -- four earned -- on 10 hits against the Mariners, but a ninth-inning rally took him off the hook.

home_pitcher_note: Santana's luck is all bad: eight runs of support in eight losses. He delivered another solid effort against the Marlins. Santana's fastball is alive and his slider is effective, but the home run ball has been the issue: 15 in 102 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan has been nothing short of dominant over his past six starts, when he has gone 3-0 with a 1.15 ERA. The sinker is consistently there, but he credits his improvement to command of his fastball after changing his pregame routine.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro continued a run of decent outings in Florida, but the bullpen was unable to protect his win. He is consistently getting into the seventh inning with his sinker and slider working effectively enough to keep the ball on the ground.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis took a no-hitter into the sixth inning his last time out, and although rookie pitcher Michael Pineda ended the bid, Marquis continued to dominate. He pitched eight scoreless frames, allowed three hits and struck out four against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Haren didn't have his best stuff, but he used his experience and resolve to hold the Dodgers to three runs on 10 hits in six innings Friday night. Haren has struggled in recent outings to put all of his pitches together, but he gets big outs.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann continues to show his consistency on the mound. On Friday, he pitched seven shutout innings and allowed six hits against the White Sox, earning a no-decision in Washington's  14-inning victory. It was his 10th consecutive quality start.

away_pitcher_note: Wang continues to make progress since returning from his shoulder woes. In his last start against the Dodgers, Wang received a no-decision and allowed four runs in six innings. He retired 10 out of the last 11 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Though Pelfrey walked two batters in the first inning Friday against the Cubs, he recovered to submit just his second quality start in his last seven tries. Next up are the Nats, who knocked him out in the fifth inning of a no-decision on Sept. 4.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock is expected to make his first Major League start on Wednesday, which means left-handers Tommy Milone and John Lannan will be pushed back a day.

home_pitcher_note: Schwinden replaces Miguel Batista in the rotation and pushes Chris Capuano's turn to Friday. The rookie right-hander allowed five runs on eight hits in five innings in his MLB debut last Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Milone made the second start of his career, lasting 5 2/3 innings and allowing three runs on eight hits. It was a much better outing than his Major League debut, in which he allowed four runs in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had one of his worst outings of the year and it proved costly, as the Nationals were pounded by the Astros at Nationals Park on Saturday night. Lannan ran into trouble in the third, when 11 men came to the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez is making his 30th start of the season. The veteran, who has hinted that he will retire after the year, has now gone 12 straight seasons with at least 10 wins. He is 2-0 with an 0.69 ERA in September. He is 5-3 (2.65) in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Making his second start of the season, Strasburg left after pitching three innings in his last outing. In the first inning, Strasburg threw 31 pitches and allowed an RBI single to Carlos Lee.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad last faced the Nationals on Aug. 3 at Washington, and he came out on the winning end of a 6-4 decision. That day, he gave up four runs on seven hits in five innings. He comes off a two-run, seven-hit no-decision in five innings at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Wang has not yielded more than four earned runs in nine starts since his return, though he also has completed six innings just four times. He is looking for his first win since Aug. 16, when he went 6 1/3 against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie lefty has shown signs of being a solid big leaguer. What he needs to show more of is consistency. Hand has lost four straight starts. In his last start, he led by a run in the sixth, but gave up a three-run homer to Atlanta's Brian McCann.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has five wins as a starting pitcher this season (one in May, June, July, August and September) and in those five wins, he's given up only three runs and 19 hits in 32 innings, with no more than one run allowed in any one of those wins.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander earned his first Major League victory in his last start Thursday, going 5 2/3 innings while keeping the Mets off-balance with an array of offspeed pitches. "I'm glad to have [the win] under my belt now," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee was just one strike from throwing his seventh shutout of the season last week in a victory against Florida, but he allowed a homer to Jose Lopez in the ninth to tie the game. Lee is 6-0 with a 0.56 ERA in his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Not pitching in a while didn't have any ill effects on Detwiler on Monday against New York. He didn't allow a run and gave up one hit over the first five innings, but he couldn't get out of the sixth inning.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed six hits, one run, three walks and struck out five in last Friday's loss to the St. Louis Cardinals at Citizens Bank Park. He remains a National League Rookie of the Year candidate, although the Phillies have lost his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan remains in search of his elusive 10th victory, which would set a career high. After a promising start, Lannan has dropped six of his past seven starts. In his last outing against Florida on Friday, he allowed three runs in six innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Fans had wondered who might be the Phillies' No. 4 starter in the postseason, but Oswalt answered those questions in Saturday's victory over St. Louis. He allowed five hits and struck out seven in seven scoreless innings to help clinch the division.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie will be making his second Major League start after earning his first career victory in his last start Wednesday. In that game, Peacock held the Mets to just one run on six hits in 6 1/3 innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals' ace is still searching for his first victory this season, but Strasburg's last outing was his best since returning to the Majors. He allowed one run on four hits over six innings against the Marlins on September 17.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson changed the position of his heel on the pitching rubber before his last start, and it helped the righty shut out the Mets over eight strong innings. He had been 1-3 with a 5.06 ERA in four starts before making the adjustment.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous outing, Wang pitched 6 2/3 innings -- his longest outing since June 2008 -- allowing three runs on six hits with a season-high five strikeouts to pick up the win.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy took a no-decision list time out against the Mets after allowing four runs in 4 1/3 innings of work. It was the most runs he's allowed since giving up five to the Rockies on July 19. The Braves have lost each of the righty's last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler pitched 7 1/3 innings, allowing just three hits against the Phillies. The key to success was simple: He kept the ball down in the strike zone. He had 10 groundouts and threw just 81 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Minor was damaged by three home runs as he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings and got a no-decision against the Marlins on Monday. The rookie left-hander has gone 5-0 with a 3.66 ERA in his past nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez lost his last start against the Braves after allowing a three-run second inning. He went just five frames and threw 83 pitches. He is 8 2/3 innings shy of his first 200-inning season. Sanchez is tied for seventh in the NL with 191 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Milone pitched six scoreless innings, allowing four hits, striking out two and walking none. It marked the third time in four starts Milone didn't walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez has pitched 25 consecutive scoreless innings, setting the franchise record for a starter. Over his past 11 games, he has gone 6-2 with a 1.54 ERA, which ranks third in the Majors. He pitched a complete-game shutout last time against the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan earned his career-high 10th win on Wednesday. It wasn't his best outing, as he allowed three runs on eight hits in five innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad, a South Florida native, will make the final start of the season and the last game for the team as the Florida Marlins at Sun Life Stadium. At home, he's 3-7 (5.04 ERA). He had a strong seven-inning start vs. Milwaukee in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: In his worst start of the year, Strasburg found himself in trouble in the first inning, throwing 38 pitches and allowing three runs -- two earned. Strasburg settled down, retiring nine out of the last 10 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Dempster's fourth Opening Day start, second with the Cubs. He's hoping for a better start. He had a 9.58 ERA in six April outings in 2011. He lost the season opener in 2011 to the Pirates, giving up six runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Strasburg's first Opening Day assignment. He missed most of last season because he was recovering from Tommy John surgery. He had a 1.50 ERA in five September games. He is expected to pitch no more than 160 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza begins his second season with the Cubs. The right-hander is coming off his second straight 10-win season. Garza hopes to get a little more support. He left with the lead but did not factor in the decision seven times last season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was 16-12 with a 3.12 ERA and had 197 strikeouts in 202 innings last season. His 8.8 strikeouts per nine innings ranked third among all qualifying southpaws. His 31 wins over the past two seasons ranks fourth among lefties.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija has wanted to be a starter and won a spot in the rotation with a strong spring. The former Notre Dame wide receiver was exclusively a reliever last year, and last started in the big leagues in 2010, when he started three September games.
away_pitcher_note: Unlike last year, Zimmermann will not be on an innings limit and is expected to pitch at least 200. He has lost twice and allowed 12 earned runs in 18 innings against the Cubs over the past three seasons.

home_pitcher_note: The fourth starter in name only at this point, Pelfrey followed a poor 2011 with an equally poor Spring Training. The front office will be watching closely as Pelfrey faces the Nats, whom he held to a total of three runs over two starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson went a combined 12-9 with a 3.79 ERA last season for the White Sox and Cardinals, registering a fourth consecutive double-digit win total. In the same four seasons, Jackson is one of 20 starters to average at least 12 wins and 200 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Using Pilates to improve his conditioning over the winter, Gee parlayed his improved shape into a strong spring. In four starts against the Nats last season, Gee finished 2-0 with a 3.60 ERA. He was also 7-3 with a 3.17 ERA in 15 games at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler is now the fifth starter in the rotation. He will probably get three or four starts before returning to the bullpen as a long reliever. Chien-Ming Wang is expected to be back with the Nationals in late April or early May.

home_pitcher_note: Due to a scheduling quirk, Santana will have an extra day of rest for six of his first seven starts. That should not change the fact that Santana will still be on a strict pitch count for much of April, likely no higher than 90 on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg pitched seven superb innings in his first-career Opening Day start against the Cubs, allowing a run on five hits and striking out five batters. The run scored in the fourth inning, when Ian Stewart scored on a single by Marlon Byrd.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez made his Washington and National League debut and had an outing he would probably like to forget. Gonzalez lasted 3 2/3 innings, allowed four runs on seven hits, struck out six batters and walked three against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Latos had a rough Reds debut on Saturday. He allowed four runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings. Latos criticized himself afterwards for trying to be too fine in his debut before a soldout crowd. Latos walked two and struck out four over 81 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann pitched seven solid innings and allowed two runs  -- one earned -- on six hits against the Cubs on Sunday. He struck out four and walked none.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo was feeling strong and had decent velocity throughout his start vs. the Marlins on Sunday. Trouble came in the seventh when he hit Greg Dobbs on the knee with a pitch. It led to a three-run rally and a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander Edwin Jackson made his Nats debut last Monday, lasting five innings, allowing three runs on four hits, striking out six batters and walking two against the Mets. Jackson was given a 3-0 lead, but the Mets tied the game in the fourth.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey was tagged for three two-out home runs vs. the Cardinals on Monday before settling into a decent performance in a 7-1 loss. He admitted that he got too passive after getting two quick outs.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Detwiler pitched five scoreless innings, allowing two hits -- both coming in the first -- and struck out six batters and walked one. At one point, Detwiler retired 10 straight hitters with four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake pitched well vs. St. Louis on Tuesday, but made three mistakes that hurt, two of which resulted in home runs by Carlos Beltran and David Freese. "Leake pitched an outstanding game outside of a couple pitches," manager Dusty Baker said.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday against the Mets, Strasburg pitched six shutout innings, allowed two hits, struck out nine batters and walked three. He also threw a career-high 108 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Weiland, acquired from the Red Sox along with Jed Lowrie in a winter trade, was rocked for eight hits and four runs in five innings in his first start with Houston on Tuesday against Atlanta. He has never faced Washington.

home_pitcher_note: This past Thursday, Gonzalez started the game for the Nationals and showed why they traded four prospects to the A's to acquire his services last December. He was outstanding, pitching seven superb innings, allowing two hits and not walking a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez held the Rockies to no earned runs in 6 1/3 innings on Opening Day, and gave up three earned runs in five innings Wednesday against Atlanta. The Astros have committed four errors in each of his two starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Zimmermann had another superb outing, pitching seven innings and allowing one run on three hits in a no-decision vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell fell behind in the count too much in his most recent start Friday in Miami, allowing seven hits and four runs in four innings. He was terrific in his first start of the season in which he threw seven scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Jackson gave the bullpen the rest it needed by tossing a complete game -- his first of 2012 and fifth of his career -- in his home debut, allowing one run on two hits. He fanned nine and walked one, with 67 of his 92 pitches strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Norris has delivered quality games in both of his starts this year, allowing six hits and four runs (three earned) in six innings Saturday against the Marlins. He's 1-0 with a 2.63 ERA in two career starts against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals didn't get a stellar performance from left-hander Ross Detwiler on Sunday afternoon against the Reds. Detwiler ended up throwing five innings and allowing five runs -- one earned -- on six hits in an 8-5 loss.
away_pitcher_note: It hasn't always been pretty, but Zambrano is getting the job done. He's ended up with two no-decisions in games Miami led entering the ninth. He did walk six in his last outing, but allowed one run against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Strasburg was solid vs. Houston in his third start of the season. He lasted six innings, allowed two runs on six hits, struck out five hitters and walked one. Strasburg threw 93 pitches, 61 strikes.
away_pitcher_note: In 17 career starts against the Nationals, Sanchez is 7-0 with a 2.06 ERA. The right-hander has thrown well in two starts this year. He struck out seven in a no-decision vs. the Astros. He has 10 strikeouts in 12 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Richard had success with offspeed pitches down in the zone, getting seven ground-ball outs in three of his first four innings Wednesday. But his fastball was up and flat, leading to five runs in the second inning and a total of eight runs on 10 hits.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Gonzalez, who picked up his first National League victory, pitched seven innings, allowed two hits, struck out eight batters and walked two. At one point in the game, Gonzalez retired 13 straight Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Wieland pitched considerably better in his second Major League start, allowing one run in six innings with seven strikeouts. He allowed three hits in the first inning and two thereafter. He got more mileage out of his curveball this time out.
away_pitcher_note: For the third start in a row, Zimmermann didn't get the run support he needed, but he was solid, pitching seven innings and allowing one run on four hits against the Astros. The Nats have scored a total of two runs for Zimmermann.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez, still looking for his first win with the Padres, took a two-hit shutout into the seventh inning of his last start against the Phillies, but he gave up three runs. Walks have been an issue (15 in 23 innings), but he's mostly pitched well.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's last outing was the antithesis of his previous start, when he pitched a two-hitter against the Reds. On Thursday night, Jackson pitched five innings and allowed five runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw had that Cy Young look about him pitching seven scoreless innings on three hits in Houston, with nine strikeouts. The Nationals should provide a better test for the lefty, who has been nearly unbeatable at home since he joined the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler was outstanding Friday, throwing six shutout innings, allowing three hits, striking out a season-high seven batters and walking one. The only time Detwiler was in any kind of trouble was in the second inning.

home_pitcher_note: The club insists Billingsley's 3 1/3-inning outing in Sunday's blowout loss in Houston had nothing to do with the sore groin muscle that bothered him in his previous start. He was roughed up for nine runs (five earned).
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg pitched six shutout innings against the Marlins on Saturday, and he allowed four hits, struck out six batters and walked one over 94 pitches. Strasburg wasn't in any serious trouble throughout his start.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano pitched out of numerous jams against the Braves in a seven-inning outing that helped rest a tired bullpen. Capuano still had four walks, two of them leading off innings, which seems to be an indication when he's not challenging hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed six scoreless innings and won his second straight start Tuesday in San Diego, and has not allowed a run in his last three outings, a streak 20 innings. Gonzalez has struck out at least six in each of his four starts for Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann tossed six innings against the Padres to earn his first win in his last start. He allowed one run on four hits, striking out six and not issuing a walk, and also drove in a run with a single.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Phillies in his last outing. He's lost his last two starts while allowing eight earned runs in 11 innings. In his first two starts, he allowed two runs in 13 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rebounding nicely from his previous start, in which he gave up five runs in the first inning, Jackson threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Padres, marking the eighth time in 19 games that a Washington starter had blanked the opposition.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off his third career shutout and perhaps his finest outing as a pro, as he handcuffed the Marlins in Miami. He lost his only start at Nationals Park last year after allowing four runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler pitched six innings, allowing three runs on five hits against the Dodgers on Friday. He had a tough time stopping Matt Kemp and Andre Either, who went a combined 4-for-6 against the southpaw.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy said after his last outing that he's felt like he's had his "C stuff" in each of his starts this year. The right-hander left his outing against the Marlins with a 2-0 lead, but the bullpen was unable to close it out.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg was dominating against the Dodgers last Saturday.  He pitched seven innings, allowed one run on five hits, and struck out nine batters without walking a batter. Strasburg, who is on an innings limit of 160 this season, threw 101 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick bounced back from a rough start to allow two earned runs in six innings in Sunday's 5-1 loss to the Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He also tied a career high with seven strikeouts. Kendrick is pitching in place of Cliff Lee, who is injured.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lost his pitch control in the sixth inning vs. L.A., walking three batters and allowing two to score on a James Loney single after cruising for the first five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Worley allowed five hits and one run, with two walks and five strikeouts in seven innings Monday against the Cubs. He is 13-4 with a 2.81 ERA in 26 starts since last season. He has allowed just two earned runs in his last 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann allowed four runs -- three earned -- in 6 1/3 innings Tuesday. In Zimmermann's five starts, the Nationals have averaged fewer than three runs per game. Zimmermann said he doesn't feel he has to be perfect every time he pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed six hits, two runs, two walks and struck out six in six innings Tuesday against the Braves. He hopes to go a little deeper in what could be an important game in the series finale against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett is coming off the worst outing of his career. He gave up 12 earned runs in 2 2/3 innings in a 12-3 loss on Wednesday. He allowed just two earned runs over 13 innings during his first two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson allowed four earned runs in six innings against the D-backs on Wednesday. He allowed eight hits, walked two batters and struck out three in the game. Jackson picked up his third no-decison of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard fanned 11 in five innings in St. Louis. The lefty struck out seven in a row at one point. He gave up two runs in the first, then shut the Cards down on two hits over his final four frames. He has won two in a row after losing four straight.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler allowed a run in 6 1/3 innings against the Diamondbacks on Thursday. Since he was picked over John Lannan to be the fifth starter at the end of Spring Training, Detwiler has been almost unhittable.

home_pitcher_note: Correia makes his 15th PNC Park start as a Pirate, still looking for third win at home. Dating to 2011, has won one of his last nine starts. Location spoiled the good stuff in his last two starts (eight runs in 11 1/3 innings vs. Reds and Braves.)
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg lasted six innings against the Phillies on Friday, allowing three hits and three earned runs -- all coming on homers -- while striking out four and walking one in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Leake pitched fairly well against the Pirates on Saturday, allowing only three runs on four hits in seven innings. All of the runs scored against Leake were on homers, which has been his main problem all season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was solid against the Phillies on Saturday, allowing a run in seven innings. He even had a double that helped the Nationals score three runs early in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Latos, who was feeling ill at the beginning of the game, finally turned in a dominant outing in Sunday's win over the Pirates. He allowed just two hits while striking out a career-high 11 in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann was defeated in Sunday's loss to the Phillies, allowing three earned runs in six innings. It didn't help that he didn't have his fastball command in the game, and that's what caused him to walk the four batters.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was brilliant vs. the Nats on April 14, with 7 1/3 scoreless frames and three hits allowed. He was out of gas after 94 pitches and lost a chance at a win on the 'pen's watch. He's been very good at using all of his pitches and changing speeds.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson was done in by the long ball in the bottom of the fourth vs. the Pirates on Tuesday.  That proved to be Jackson's only bad inning.  He ended up going seven innings, allowing two runs on three hits, striking out five batters and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates scored three runs in the third inning on Wednesday off Detwiler, who lasted six innings and allowed seven hits in his second loss of the season. It was his fourth quality start in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer makes his first start of the season against the Nationals. He might have been the Opening Day starter had he not come down with a strained right elbow late in Spring Training. He has a 3.15 ERA over the last two seasons in 63 games.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was almost unhittable as the Nationals defeated the Pirates on Thursday night. In his six innings on the mound, Strasburg struck out 13 batters and walked three. At one point, he struck out seven straight hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Bass allowed one earned run in 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Rockies but took the loss. He struck out four and walked one. He's mostly pitched well since moving into the starting rotation last month and his command has gotten better.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez picked up his fourth win in five decisions by striking out nine in five innings in a win at Cincinnati. Gonzalez threw 115 pitches and walked four in his shortest outing since going 3 2/3 innings April 7 at Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard gets his Mulligan against Washington, the team he was facing last week when ousted after an inning with back spasms. The Pirates will keep a close eye on the lefty to make sure he doesn't alter his normal delivery to favor his back.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann picked up his second win of the season by going seven innings and striking out nine in a 2-1 victory at Cincinnati. He lowered his ERA to 2.14 and has allowed just 37 hits in 46 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald will try to extend a stretch of domination that has seen him ring up almost twice as many strikeouts (33) as hits allowed (18) in his last four starts, covering 29 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson allowed three earned runs in a no-decision against the Reds this past Sunday. Two of those runs came on solo homers by Joey Votto. Jackson is looking for his first victory since April 14, when he pitched a complete game against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta took a pounding in his most recent start, posting season worsts of seven runs, 10 hits and only 3 2/3 innings pitched. Arrieta has the stuff to be successful, but must regain command of his fastball and keep his pitches down in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler started for Washington and had his toughest start of the season. He pitched five innings and allowed five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel skipped his May 10 start to rest a sore right knee, and as a result he fatigued quickly in his next outing. After throwing three shutout frames Tuesday vs. the Yanks, he allowed five runs on five hits in the next two-plus frames.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg faced his hometown team, the Padres, for the first time in his career on Tuesday afternoon. It turned out to be one of the worst outings of his career as he allowed four runs over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old rookie has been solid in all seven of his starts, allowing no more than three earned runs in any outing. Now, he'll try his hand against the National League for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed three hits and one earned run in six innings Wednesday in a victory over the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He has a 2.12 ERA in his past three starts this season and a 2.96 ERA in 13 starts dating to last season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez leads the National League in strikeouts with 60 and will make his first start on the road against a divisional rival. In his most previous outing, Gonzalez allowed three runs in seven innings of a win over the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay picked up his first win since April 16 in Thursday's victory over the Cubs. He allowed seven hits, three runs and struck out four in seven innings. Halladay hopes Thursday was the beginning of some positive momentum for him.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann struggled in his most previous outing against the Pirates, allowing a season-high four runs and seven hits with six strikeout and one walk through six innings. The Nats have scored fewer than three runs in seven of his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole Hamels continued his strong season with a win against the Red Sox on Friday night. The lefty allowed three runs on six hits, struck out nine and walked just one in his sixth consecutive victory.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson had one of his best outings in Friday's 2-1 loss to Baltimore. He allowed just the one run on five hits and one walk while striking out eight over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson tossed a gem against the Rays in his last outing on Sunday to pick up his third victory. He allowed four hits and two walks, while fanning three, over 7 2/3 scoreless innings in his 99-pitch outing.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler was roughed up by the Orioles on Saturday, allowing six runs in five innings. Even worse, he has allowed 10 runs in his past 10 innings. Davey Johnson said Detwiler is still in the rotation despite having two bad starts.

home_pitcher_note: The long ball has been Minor's nemesis in the last month. He has allowed multiple home runs in four of his past five starts, including giving up four solo shots to Cincinnati in his last start. Still, his ERA dropped after that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Despite having forearm tightness, Strasburg is expected to make his next start on Saturday against the Braves. He's coming off a game in which he hit his first Major League home run against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy suffered his first loss since his first start of the season his last time out at Cincinnati. He gave up three home runs for the first time in his career. He had allowed just one home run in 54 innings to begin the season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Gonzalez pitched six scoreless innings, struck out nine hitters and held the Phillies to three hits in a 2-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano had allowed three runs or fewer in seven straight starts until Colorado put up seven in five innings in his last outing. Zambrano lost at Washington on April 20, giving up one run on two hits in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Benefiting from the run support against the Phillies on Tuesday, Zimmermann threw six innings, allowing one run on seven hits. He even helped himself with the bat, going 2-for-3 and scoring the Nationals' first run.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Giants, Sanchez endured his worst start of the year. After notching quality starts in his first eight outings, he gave up five runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. He walked two and fanned seven, but two wild pitches proved costly.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson had another quality outing, but ended up losing his second game of the season on Wednesday. He pitched seven innings, allowed three runs on seven hits, and struck out four batters against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson's string of three straight starts of seven innings was snapped in his last outing. JJ gave up three runs in five innings in a no-decision against the Giants on Friday. He gave up nine hits and threw 90 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Nationals manager Davey Johnson has decided that Wang will be the team's fifth starter, while left-hander Ross Detwiler will be sent to the bullpen as a long man. It didn't help Detwiler that he had three bad outings before the move was made.

away_pitcher_note: Since the start of 2016 season, Roark is 4-0 with a 1.87 ERA and 0.97 WHIP against the Phillies. He has not given up more than three earned runs in a start since July 29.
