away_pitcher_note: After recording a 6.62 ERA in his first 10 second-half starts, Nova has allowed only three earned runs in 11 1/3 innings over his last two outings. He will look to end the season on a high note in his career-high 31st start.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Strasburg’s final start of the regular season, a milestone only for the fact that he is healthy at the end of a season. The Nats limited him to 83 pitches in his most recent outing.
away_pitcher_note: Cole enters his final start needing 2 1/3 innings and 11 strikeouts to reach 200 in each category. Cole has not been particularly strong of late, however, allowing 14 runs in 16 2/3 innings over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: As he completes another season that will put him on the cusp of the NL Cy Young Award, Scherzer currently owns the lowest ERA of his career. He will almost certainly reach 200 innings in this outing in his final tuneup before the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon will finish a trying year by making his 25th and final start. After a brutal second-half slump in which he posted a 7.17 ERA in 11 outings, he has allowed three runs over 10 innings with 10 strikeouts his last two times out.

home_pitcher_note: This start wraps up what has been one of Gonzalez’s best seasons. He could finish with the lowest ERA of his career and reach 200 innings for the first time since 2011. That could earn him consideration for the NL Cy Young Award.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will make his fourth start as the Pirates end their season in Washington. His Triple-A success has followed him to Pittsburgh, as he has posted a 2.37 ERA in 19 innings over his last four appearances (three starts).

home_pitcher_note: In his only start against the Cubs this year, Gonzalez tossed six innings of one-run ball but took the loss. In four career postseason starts, he's posted a 3.93 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Roark pitched much better in the second half (3.90 ERA, .223 BA against) than the first (5.27, .278). He lasted 4 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on seven hits and three walks in his only career postseason start in last fall’s NLDS vs. the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Romano came into spring with an inside track for a rotation spot and didn't give it up with a consistently strong camp.  Over his final eight starts of 2017, he had a 3.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg will start the Nats’ home opener looking to build off a solid first start of the year, in which he struck out seven and limited the Reds to three runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Holding the Cardinals to one run in 5 2/3 innings in his season debut, deGrom improved to 18-8 with a 1.98 ERA -- baseball's lowest in more than a century -- in day games. His next start will also be a matinee: the Nationals' home opener.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez filled up the strike zone in his first outing of the year during six innings of one-run ball with seven strikeouts in a victory against the Reds. It was encouraging start for him in a contract year coming off a strong 2017 season.

away_pitcher_note: Harvey’s debut wasn’t perfect, but his five scoreless innings vs.  Philadelphia gave the Mets hope for a successful season. He’ll return to the mound at Nationals Park, with the spotlight shining brighter in a nationally televised Sunday night game.

away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has seemingly benefited from the subdued windup he developed over the offseason.  Limiting the number of moving body parts has improved his command and allowed for more consistency throughout his four-pitch arsenal.

away_pitcher_note: McCarthy’s slider hasn’t been as effective as he had hoped, but the veteran has commanded his fastball consistently enough to work into the sixth inning in his first two starts. He limited the  Nationals to two runs over seven innings in June.

away_pitcher_note: Bettis led all Rockies starters with a 2.53 ERA through the club's first two turns through the rotation, most recently holding the Braves to one earned run and four hits. He has yet to exceed 88 pitches this season.

home_pitcher_note: If Scherzer can reach double-digit strikeouts again, he would become one of 17 pitchers in MLB history to record three 10+ strikeout games in his team's first 15 games. He is coming off a shutout in his last start.

away_pitcher_note: Anderson is coming off consecutive starts against the Padres in which he gave up just two earned runs over 12 innings. Take out a rough showing in Arizona on March 30, and Anderson has a 1.30 ERA over his past six starts dating back to September.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler pitched well enough in his season debut to earn at least one more start, striking out seven Marlins over seven innings of one-run ball in Miami. He did so featuring a new delivery, keeping his elbow higher to reduce stress on it.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has been masterful in 15 career starts at Citi Field, going 10-1 with a 1.69 ERA. The southpaw has held the Mets to a .167 batting average and just five home runs in 95 2/3 innings at their home stadium.

away_pitcher_note: Roark is 7-2 with a 3.13 ERA in 18 career outings (12 starts) vs. the Mets. He settled for a no-decision the last time he faced them, giving up five earned runs in five innings on April 8 at Nationals Park.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu goes for his third straight win as he puts his undefeated record on the line against one of the most explosive offenses in the Majors. Ryu went six innings his last time out against the Padres, allowing two runs on three hits with nine K's.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg is 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA and 26 K's in 26 1/3 innings across his first four starts. Last June, Strasburg was outdueled by Clayton Kershaw in a 2-1 loss.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson took over for A.J. Cole as the fifth starter on April 16 and he received a no-decision vs. the Mets. Hellickson went 4 2/3 innings and threw 61 of his 88 pitches for strikes. This will mark his first career outing at Dodger Stadium.

away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is off to a fast start in what will be a contract year. Through four starts, his ERA and strikeout percentage are both even better than they were last season. He owns a 3.06 ERA in 12 career starts against the Giants.

away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is off to another spectacular start in 2018. He finished his last start leading the league in strikeouts with 47 in 33 innings. He has performed well against the Giants in his two most recent starts with 21 strikeouts and just one walk.

away_pitcher_note: Ray is still looking to regain the dominant form he had for most of 2017. Falling behind hitters has been an issue for him. He got a no-decision in his last start against the Phillies, striking out 11 over 4 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Taillon is looking to get back on track after a pair of rough outings. He's allowed 12 runs on 14 hits in 5 1/3 innings over his last two starts, both losses. He held the Nats to one run on four hits in seven innings last Sept. 30 in Washington.

away_pitcher_note: Kuhl has made consecutive six-inning starts, both wins. He tied a career high with eight strikeouts on Wednesday against the Tigers. He threw six shutout innings, allowing only one hit, in his only career start at Nationals Park on July 17, 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg has lost his past two starts despite allowing only 11 hits in 13 1/3 innings. His 2-3 record is partly due to the home run ball. Strasburg has allowed seven homers across his six starts, including at least one in all but one of his outings.
away_pitcher_note: Nova made his best start of the season Thursday vs. the Tigers, firing eight scoreless innings with five strikeouts. He has not walked a batter since April 4, going without a walk in his last four outings. He posted a 3.27 ERA in five April starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson held the D-backs to two runs, both on solo homers, over 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision on Saturday. He is 3-1 with a 2.86 ERA in five career starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Entering his last outing, Gonzalez asked for more leeway on the mound from his manager to allow him to pitch deeper into games. He responded by throwing seven innings of one-run ball with eight strikeouts to lower his ERA to 2.67.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta struggled a bit in his last start Saturday against the Braves, but he has otherwise been one of the team’s biggest surprises. He has struck out 34 and walked just seven in 33 innings. He has posted a 2.79 ERA in his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Roark has been steady for the Nats this season, with a 3.55 ERA through six starts, and he is coming off one of his best performances. He threw seven innings of two-run ball in a victory over the Pirates in his most recent outing.
away_pitcher_note: Will the real Velasquez please stand up? He had a three-start stretch last month in which he posted a 2.41 ERA, striking out 20 and walking three. But he has allowed 10 runs in 8 2/3 innings in two starts since.

home_pitcher_note: After winning back-to-back National League Cy Young awards, Scherzer was named the NL Pitcher of the Month for April. He has posted a 1.79 ERA, and his 65 strikeouts are among the best in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta figures he has one or two really bad starts a year. He hopes Monday’s in Miami was one of them. He allowed six runs in just 3 2/3 innings, making it easily his worst start with the Phillies. He had 1.82 ERA in his first four starts.

home_pitcher_note: With less velocity and more precision, Ross is a different pitcher from his first stint with the Padres. This version might be even better. He struck out 9 Giants on Tuesday, using his nasty slider to induce 12 swings and misses.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg picked up a win for the first time in nearly a month in his last outing, when he struck out a season-high 11 Pittsburgh batters over seven innings. He’ll be making his fourth career big league start in his home city of San Diego on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander was roughed up for seven runs in his last time out. He’s off to a rough start to the season, and he pointed to his command as the biggest reason why. Richard has walked at least three in each of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie lefty battled sheets of pouring rain in Monterrey in his last start, and he allowed three runs over five innings. Lucchesi will be thrilled to return home where he has a 3.08 ERA and 28 strikeouts in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has allowed only one run over his last 12 frames to lower his ERA to 2.33 after seven starts. If he can replicate that across a whole season, he has a chance to surpass the career-best 2.89 ERA he posted in 2012, his first year in D.C.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off his best back-to-back outings of the season, giving up a run in 5 2/3 innings against the Astros on Saturday and two runs over six innings to the Dodgers on April 30.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Roark faced the D-backs came last July when he struck out a season-high 11 batters. He extended himself to 115 pitches in his most recent outing and has thrown over the 100-pitch mark in his most recent four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Koch hasn't given up more than two earned runs in each of his four starts and is coming off an outing Sunday when he gave up just one run in 6 1/3 innings in a victory over the Astros.

away_pitcher_note: It's almost as if Strasburg has yet to truly get on a roll this season and yet he still enters this start with a 3.52 ERA and 59 strikeouts, which ranked third in the National League at the end of his last start.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson has been all the Nats could ask for since joining their rotation as the fifth starter. He takes the mound after flirting with a perfect game in his most recent outing. He finished with a season-high 6 2/3 innings and struck out eight.

away_pitcher_note: Tanaka is unbeaten over his last four outings, going 2-0 with 3 quality starts and a 3.38 ERA. He has faced the Nationals just once, earning the win after firing seven innings of one-run ball in June 2015. He's coming off a no-decision vs. Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Roark tossed seven innings of one-run ball in his most recent start against the D-backs and has held opposing hitters to a .197 batting average. He has bounced back after posting a career-high ERA a year ago to post a 3.33 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Stripling looks to reverse his trend against the Nationals. He is 0-1 lifetime in two relief outings against Washington, allowing four runs in 1 2/3 innings. The righty is 0-1 with a 4.05 ERA as a starting pitcher this season.

away_pitcher_note: Hill went 5 2/3 and 98 pitches against the Reds Sunday before leaving with a left middle finger blister but is back in action against the Nationals and seeking his first win since April 1.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps Strasburg is starting to hit his stride after winning three straight starts, with a 2.61 ERA over that span. He tossed seven innings of two-run ball with 10 strikeouts in a loss to the Dodgers on April 21.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez makes his first start of the season after making a relief appearance last week in Washington. This is an important year for Velasquez, who has been inconsistent as a starter. With the expectations higher than ever, he needs to produce.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez had his season debut cut short after he took a line drive off his hip, which left a bruise, but he doesn’t expect it will be an issue in this start. This will be his fourth consecutive start against the Phillies, dating back to last season.

home_pitcher_note: Nola has not been sharp in his first two starts, allowing seven runs in nine innings, walking seven and striking out 10. It is no reason to panic, but Nola's start against the Nats is worth watching closely because he is such a key to the season.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg has allowed eight hits or fewer in his past 53 starts dating to Sept. 7, 2016, the longest streak in franchise history and tied for the third-longest active streak in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta is looking to put together his first quality start, allowing 17 hits and eight runs in 9 2/3 innings. He has arguably the best stuff on the team, so expectations for a breakout season are high. Maybe it begins Wednesday against the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson's first start of 2019. He had a brief stint in the bullpen to begin the season, where he appeared in one game, tossing two innings and giving up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Patrick Corbin will make his third start for the Nationals -- but his first against any team other than the Mets. He recorded a quality start in each of those first two outings against New York, but he settled for a no-decision in both.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has thrown six innings in each of his first two starts of the season. After a scoreless outing in his debut, Williams allowed four runs (three earned) in his last outing. He enjoyed a breakout season last year with a 3.11 ERA over 31 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez will take on Pennsylania's other MLB team after facing the Phillies in each of his first two outings. He came within an out of a quality start in his last outing, but was ultimately done in by a pair of home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Archer is scheduled to start after he appealed his five-game suspension for his role in a benches-clearing incident against the Reds. Archer threw six innings in that start when he struck out seven and surrendered three runs. He threw five scoreless in his 2019 debut against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer admittedly felt sore after taking a comebacker off his right leg in his last outing, but he figures to benefit from extra days of rest, thanks to Thursday's off-day switching starts with Anibal Sanchez. He has 28 strikeouts in 19 innings through his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon will start after lasting just two innings in his last start against the Cubs. Taillon avoided serious injury after being hit on the head by a line drive that had an exit velocity of 102 mph off the bat of Anthony Rizzo. He allowed six unearned runs in the second inning of that game.

home_pitcher_note: When Strasburg made his Major League debut in 2010, Ivan “Pudge” Rodriguez, the father of opposing starter Dereck, was behind the plate as Strasburg's catcher. In three starts this year, Strasburg has struck out 20 with seven walks.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was charged with the tough-luck loss after giving up two runs over seven innings against the Padres on Wednesday. He made his only career start against the Nationals on June 9, 2018, when he surrendered five runs over 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson’s first start of the season could not have gone any smoother. He tossed six shutout innings on Wednesday night in Philadelphia with six strikeouts and four walks. The Nats went 4-1 in Hellickson's home starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off his best start in over a year, as he struck out seven over seven shutout innings against the Rockies on Thursday. He is 2-8 with a 4.63 ERA in 17 career appearances against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin’s most recent outing was his best in a Nationals uniform, limiting the Pirates to one run in seven innings with 11 strikeouts. In his last seven starts against the Giants, Corbin is 4-1 with a 1.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz gave up two runs over five innings against the Rockies in his start on Friday. He has yet to pitch more than five innings in any of his first three starts this year. Pomeranz is 2-0 with a 2.19 ERA in two starts against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Smith has impressed. He isn't allowing much hard contact or many base runners. His WHIP is 0.88, and his hard-hit percentage is 18.4, top five among all pitchers. The lefty has 21 strikeouts in 17 innings. He's gone six innings in consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez started his career with the Marlins, and in seven seasons with Miami, he posted a 3.75 ERA. He has pitched five games (four starts) against the club that he debuted with, and owns a 2.91 ERA with 19 strikeouts and seven walks.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins have lost all four of Urena's starts, but the right-hander was much more effective in his last start, a no-decision against the Phillies. Urena fanned seven in seven innings that afternoon. Batters are hitting .390 off his sinker.
away_pitcher_note: In his three most recent starts against the Marlins, Scherzer has given up just one earned run in 21 innings (0.43 ERA). He has also guided Washington to a victory in each of his last seven starts against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: In 29 career starts, Richards has 151 strikeouts in 149 innings. He looks to rebound from his shortest outing of the season, 4 2/3 innings, allowing five runs on four hits with just three strikeouts in a loss to the Cubs. Chicago mostly did not chase Richards' changeup, which he throws 36.1 percent of the time this season.
away_pitcher_note: When Strasburg completes one inning Sunday, he will match Gio Gonzalez for the most innings thrown as a member of the Nationals. Strasburg has not been his usual dominant self to start the season, but the Nats are confident he will eventually regain his form.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was activated from the injured list to make the start after left knee inflammation had affected his performance.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson’s first career start at Coors Field. He has transformed himself into a very consistent starter since joining the Nats, giving up three runs or fewer in all but two of his 21 career starts in D.C.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman, called up from Triple-A, was 0-2 with a 13.89 ERA over 11 2/3 innings in three games with Albuquerque.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin has plenty of experience pitching at Coors Field, but not much success. In 11 games (10 starts) in Colorado, he owns a 6.55 ERA and 1.655 WHIP. Overall, he has made 21 starts against the Rockies in his career, the second most against any team.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez battled through five innings while suffering from pain from an infected tooth in his last start, an eventual Rockies win over the Phillies. The tooth has been pulled, and at 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA he can smile easily.
away_pitcher_note: In two career starts at Coors Field, Sanchez owns a 3.46 ERA with 13 strikeouts and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer tweaked his left intercostal muscle getting out of the way of a foul ball in the dugout in Miami last weekend, but he is on track to start against the Padres. In his last start, he was hit hard for seven runs (six earned) on 11 hits against Miami.
away_pitcher_note: There were questions as to whether Strahm could handle a transition to the rotation. Those questions aren't so persistent anymore. Strahm worked eight innings of one-run ball against Cincinnati on Friday -- easily the longest outing of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg is coming off a tremendous start against the Marlins during which he dominated Miami for eight scoreless innings, yielding only two hits while walking two and striking out 11.
away_pitcher_note: Lauer has lost consecutive starts in which he received little help from the Padres' offense. He's done some nice things with his curveball, but hitters -- specifically righties -- are squaring up his other pitches a bit too frequently.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson endured his first subpar start of the season in his last outing, giving up five runs on nine hits over five innings in his first start at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Joey Lucchesi's signature pitch is a mixture of a changeup and curveball that he calls a "churve." He's gotten more swings-and-misses than ever before over his last couple starts. Lucchesi threw it 38 times and induced 12 whiffs vs. Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: The Nats have to be thrilled with the start from their biggest free agent acquisition in Corbin, who has been their most consistent starter. In each of his last five starts, he has thrown at least six innings and given up three runs or less.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha missed his turn the last time through the rotation due to a bout of left knee tendinitis. But he felt fine throwing a side session on Friday, and hopes to pick up where he left off in his six-inning quality start on April 17 vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is looking to get back on track after getting roughed up at Coors Field in his most recent outing. He faced the Cardinals last September and struck out a season-high nine batters with no walks in six innings of two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has finished six innings in three of his five starts, a good sign for a 37-year-old coming off multiple arm injuries. On a personal note, this start will be special since it'll be his first since finalizing the adoption of a son, Caleb.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer, a St. Louis native, has recorded 14.85 strikeouts per nine innings in his last three starts against the Cardinals, dating back to April 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Mikolas continues to be bitten by the long ball, a somewhat surprising development since he allowed just 16 homers in 32 starts last year. This season, Mikolas has already been tagged for eight, with all of them coming off his sinker and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg is coming off back-to-back dominant outings, tossing 15 innings while allowing two runs and racking up 20 strikeouts. He has not faced the Cardinals since the 2016 season.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson picked up victories in his last two starts, and his 5 2/3 innings his last time out marked the longest outing of his career. Exclusively a reliever last season, another solid start should see him surpass his total of 27 1/3 innings from 2018, his big league debut.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff tossed an absolute gem on Friday, allowing just two hits over seven scoreless innings against the Marlins. He hasn't allowed a run in 11 innings at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson’s third game against the Phillies, including one start and one appearance in relief. In eight innings, he has given up two runs on six hits with six strikeouts and four walks, and earned a victory on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta had allowed one run through five innings Saturday against the Marlins. He allowed four runs without recording an out in the sixth, raising his ERA nearly a full run. He had been pitching solidly until that moment.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin gave up six runs in five innings in his last start against the Cardinals, the most runs he had given up in a single start in more than a year. He will attempt to turn the page from that outing in his first matchup vs. the Phillies this season.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin pitched the team's first complete game since September 2017, when he dazzled against the Marlins on Sunday. It was the team's first nine-inning complete game since September 2016, and Eflin's first complete game since July 2016.
away_pitcher_note: When Sanchez faces the Phillies on Sunday, it will be for the 3rd time in his first seven starts of 2019. He has completed six innings just once this season and his strikeout-to-walk ratio (1.50) would be the worst in any full season of his career.

home_pitcher_note: So steady last season, it wasn’t until Chacin worked six scoreless innings against the Rockies earlier on this homestand that he delivered a scoreless start. The Brewers hope it was something to build on for their Opening Day starter.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals have lost six of Scherzer’s seven starts on the season, though their ace leads the Majors with 62 strikeouts compared to just seven walks. He did not face the Brewers in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: Houser was Triple-A San Antonio’s Opening Day starter and made his first Major League start last month in St. Louis, but he’s effectively an “opener” here, pitching as deep into the game as he can before Freddy Peralta likely follows.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg has started to find a groove in his last three starts, pitching to a 1.25 ERA with 29 strikeouts in just 21 2/3 innings. Opposing batters are hitting .162 during that span.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff is improving after a slow start, coming off back-to-back outings against the Mets in which he allowed one run on six hits in five innings in each start. "Of all our young guys, I think he has as high a ceiling as anybody," Ryan Braun said.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson is 3-1 with a 4.26 ERA in seven career starts against the Brewers. He is 2-1 in four starts at Miller Park. He held Philadelphia to two runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Sharp against the Pirates in his 2019 debut, Hill was taken deep twice by former teammate Manny Machado last time out, leading to his exit after only four-plus innings. He allowed three runs in the loss to the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin opens the four-game series at Los Angeles. As a member of the D-backs last season, he was 1-0 with an 0.77 ERA with 31 strikeouts in 23 1/3 innings in four starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: In contrast to strike-throwing teammate Hyun-Jin Ryu, Maeda has been nibbling around the strike zone and it’s gotten him in trouble. In four of his starts, he has issued more than two walks, including his no-decision vs. the Padres last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has lost four consecutive starts, allowing 14 runs in 20 innings, but just one home run. He has walked at least four batters in four of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Other than being vulnerable the third time through the order, Buehler is giving his club a chance to win each start, despite a 4.95 ERA. Opponents are batting .196 the first two times through the order, but .409 the third time.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer struck out 10, allowing one earned run in six innings against Milwaukee on Monday, but did not receive a decision. The Nationals are 1-7 in his eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu’s last start was a 93-pitch, four-hit shutout of the Braves. It was another walkless start for Ryu, who has 45 strikeouts and only two walks. The Dodgers and Nats have split two previous matchups between Ryu and Stephen Strasburg.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg allowed just three hits over six scoreless innings before the Brewers got to him for four runs in the seventh Monday. He tied his season high with 11 strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson’s first start of the year against the Mets, whom he faced twice last season and went 1-0 with a 2.53 ERA. He has been up and down to start the year, and his last outing he gave up six runs (three earned) in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Syndergaard is looking to get his season on track after a difficult first six weeks. He struggled in his last outing in San Diego, giving up four earned runs on nine hits, including a pair of homers. In two starts against the rival Nationals this season, he has allowed six runs over 12 innings and struck out 13.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has already faced the Mets twice this season, his first two starts of the year. In 12 innings vs. New York, Corbin has given up five runs on 13 hits with 13 strikeouts and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Trade acquisition Wilmer Font impressed the Mets enough in his debut that he earned a second start, subbing for injured teammate Steven Matz. Font threw 60 pitches over four innings last time out in San Diego, and could stretch out to 75 in this one.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is off to a disappointing start in his first season in Washington, and he will try to avoid becoming just the second pitcher in Nats history to start the year 0-7 (Jason Marquis 2010).
away_pitcher_note: In his past six starts, Wheeler has gone 3-1 with a 2.93 ERA and 49 strikeouts in 40 innings. He has failed to deliver a quality start only three times this season, but two of those came against the Nationals, who tagged him for 11 runs in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: These two starters engaged in a pitchers' duel last August at Wrigley Field with Scherzer (seven shutout innings with 11 strikeouts) besting Hamels (seven innings of one-run ball with nine strikeouts), although the Cubs eventually won the game.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has gone 2-0 with a 2.33 ERA in his last six turns for the Cubs, striking out 40 and walking 14 in 38 2/3 innings in that stretch. The lefty is 16-9 with a 2.67 ERA in 37 career starts against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: After an up-and-down start to the season on the mound, Strasburg has settled into a groove in his last five starts. In 34 1/3 innings, Strasburg has posted a 2.36 ERA with 47 strikeouts and nine walks.
away_pitcher_note: Since coming off the injured list, Lester has spun a 0.36 ERA with 25 strikeouts against just two walks in 24 2/3 innings. He is 2-2 with a 4.25 ERA in seven career outings against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: A first-inning grand slam did in Hellickson in his last outing, but it was the third time this season he has surrendered at least five runs (he did so only once all of 2018). In his last five starts, his ERA is 8.06 and he's surrendering a .976 OPS.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks has a 1.95 ERA with 31 strikeouts and four walks in 37 innings over his last five starts. The righty has given up zero earned runs in three of those turns. He allowed three hits and notched three hits in a win over the Reds on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Font draws a third start for the Mets, and his first at Citi Field, in Monday's series opener. It will be his second straight start against the Nationals, who got him for five runs in 2 1/3 innings in Washington last Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Corbin’s second straight start against the Mets and his fourth appearance against New York in 10 starts this season. He is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA with 24 strikeouts and four walks against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler faces the Nats for the second straight start and fourth time already this season (9.77 ERA). Last Thursday, Washington jumped on Wheeler with four runs in the first before he managed to get through six innings and allowed just two more runs.
away_pitcher_note: Fedde will make his first start of the season, joining the Nationals' rotation in place of the injured Anibal Sanchez. Four of Fedde's five outings from the bullpen have been scoreless, and he will aim to continue that success.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom allowed seven runs (six earned) last Friday vs. the Marlins, the most runs he has given up in a start since September 2017. The reigning NL Cy Young Award winner has been frustrated with his inconsistency, particularly his pitch location.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals have lost eight of Scherzer’s 10 starts this season, including a 2-0 setback in his matchup with Jacob deGrom on Opening Day. Scherzer struck out 12 in 7 2/3 innings but was bested by deGrom's six scoreless with 10 K's.

home_pitcher_note: Matz's pitch count was up in his return from the IL, which forced him out after 3 2/3 innings last Saturday in Miami. Most encouraging was he didn't feel discomfort while throwing his curve, a pitch that possibly irritates the nerve in his forearm.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg has been locked in since April 16, striking out 62 batters while issuing nine walks and holding hitters to a .189 batting average. He is 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in a pair of starts against New York this year.

home_pitcher_note: McGowin gets a spot start in place of the injured Jeremy Hellickson. McGowin has pitched in six big league games in his brief MLB career, including one start, and has given up eight runs (seven earned) in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez has been more on the attack with his two-seam fastball (or sinker), and is getting more ground balls -- 53 percent rate, up from 50 percent last year. He's averaging 9.19 K/9 and 2.44 BB/9, both improved from 2018 (7.06 K/9, 2.76 BB/9).

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has not faced the Marlins since September 2017, when he tossed 6 2/3 innings of two-run ball against a lineup that featured names like Giancarlo Stanton, Christian Yelich, Marcell Ozuna and J.T. Realmuto.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off his first career shutout, Alcantara looks to build off his finest outing, when he blanked the Mets on 89 pitches. Now, he goes on the road, where he has a 4.58 ERA. Alcantara used 51 sinkers vs. the Mets, and he has a 46.3 percent ground ball rate.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde will make his second consecutive start in place of the injured Anibal Sanchez. The righty tossed five innings of one-run ball in a no-decision against the Mets on May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Smith comes off an "off outing" by his standards, a start in which he struck out seven while allowing two runs and three hits in five innings vs. the Tigers. The performance snapped a string of five straight starts with at least eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals are 2-9 in Scherzer’s starts this season, unable to capitalize with their best pitcher on the mound despite his dominance. He leads the National League with 96 strikeouts and a 2.32 FIP.
away_pitcher_note: Urena has impressed in May, with a 3.24 ERA in the month. He's not striking out many -- just 14 in 25 innings in the month -- but he's logging innings. He's gone at least six innings in seven straight starts. He beat the Nationals on April 20 in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Fried will be working with an extra day of rest as he attempts to win a fourth straight start. He has surrendered six hits over 12 innings since allowing a season-high nine hits over just five innings of a May 9 win in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Strasburg threw seven innings and allowed five hits, two walks and three runs (two earned) in a no-decision against the Mets. The righty has been inconsistent against Atlanta in his career, with an 11-11 record and 4.07 ERA in 30 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman hasn't allowed a homer while working six innings and allowing three earned runs or less in each of his past three starts. The veteran hurler has essentially ditched his slider. He's relied almost exclusively on his four-seamer and splitter.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez returns from the injured list to make his first start since May 16 after being sidelined for the past two weeks with a strained left hamstring. Prior to the injury, he had struggled to a 5.10 ERA while averaging fewer than five innings per start.

home_pitcher_note: In an 8-6 loss to the Cubs Saturday, Mahle gave up six earned runs and nine hits over five innings with one walk, five strikeouts and three home runs allowed. Each of the homers came on fastballs that were left up and over the heart of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off a complete game shutout in his last outing against the Marlins, Corbin will take the mound at Great American Ballpark on Friday, the site of another of his five career complete games, which came back in 2013. Corbin is 2-0 with a 3.44 ERA in three starts in Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Roark will face his former club for the first time since being traded to Cincinnati in the offseason. He pitched five scoreless innings with six hits, one walk and nine strikeouts for a 10-2 win over the Cubs Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: After back-to-back solid outings, the Nats are hopeful that Fedde is putting together a breakout year on the mound. In seven games (two starts) this year, he owns a 2.18 ERA and 1.11 WHIP, although he has only 12 strikeouts and eight walks.

home_pitcher_note: Gray allowed one earned run and five hits over six innings with two walks and seven strikeouts for an 8-1 win over the Pirates Monday. He seems to have found a groove by going 2-0 with a 2.12 ERA in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals' inability to win with Scherzer on the mound has been startling, as they have gone 2-10 with their ace on the bump despite his 3.26 ERA, MLB-best 2.30 FIP and NL-high 102 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg who has won his past two decisions, fanned 11 over seven innings in a dominant performance against the Braves last time out. He will be facing the White Sox for just the second time in his career. He hasn't faced them since June 18, 2010, when he fanned 10 and walked none over seven innings of a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez won just one of his six starts during the month of May, finishing the month with a 6.35 ERA over 34 innings. The right-hander, who was acquired via trade from the Nationals, makes his first career start against his old team.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is hoping to build off his last start on Wednesday when he allowed one hit over six innings in a 14-4 win at Atlanta. He struck out seven and walked only one to earn his first victory of the season after six straight losing decisions. He is 3-6 with a 4.60 ERA in 15 career appearances against the White Sox including 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The White Sox skipped Manny Banuelos (who pitched Thursday) and kept Covey on turn after he pitched Friday. Covey was 0-10 with a 5.96 ERA in his last 14 starts dating back into 2018 before notching a win against the Indians on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Lucchesi has lowered his ERA by more than one run over his last four starts. In that span, he's struck out 26 hitters and walked only three. Lucchesi has pitched into the seventh inning in three straight outings for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin got well acquainted with the Padres when they were his division rivals in the NL West. In 19 games (14 starts) against San Diego, he is 6-7 with a 4.24 ERA although he has had better success at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty got off to an excellent start, but he's been poor since early May. Margevicius owns a 9.17 ERA in his last four outings, and he's pitching for his job, as the six-man staff is expected to go back to five next week.
away_pitcher_note: Fedde made his 2019 season debut against the Padres when he threw four shutout innings in relief on April 28 at Nationals Park. He is aiming to bounce back from a short start last time out in Cincy, when he gave up two runs in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lauer fell into a mid-May rut, but he appears to have fully snapped out of it. In each of his last four starts, he's allowed just one earned run. Lauer threw six innings of two-hit ball against the Phillies on Monday -- his 24th birthday.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer enters this start with an extra day of rest coming off his best outing of the season. He struck out 15 in eight innings of one-run ball in his most recent outing against the Reds, although he needed 120 pitches to do so.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres have a scheduled bullpen day on Sunday, with Perdomo slated to get the ball first. After pitching an inning on Saturday, the hard-throwing right-hander probably won't pitch for very long on Sunday. Lefty Robbie Erlin could follow him.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark the fifth time in his career that Strasburg is slated to pitch in his hometown of San Diego, which was also his offseason home until he moved to D.C. recently. He is 3-1 with a 3.12 ERA in his previous four starts at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Despaigne was called up from Triple-A Charlotte to make his White Sox debut. He signed with the club as a Minor League free agent last month. In 19 games (five starts) last year with the Marlins and Angels, he went 2-3 with a 6.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sánchez faces the White Sox for a second straight start. On Wednesday at Washington, he allowed one run, four hits and one walk in 5 1/3 innings, while striking out seven in a no-decision. He has a 2.61 ERA in seven career outings at Guaranteed Rate Field.

home_pitcher_note: Banuelos will make his first appearance in June, having had his last start skipped with the White Sox not needing a fifth starter. The southpaw last worked on May 30 when he got the win over Cleveland by allowing three runs over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since he shut out the Marlins on May 25, Corbin has a 10.57 ERA in two short starts. He has struggled with fastball command while allowing 16 hits in 7 2/3 innings. The White Sox unfamiliarity with him could help. He logged a win in his lone start against them in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde has made four starts since joining the Nationals’ rotation last month, and has posted a 2.70 ERA with 13 strikeouts and seven walks during that span. He will face the D-backs for the first time in his young career.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke got the win on Saturday against the Blue Jays after allowing just four hits over six scoreless innings. He was given an extra day of rest prior to that outing after experiencing some neck stiffness in his previous start.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has upped his dominance to another level in his last four starts. During that span, he owns a 0.67 ERA, a .198 opponents’ batting average, no homers allowed and 39 strikeouts vs. five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Ray struck out 10 batters on Sunday against the Blue Jays, while allowing just two runs over 6 2/3 innings. He has struck out 19 and walked two in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg has found a way to keep the ball in the yard recently, giving up just two homers in his last eight outings, after giving up six homers in his first six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Clarke pitched in the rain in Philadelphia on Monday and allowed four runs on six hits, including a pair of homers, in just 3 1/3 innings. The D-backs won the game 13-8 thanks to a club record eight home runs.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts since coming off the injured list, Sanchez has looked more like the pitcher the Nats believed they signed this offseason. He owns a 1.04 ERA with 15 strikeouts and three walks over that span.
away_pitcher_note: Bradley will take the spot of the injured Jon Duplantier. This will be Bradley's first start since Oct. 1, 2016, when he struck out 11 Padres over seven innings. Bradley is not stretched out so it likely will be a two or three inning outing.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin looks to find a rhythm after allowing four runs in as many innings Sunday against the Mets. He is 4-3 with a 3.91 ERA over 12 career starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Campbell, who has been pitching in long relief, will get his first Major League start in his fifth outing. The Rule 5 Draft pick had been on a starter's schedule leading up to his most recent appearance last Sunday, when he allowed three runs during a rainy second inning before pitching two scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is looking to return to form after allowing two home runs (including a grand slam) to Vladimir Guerrero Jr. in his last start on Tuesday against the Blue Jays. Over his career, he is 13-5 with a 3.11 ERA in 24 starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers outdueled Brewers ace Corbin Burnes in his last start, pitching six scoreless innings with seven strikeouts. In his past two outings -- both caught by veteran Sandy León -- the rookie lefty hasn't given up a run in 13 frames with 15 strikeouts and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Ross threw six innings of one-run ball against the Mets in his last outing on April 24. On Tuesday, he will make his first start against the Braves since July 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Ynoa will face the Nationals for the second time this season after shutting them out over five innings on two hits on April 7. He earned his second straight  win after throwing a career-high 101 pitches while holding the Cubs scoreless over 5 1/3 innings in his last start on April 28.

home_pitcher_note: Over Fedde's past four starts, he has recorded a 2.61 ERA, an opponents' batting average of .167 and 24 strikeouts. He is looking for his first career win (0-2, 14.06 ERA) against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will make his return to the mound after exiting with a right hamstring strain in an April 13 loss against the Marlins. Fried has made adjustments and feels ready to return from the injury, after posting an 11.45 ERA through his first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lester will make his second start of the season after throwing five scoreless innings against the Marlins in his debut on Friday. Over his career, he is 7-2 with a 2.30 ERA in 11 starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly will look to pick up his first win of the season in the Braves' series finale against the Nationals. Smyly enters with an 8.05 ERA through 19 innings and an 0-2 record.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon picked up his first victory in exactly two years in his last start, striking out eight over five innings of one-run ball against the Tigers. Taillon has struck out five or more batters in four of his five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin has made two starts against the Yankees over his career, in which he has compiled a 1.35 ERA without a decision. The lefty has recorded 15 strikeouts over 13 1/3 frames vs. the Interleague opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber is coming off AL Player of the Week honors after going 2-0 with a 0.61 ERA in two starts against the Orioles and Tigers. Kluber generated a career-high 13 swings and misses on his changeup against Detroit on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is riding the momentum of pitching a one-run complete game on Sunday vs. the Marlins, just hours before the birth of his third child. He is 4-4 with a 4.34 ERA over eight career starts against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Germán lasted five innings against the Astros in his most recent start, permitting three runs -- including homers to Alex Bregman and Michael Brantley. Germán brought a 12-inning scoreless streak into that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Ross will make his first appearance against the Yankees. He is 3-2 with a 4.79 ERA over 35 2/3 innings of Interleague action for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde is 2-4 with a 5.26 ERA in eight appearances (seven starts) in his career against the Phillies. He allowed five runs in as many innings in his last start on Wednesday vs. the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies have gotten just enough from Anderson in his last two starts. They won both games. But Anderson still has not pitched more than five innings in any of his first six starts. They would love to see him pitch deeper.

home_pitcher_note: Over 11 career starts against the Phillies, Lester is 8-1 with a 1.92 ERA. The only loss occurred in his last outing against them -- May 23, 2019, with the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler threw the second shutout of his career Thursday against the Brewers. He has reached the ninth inning in two of his last three starts. He has a 1.88 ERA during that stretch, striking out 23 and walking four in 24 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Since joining the Nationals, Corbin is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts vs. the Phillies. He allowed three solo home runs in his last start on Friday against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin continues to pound the strike zone, which is a big reason for his strong start. He has walked only three batters in 45 1/3 innings in his first seven starts. And one of those walks was an intentional walk. He has struck out 42.

home_pitcher_note: Smith has bounced between the rotation and the bullpen this year, making seven appearances, four of which have been starts. Last time out against the Mets, he allowed two runs on four hits in four innings. This will be his first career appearance against the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was drafted by the D-backs in 2006, and he played for them for two seasons. Since then, he is 7-0 with a 2.55 ERA in 10 starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Frankoff will be making his first career Major League start and his first appearance for the D-backs. The right-hander has pitched in three games in the big leagues, which included posting a 16.88 ERA in two outings for the Mariners last season.
away_pitcher_note: Ross is 2-0 with a 1.17 ERA in three starts against the D-backs. He struck out seven and allowed two runs with three hits and five walks in his last outing on Sunday at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver bounced back in his last start, tossing 6 1/3 scoreless innings and striking out six in a win over the Marlins on Monday. It was a step forward after the right-hander allowed six runs in four innings in his previous outing, also against Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Fedde is making his second start of the season against Arizona. On April 17, he tied his career high of nine strikeouts over five innings of one-run ball in a 6-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: Alzolay had a quality start Tuesday, allowing three runs in six innings at Cleveland in a loss. He struck out six and walked none. The righty has featured one of MLB's elite sliders and has 19 strikeouts against two walks in his past three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester returns to Chicago, where he played from 2015-20 and helped the Cubs win the World Series in '16. He is 2-0 with a 5.68 ERA in two career starts vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Davies limited Cleveland to one run on five hits over 5 1/3 innings Wednesday, giving the righty a 1.10 ERA in three starts in May (16 1/3 innings). It has been a solid comeback from April, when he had a 9.47 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin makes his first start against the Cubs in a Nationals uniform. He is 5-2 with a 3.80 ERA in eight games (seven starts) vs. Chicago. This is Corbin's first appearance since the birth of his son on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta was solid in his return from the IL on Friday, logging a quality start in a win over Detroit. The righty faced the minimum in his first five frames before allowing two solo homers. He has a 1.59 ERA in three starts at Wrigley Field this year.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer makes his first start at Wrigley Field since Aug. 12, 2018, when he fanned 11 over seven innings. He has recorded a total of 30 strikeouts in his last three starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: Williams was pulled after two innings and 42 pitches in Detroit on Saturday. He has allowed 11 runs on 15 hits with 10 strikeouts and eight walks in 8 2/3 innings in his past three turns. In four starts at home this year, Williams is 2-0 with a 3.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ross is looking to bounce back after allowing eight runs in four innings on Saturday against the D-backs. He is 0-2 with a 3.54 ERA in six games (five starts) vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time in over a month, Strasburg will take the mound for the Nationals. He's started just two games this season, and he got tagged for seven earned runs in his last outing on April 13 before he was put on the injured list with right shoulder inflammation.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez was hit hard in his last outing, allowing five runs in two innings to the Yankees on Saturday. The right hander has completed at least five innings in just two of his seven starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Following his return to Wrigley Field on Monday, in which he gave up five earned runs in 5 1/3 innings, Lester will take the bump in the second game of a nine-game homestand for the Nationals. Lester is still looking for his first win in a Washington uniform.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann returned to the Majors in a big way last time out, providing 5 2/3 innings of essential bulk relief in the Orioles' comeback win over the Yankees on Sunday. He returns to a starting role for the first time since May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Since allowing 15 earned runs over his first two starts, Corbin has turned things around. He is 2-1 with a 3.34 ERA over 35 innings pitched in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey is 1-3 with an 8.62 ERA in his past four starts, after allowing just 14 runs in his first six (3-1, 4.06 ERA). He lasted 1 2/3 innings Tuesday, the second-shortest start of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is 5-0 with a 1.06 ERA and 55 strikeouts in five starts against the Reds while with the Nationals. He fanned eight over five innings in his last start on Wednesday against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Mahle will be looking to shake off a bad outing of two-plus innings with seven earned runs and seven hits allowed in a 19-4 loss to the Giants on Thursday. He lacked his strong slider and left too many pitches over the plate.

home_pitcher_note: In his last two starts against the Reds, Ross is 2-0 with a 1.32 ERA. He is looking to bounce back from allowing four runs in 3 2/3 innings on Thursday against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman survived a shaky second inning Friday, where he walked three straight batters and forced home a run. He stuck around to throw 99 pitches in five innings. He retired nine of his final 10 batters to qualify for the victory in a 9-4 Reds win over the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg will make his second start since returning from the IL on Friday. With Strasburg on the mound against the Reds, the Nats have won five consecutive games dating back to July 3, 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Gray is coming off a six-inning, three-run outing against the Brewers on Saturday. Despite the quality start, Gray is still winless on the season.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin earned the win in his last outing, allowing four runs on 11 hits against Baltimore. He faces the Brewers in the first game of a doubleheader after Friday's game was rained out. In four day games, Corbin is 3-1 with a 4.18 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: He has flown under the radar because of his teammates' dominance, but Peralta has been terrific during 2021 in his own right. Among MLB's qualifying starters, he has the most strikeouts per nine innings (13.8) and the fewest hits allowed per nine innings (4.3).

home_pitcher_note: In 13 career starts against Milwaukee, Lester is 5-4 with a 3.09 ERA. Lester, who is looking for his first win, allowed six runs (a season high), three walks and four strikeouts over four innings in his last start against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was in the middle of a solid outing in steamy Cincinnati last weekend when he felt some nausea while the Brewers battled during a long sixth inning. So the club opted to take him out after 65 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer took his third loss in his last outing against the Reds despite striking out nine and allowing two runs over seven innings. In each of his past four starts vs. Milwaukee, Scherzer has allowed just one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff is having a season for the ages, boasting a 1.41 ERA and 73 strikeouts in 64 innings. Woodruff last started on Monday against the Padres and earned his third win by throwing seven shutout innings and striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Morton navigated his way through a first-inning threat on his way to limiting the Red Sox potent offense to one unearned run over seven innings on Tuesday. The veteran has gained a better feel for his curveball as the season has progressed.
away_pitcher_note: Ross has not allowed more than two earned runs in five of his six road starts this season. He tossed four shutout innings against the Reds on Wednesday before rain cut his outing short.

home_pitcher_note: Fried has allowed exactly one run in each of the four starts he has made since returning from the injured list. He matched a season-high eight strikeouts when he tossed six strong innings against the Mets on May 17.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg struck out eight and allowed only one hit over six shutout innings against the Braves on April 7. He has a career 3.94 ERA in 35 starts vs. Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly will be pitching with two extra days of rest when he makes his third start of the season against the Nationals. The lefty has surrendered just one homer while allowing two earned runs over 12 innings vs. Washington this year. He has allowed at least two homers in five of his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lester will start against the Braves on short rest after pitching four innings on Saturday against the Brewers. He will take the mound after the Nationals deemed Erick Fedde was not ready to do so.

home_pitcher_note: To reshuffle their rotation for the upcoming Dodgers series, the Braves will call up Davidson to make what could be just a spot start. Davidson will be making his second start of the season. He allowed three runs over six innings against the Mets on May 18.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw allowed his fifth first-inning home run of the year against the Brewers on Saturday, which is the second most in the Majors. The most first-inning homers Corbin has allowed in his nine seasons was six in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler struck out a career-high 14 batters Saturday against the Rays. He joins Curt Schilling and Steve Carlton as the only Phillies pitchers with three consecutive games with 10-plus strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is 5-1 with a 2.63 ERA in his eight starts in Philadelphia since joining the Nationals in 2015. The Nats are 7-1 in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Howard makes his third start since replacing Chase Anderson in the rotation. He has a 3.86 ERA in his first two starts, although he has struggled with his velocity the deeper he pitches into the game. It is worth watching as he progresses.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals are undefeated in Ross' career starts vs. the Phillies. He is 2-0 with a 1.75 ERA against the NL East rival.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez had a 2.30 ERA in his first six starts after rejoining the rotation April 23, but he suffered his worst start Monday against the Reds, allowing six runs in just three innings. He hopes to get back on track this weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Voth gets the start as the Nationals go with a bullpen day in the series finale. He has added versatility to the Nats' pitching staff with the ability to throw multiple innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bumped back two days from his scheduled Sunday start to manage his already high workload, Glasnow will take the mound to start a two-game series against the Nationals. He has a 1.72 ERA with 55 strikeouts in five starts at Tropicana Field this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is making his 31st career start against the Rays, marking the most appearances against any opponent. He is 13-11 with a 4.47 ERA vs. Tampa Bay, and he last faced them in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: McClanahan is coming off an inefficient outing in which he threw 79 pitches in 3 1/3 innings in a road loss to the Yankees. There's a lot to like about the righty's peripherals, as he has 38 strikeouts and nine walks in 30 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is making his first career start against the Rays. In his last outing, he recorded four strikeouts and allowed six hits off four runs in 5 1/3 innings vs. the Braves on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer fanned nine batters and allowed just one run in 7 2/3 innings against the Phillies in his last start Friday. He will face the Giants for the first time in three years, last seeing them on June 10, 2018.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani was originally scheduled to start Thursday, but his outing was pushed back after the series opener at Nationals Park was postponed due to inclement weather. He is 2-1 with a 3.55 ERA in eight career appearances against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: After being sidelined on the COVID-19 IL, Fedde will make his first Major League start since May 16. He tossed five innings in a rehab start with the High-A Wilmington Blue Rocks as he worked toward his return.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman struck out 10 while giving up two unearned runs over seven innings against the Cubs last Saturday. Scheduled to start one of Saturday's doubleheader games, he is 5-2 with a 5.24 ERA in nine career appearances against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will make his first start since the 2019 season, when he was a member of the Indians. This season, he has a 1-0 record with a 7.56 ERA over six games (five starts) with Triple-A Rochester.
away_pitcher_note: Menez will make his first start of the season -- and fourth of his career -- in Game 2 of Saturday’s doubleheader. In four relief appearances this season, the lefty tossed eight scoreless innings, fanning 10 batters without issuing a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Ross will face the Giants for just the third time in his career. In Ross' last outing, where he tied his season high of six innings, he allowed four unearned runs to the Phillies on June 5.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto gave up four runs (three earned) on six hits over 4 1/3 innings against the Cubs in his last start. He is 7-4 with a 3.67 ERA in 12 career starts against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Lester's previous start lasted just 3 2/3 innings against the Rays on Tuesday. The southpaw had an elevated pitch count (91) and was unable to find the strike zone. He issued a season-high four walks in the no-decision outing.
away_pitcher_note: Brubaker allowed three runs in 4 2/3 innings last time out against the Dodgers. Since posting a 2.58 ERA through his first seven starts, he’s given up 15 runs across his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin is 2-2 with a 3.53 ERA over eight career starts against the Pirates. In five innings on Wednesday, he allowed three runs off three hits and four walks vs. the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was tagged with a pair of solo homers by Justin Turner, but those were the only runs he allowed on Wednesday against the Dodgers. In that start, he went six innings -- the first time he'd done so in exactly a month.

home_pitcher_note: With Max Scherzer on the IL, Paolo Espino will make his second start of the season for the Nationals. On Friday he fanned five and allowed one run in 3 1/3 innings after Scherzer's early exit.
away_pitcher_note: De Jong struggled a bit with command in Milwaukee on Friday, when he issued four walks in five innings, but he was still able to limit the Brewers to two runs. He's given the Pirates five innings in all three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde has not allowed a run in his last two starts (12 innings). He is 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in nine appearances (4 starts) against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Despite Lucchesi's recent success -- a 1.56 ERA over his last four starts -- the Mets still aren't letting him face opposing batters more than twice. Perhaps that will change after he set season highs with five innings and 72 pitches last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Ross threw eight scoreless innings with nine strikeouts in his last start on Sunday against the Giants. He earned a win vs. the Mets on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing nine runs in three innings over his first two starts of June, Peterson rebounded to deliver one of his best outings of the season, with six one-hit innings against the Cubs. He'll look to keep the momentum going in Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Lester goes for his first win of the 2021 season. Over his career, he is 7-1 with a 3.20 ERA in 10 starts against the Mets.
Corbin is riding the momentum of his best start of the season. He struck out seven and allowed one run in 8 1/3 innings on Tuesday against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Walker, who struck out a career-high 12 in his last start against the Cubs, blanked the Nationals over seven innings the first time he faced them on April 25. From that day forward, he's posted a 1.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler looks like a lock to make his first National League All-Star team, consistently pitching deep into games, racking up strikeouts and giving the Phillies a chance to win. If he keeps it up, he should be in NL Cy Young consideration.

After posting a 2.30 ERA in his first six starts, Velasquez is struggling again. He has a 7.88 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 14 and walking nine in just 16 innings, and has not pitched more than five innings since May 25.
away_pitcher_note: Fedde is riding a streak of 20 consecutive scoreless innings. He last faced the Phillies on May 11, when he struck out four and allowed three runs in five frames.
